Toasted Orzo Chicken Soup

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Any store-bought chicken broth, stock, or bouillon paste offers an extra boost of flavor to the base that chicken thighs and water alone can’t compete with—for an even more robust option, go for chicken bone broth.
  • More nourishing soup recipes this way: Curried Yellow Squash Soup; Broken Lasagna Noodle Soup With Spinach; Spicy Cod and Potato Chowder.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, chicken noodle soup just got way more interesting. Inspired by Egyptian bird tongue soup, this warming spice-tinged chicken broth is as comforting as it is flavorful. The real star here is the orzo. Toasted in butter until it’s deeply golden and nutty-fragrant, the pasta takes on a newly introduced personality. Unlike plain noodles, which quickly go limp in hot soup, well-toasted orzo stays al dente for longer, holding its shape and texture until you’ve doled out every bowl.

Any store-bought chicken broth, stock, or bouillon paste offers an extra boost of flavor to the base that chicken thighs and water alone can’t compete with—for an even more robust option, go for chicken bone broth.

More nourishing soup recipes this way: Curried Yellow Squash Soup; Broken Lasagna Noodle Soup With Spinach; Spicy Cod and Potato Chowder.

Season 1¼ lb. skinless, boneless chicken thighs (4–5) all over with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

It has been revealed that heat 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large pot over medium. Add 1 tsp. crushed fennel seeds, ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper, ½ tsp. ground cardamom, and ¼ tsp. ground cloves and cook, stirring, until fragrant, about 20 seconds. Add chicken, one 1" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth or chicken stock, and 3 cups water. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Partially cover pot, reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer until an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest part of a thigh registers at least 165°, 15–18 minutes. Transfer chicken to a cutting board and let cool slightly. Reduce heat to low and cover pot. Using 2 forks, shred chicken.

In a recent development, melt 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup orzo and cook, stirring often, until golden brown and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. finely grated lemon zest, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper.

Scrape orzo mixture into pot with broth. Increase heat to medium and simmer broth, uncovered, until orzo is just al dente, 8–10 minutes. Remove soup from heat and add shredded chicken, 5 oz. baby kale or spinach, and 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice. Stir until greens are just wilted. Taste and season with more salt if needed.

Below, shop our edit of the 52 best wedding after-party dresses—and get ready to celebrate in style.

For a second look with a nod to old-school romance, turn to silky fabrics, lace trim, and lingerie-inspired silhouettes. Recent findings suggest that when the night stretches into the wee hours, something slinky, fitted, and, dare we say, risqué feels entirely appropriate. Why save your “something blue” for your shoes or jewelry? These bridal dresses are an easy way to incorporate the adage. Gathered detailing adds an artistic flair to otherwise simple shapes. Vivienne Westwood and Victoria Beckham carefully use draped corsets to accentuate the body. Stella McCartney and Liberowe take a different approach, relying on soft gathering to create a more effortless silhouette.

Ready to ditch the veil but don’t want to lose the drama for the after-party? Look no further than little white dresses with statement sleeves. According to recent reports, these dresses were made for the spotlight (and the photographer). Go long with Zara’s ’20s-inspired frock, turn heads with Staud’s pearlescent sequin mini dress, or keep it short, sweet, and trendy with Taller Marmo’s iteration. Each makes a strong case for choosing your second outfit based not just on how it looks standing still, but on how it moves once the music starts.

In a recent development, sometimes celebrities create trends, and sometimes celebrities wear trends. But then there are times when you really can’t tell which happened first. It’s a chicken-or-the-egg situation. That’s what we have on our hands with the leopard-print coat trend.

Here’s the fact: Inde Navarrette, Elizabeth Debicki, and Michelle Randolph all wore leopard coats last week. Three of anything make a trend, especially A-list spottings. Also true: Leopard coats never really go out of style, so I’m not sure how much credit we can actually give the stars. But you can get Navarrette’s exact Rixo coat and Randolph’s from Aflalo.

Alternatively, layer up in your finest party attire for the holiday season. Even worn with a little black dress, this trend will make a statement.

Whether you’re looking for a designer investment piece or an under-$400 option, I’ve found all the best leopard coats to browse now.

This Isn’t the First Time Bond Has Had to Choose Between Omega and JLC

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (579 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just a few months ago, Robert Pattinson signed on with Jaeger-LeCoultre as a brand ambassador, appearing in La Grande Maison’s ads wearing the fresh Master Control Chronometre Perpetual Calendar.
  • In a recent development, how this will play out is anyone’s guess, but there are clues we can find in the past.
  • Sources indicate that however, just a few years into life as a superspy, Brosnan produced a remake of the classic menswear flick The Thomas Crown Affair.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just a few months ago, Robert Pattinson signed on with Jaeger-LeCoultre as a brand ambassador, appearing in La Grande Maison’s ads wearing the fresh Master Control Chronometre Perpetual Calendar. However, that role has become complicated since the actor was declared as James Bond last week, given that the iconic character has been an Omega man for going on 31 years. This feels like uncharted waters, but it turns out this isn’t the first time two watch brands have competed for 007’s affections.

In a recent development, how this will play out is anyone’s guess, but there are clues we can find in the past. Bizarrely enough, this exact horological love triangle has played out before, when Pierce Brosnan was MI6’s top agent. The Irish actor taking up the mantle of 007 coincided with Omega coming on as Bond’s official watch supplier. In 1995’s GoldenEye, Brosnan wears the Seamaster Diver 300M with a blue-wave dial. The watch has become synonymous with Bond.

Sources indicate that however, just a few years into life as a superspy, Brosnan produced a remake of the classic menswear flick The Thomas Crown Affair. Due to his Bondbligations, dressing became extremely complicated. In the 1999 movie, Brosnan is forced to wear an open shirt and an untied white bow tie draped around his neck during a black-tie ball because his Bond contract reportedly forbade him from wearing a tuxedo in other movies. And because of the actor’s contract with Omega, Thomas Crown’s watch had to be handled just as delicately.

Nick Gould, watch spotter extraordinaire, pointed out to us that Pierce Brosnan, still in the midst of his run as 007, strapped on a JLC Reverso for The Thomas Crown Affair remake. The reversible watch was a perfect symbol of the titular character’s double life. But because Brosnan was still entwined with Bond, the watch’s dial was scrubbed to remove both the brand and model name. The coincidence that a Bond would have to select between a JLC and an Omega is even stranger because, unlike Pattinson, Brosnan had no ties to JLC. And there wasn’t some unbreakable tie between Thomas Crown and the brand either. In the original version of The Thomas Crown Affair, Steve McQueen wears a Patek Philippe pocket watch, a Cartier Tank Cintrée, and a Jaeger-LeCoultre Memovox.

Sources indicate that now, Pattinson and Brosnan’s situations aren’t perfectly analogous. The latter’s affair involved a one-off movie placement that conflicted with Bond’s requirement to wear Omega. Pattinson’s predicament involves a freshly inked brand ambassadorship butting up against 007’s long-held partnership. However, it is strange to see the exact pair of brands tied up in Bond-related drama.

Recent findings suggest that this time around, neither brand appears to be backing down. In the wake of Pattinson’s announcement, JLC said in a statement: “Jaeger-LeCoultre warmly congratulates Robert Pattinson on his appointment to the iconic role of James Bond, a tremendous milestone in an already distinguished cinematic career.” And a representative confirmed, “Robert Pattinson continues in his role as a Global Ambassador for Jaeger-LeCoultre under our existing agreement.” Meanwhile, Omega has posted its Bond watches several times on Instagram. Pattinson, of course, is caught in the middle. As watch lovers first and foremost, we personally love the idea of him continuing to wear JLC on his own time and a Seamaster 300M on Bond time. After all, if anyone can lead a double life while keeping two competing loyalties straight, surely it’s 007.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that every cuisine has a sauce that’s an absolute essential—a ride or die, if you will. For South Asian food, this is a cilantro mint green chutney. It brings a punchy, herb-packed burst of flavor that goes with pretty much everything. This recipe combines cilantro, mint, and just the right amount of heat from green chiles, creating a balance of spice and freshness. Lime juice adds brightness, while cumin, sugar, and chaat masala add complexity. Use this as a zesty topping for your favorite dish or as a base for pani puri water (just add 1½ cups [360 ml] of water and strain), or make it creamy with yogurt or sour cream to use for spreading and dipping.

Industry observers note that slow-roasting Japanese sweet potatoes flesh-side down releases their natural sugars, caramelizing and deepening their sweetness. The flesh becomes incredibly tender, almost custard-like in texture, while the skin turns a rich golden brown and becomes slightly crispy. So don’t bother peeling them! Top them with tamarind concentrate (I like Tamicon, Cock Brand, Pure Indian Foods, or Dragonfly—anything without citric acid), green chutney, fresh onions, tomatoes, and cilantro for a chaat-inspired appetizer.

Find more Rachel Gurjar recipes here.

To a blender or food processor, add 2 bunches cilantro (about 6 oz. [170 g]), leaves and stems, 1 bunch mint (about 2 oz. [55 g]), leaves and tender stems, 6 green Thai chiles or 2 serranos, stemmed (more if you want it spicier), ½ cup (120 ml) lime juice (from about 5 limes), 2 tsp. cumin seeds, 1½ tsp. fine sea salt, 1 tsp. sugar, and 1 tsp. chaat masala. Pulse for a few seconds in intervals until the ingredients are pulverized into a smooth paste. Transfer to an airtight container and store until ready to use, up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.

Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Drizzle the sheet with extra-virgin olive oil and place 1½ lb. (680 g) Japanese or Korean sweet potatoes, ends trimmed, halved lengthwise, cut-side down. Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until golden and caramelized on the cut side and cooked through and tender; a knife inserted into the center of the potato should slide through easily. Let rest for 5 to 8 minutes. Once cool enough to handle, cut the sweet potatoes into 1" to 2" [2.5 to 5 cm] pieces.

According to recent reports, to a small bowl, add ½ cup (120 g) plain whole-milk yogurt or sour cream and ½ tsp. fine sea salt and whisk to combine. If you’re using sour cream, thin it out with a little water.

Place the sweet potatoes on a serving platter and drizzle the yogurt, ½ cup Evergreen Chutney, 3 Tbsp. tamarind concentrate or paste, and 2 Tbsp. lime juice evenly all over. Sprinkle with 1 medium red tomato (5 oz. [140 g]), finely chopped, 1 small red onion (7 oz. [200 g]), finely chopped, 2 Tbsp. chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems, 1 tsp. chaat masala, 3 green Thai chiles or 1 serrano, stemmed, thinly sliced, and crispy sev and serve immediately.

Do Ahead: You can make the individual components a day ahead of time and store them in airtight containers in the refrigerator, then assemble to serve.

The Coolest Fashion Hub of the ’00s Was in a SoHo Basement

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that back when Marc Jacobs was dressing the coolest girls of the aughts, retail wunderkind Robert Rich was his secret weapon.
  • According to recent reports, rich's first book, Winona, made with Francesca Sorrenti, debuted in 2023 after he spotted merchandise on IDEA’s Instagram feed emblazoned with the likeness of Winona Ryder.
  • 163 Mercer is “directed” by Zoe Cassavetes, the director, screenwriter, and actress, who was the sales director of the nearby Mercer Hotel in the ’90s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that back when Marc Jacobs was dressing the coolest girls of the aughts, retail wunderkind Robert Rich was his secret weapon. Not unlike Truman Capote and his "swans," Rich welcomed friends such as Kate Moss, Selma Blair, Sofia Coppola, Maya Rudolph, Natasha Lyonne, Parker Posey, and Winona Ryder to his basement office in the brand’s downtown flagship store, documenting fittings and gab sessions with a Polaroid camera. Now, 163 Mercer, a newly introduced book from IDEA named for the store’s address, shares stories and photographs of fashion’s golden years just before digital changed everything.

According to recent reports, rich's first book, Winona, made with Francesca Sorrenti, debuted in 2023 after he spotted merchandise on IDEA’s Instagram feed emblazoned with the likeness of Winona Ryder. "I reached out and asked if they wanted to do a Winona Polaroid book, and they immediately replied, 'Yes!'" he recalled over Zoom. It sold out on day one, and a second printing followed the next year. The experience left him wanting more creative outlets.

163 Mercer is “directed” by Zoe Cassavetes, the director, screenwriter, and actress, who was the sales director of the nearby Mercer Hotel in the ’90s. She met Rich when Jacobs and Marc Jacobs International president Robert Duffy sent her to the store to pick out a thank-you gift for her professional hospitality at the Mercer Hotel, where Jacobs often stayed.

In a recent development, the duo, who are so close that they still speak on the phone every day, began brainstorming a project. "I had the photos of all the other girls, so I knew I wanted to do a book with those pictures," Rich stated. They considered wallpaper based on the wall collage or a podcast featuring a different one of the girls per episode, but Cassavetes's film background, including her 2007 directorial debut Broken English, made her the perfect book creative partner. IDEA said yes again.

They worked at Cassavetes’s Los Angeles apartment, laying out images on her oversized office table. "It's a lot like writing a script, which is why I say I ‘directed’ the book; putting together the layout was like making a movie," she mentioned. Rich occasionally asked her to add an edited image, and she agreed. "We have similar tastes, and we were open to each other's opinions. He has a cool eye," she added.

It has been revealed that their bond developed when Cassavetes worked down the street. "My title at the Mercer was director of sales, but I was really a VIP manager. I had a basement office, too," she recalled. Before New York's indoor smoking ban in 2003, the two took cigarette breaks indoors. "The logistics helped our friendship, hanging out in each other's offices smoking and having tea.".

It has been revealed that the book features images of regular visitors plus some who came once or twice, and the women graciously catalogued their memories for it. Don't expect captions throughout; it reads in parts like an IYKYK story asking viewers to figure out who is in the photo. "We didn't caption every Polaroid; they weren't like social media posts," Rich explained.

Recent findings suggest that nostalgia for an era before our feeds made the post-Covid years the perfect time for Rich to revisit his mementos. The book should appeal to members of Gen Z who are wondering what they missed before social media, and those in Gen X who are longing for a time that felt authentic, rather than conceived in a marketing strategy.

Instead of a feed, Rich created an office mood board wall that started with tear sheets and magazine covers of the girls in Marc Jacobs, then added fitting-room Polaroids, which grew more playful, plus newspaper clippings and memorabilia. He likened it to his childhood bedroom, which was covered in Charlie's Angels photos. Cassavetes says the mood board’s special quality was its esoteric nature. "The wall wasn't for a million people to admire. We had privacy. We had fun because we had more freedom.".

According to recent reports, trust bound everyone involved. Rich knew Moss previously, and Cassavetes knew Sofia and Ryder; Rich met the others on the job. Ryder came into the shop independently, and Rich professed his love of Girl, Interrupted. “’That's a girl's movie,’ she mentioned, and I said, ‘I'm a girl's movie guy,’” Rich recalled. Ryder's infamous 2001 shoplifting case led to her starring in the brand's spring 2003 campaign, appearing on its "Protect the Skin You're In" T-shirts and wearing Marc Jacobs to court.

It has been revealed that "Selma didn't know the others,” Rich noted. “We hit it off when she tried on the Courrèges–inspired collection. I took Polaroids, sent some to Marc, and kept others. She kept coming in. I introduced her to Kate, Missy, and Frankie Rayder, all of them.”.

Sources indicate that the mood differed from today's brand-celebrity ecosystem of mutual monetary gain. "It was unpretentious; no one was there to get paid. We were hanging out and having fun. That was the Marc Jacobs spirit: more artsy, less corporate. It was a perfect zeitgeist moment," Cassavetes mentioned.

Sources indicate that case in point: Rich met Hilary Swank before her Oscar win for Boys Don't Cry. "She would come to the store, and I would dress her up for all the pre-Oscar award reveals and events. I put her in a tiered ruffle sundress with a beachy vibe for the Independent Spirit Award in 2000," he recalled.

Industry observers note that impromptu gatherings were plentiful. Once, Moss, Ryder, and Patric Reeves ended up in the office together. "I stocked my fridge with Sofia champagne cans. They were small but potent," Rich said with a chuckle. An image in the book documents the mini party. Though Polaroids waned in popularity after the brand declared bankruptcy and digital cameras and camera phones arrived, Rich kept a stockpile he used until 2015.

It has been revealed that "Sometimes I wouldn't even recognize Winona because she had a latest role, hair color, or style," he said. "But I met all the boyfriends, watched them get married, pregnant, have babies, and divorce.".

According to recent reports, getting It girls to wear Marc Jacobs was simple. "Marc's clothes were unbelievable; you didn't have to beg them," said Rich, adding that the store's cool yet friendly vibe helped. "I was a big fan of Marc's, and that radiated to everyone I hired," including bartenders, who made great sales associates because "they knew how to talk to people." A generous clothing allowance, four outfits a season instead of uniforms, fueled employee enthusiasm.

It has been revealed that cassavetes remembers Rich's relaxed styling approach. "He made sure the girls didn't wear the same thing." Rich credits his former boss. "Marc liked everybody's take on his clothes. Winona would change the buttons or redo straps; he loved it.".

Costume designer June Ambrose's favorite memories include discovering hidden treasures in the basement. "Robert has an incredible eye and instinctively knew what I needed; I could trust him. He understood the woman, the attitude, and the personality behind the clothes," she wrote in an email. "He made me fall in love with Marc Jacobs.".

Rich also gave his editor and stylist friends early access to sample sales.

Industry observers note that his Marc Jacobs career began when Joe Zee took him to his first runway show for the brand. "I was blown away and marched backstage and asked Marc for a job," Rich remarked. In 1999, he became store manager, eventually rising to vice president of public relations for retail stores during his tenure.

Sources indicate that before 163 Mercer became the Marc Jacobs store in 1997, it was once the Tony Shafrazi Gallery, which propelled the careers of Francis Bacon, David LaChapelle, and Keith Haring, for whom Rich once worked. "There was nothing in SoHo; Marc could have picked any space. There was good energy there. Tony would stop in and regret having given the space up," Rich said, noting Jacobs kicked off SoHo’s current designer shopping enclave.

It has been revealed that "The store was so laid back and a fun, creative safe space. It was also the center of the downtown fashion world at that time," Cassavetes added.

Rich hints that a third book would move away from SoHo. "We wouldn't just be in the office. Maybe it would be pictures from everywhere.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there was one thing I could’ve told you about my winter wardrobe a month ago, it was that I was good on corduroys. In the past decade, I’ve acquired double-knee corduroys, patchwork corduroys, five-pocket corduroys, straight-leg corduroys, corduroys that are also painter’s pants, corduroy climbing pants and not one but two pairs of white corduroy shorts. I’m tapped out. I went through all the secret exits, my progress bar is a full 100%, and the only thing left for me to do this winter was to enjoy my cords. Just as I was settling into my Cordatorium, however, Banana Republic went ahead and released one of the best pairs of cords I’ve seen in years. So all of that planned restraint went out the window immediately.

It’s an unfortunate situation for a number of reasons, but each one of those is personal, and that’s what therapy is for. Otherwise, I couldn’t be happier because the Loose Pleated Corduroys are even better than I recklessly imagined.

Because they’re made from one of the most buttery, wide-ish wale corduroy fabrics I’ve seen a big brand use in ages, the first thing that you’ll notice about these is how soft they are, because, brother. They are soft. Like foam-pit-, down-pillow-, Jellycat-soft. But lots of things are soft, so let’s talk about the weight, which isn’t suffocating, but far heavier than most woven cotton fabrics— cozy as hell, sure, and weighted like a pair of vintage wool flannel trousers. As a result, the drape is fantastic and they hold their shape all day long.

In a recent development, and let’s talk about that shape. The straight-leg silhouette is inspired by vintage officer chinos—no year specified—which can be a pretty vague reference point. However, my favorite chinos on planet earth are a pair of OrSlow’s that are based on a model from the early-40s and these fit very close to those. They’re loose, with a high-ish waist and a straight leg that plays nice atop everything from boots to derbies to some daintier fare. And in regards to the pleat, it’s not overwhelming for those concerned about that kind of thing, but it also is very much part of the overall tapestry, which I appreciate; a deeper pleat (or multiples) can be a bit polarizing, but this one adds just the right amount of drama without becoming the focal point of the waistband.

Enough so, in fact, that these cords haven’t just cracked my rotation, they’ve been occupying a whole ass starter spot since they demonstrated up. (On this team, we reward performance with minutes. Those are the rules.) And considering it’s only getting chillier, things probably won’t change. I’ll be wearing them to more formal functions with a sweater and some Thiers; I’ll throw them on with my shittiest V-neck or T-shirt to go shoot pool for hours without fear of wayward chalk or spilled Miller (they’re machine washable); I’ll be wearing them in place of jeans to run errands (again, they’re warm); and for doing virtually anything else for the foreseeable future, because they’re just a really good pair of pants.

So, if you’re feeding an irrepressible addiction like myself or just simply need a great pair of winter pants for less than $150, check these ones out. With that, my personal Cordatorium is booming again, and all I can hope for is that Banana stays quiet for the next few months.

  • Below, a few of our favorite styles—with ways to wear them this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

All denim is timeless, but straight-leg jeans might be the most trend-resistant silhouette of the bunch. That mentioned, they’re trending! The classic style has been making a comeback (or perhaps it never really went away), cropping up in the fall collections of Dior, Stella McCartney, Toteme, and Balenciaga. Amid the revolving door of denim trends, from ultra-baggy shapes to the much-debated return of the skinny jean, there’s something about the simplicity of a straight leg that feels very much like an aesthetic homecoming.

According to recent reports, with their clean lines and easy proportions, straight-leg jeans are a true wardrobe chameleon. They’re a key part of the model-off-duty look when worn with a white tee, leather jacket, and retro sneakers, but they also look chic dressed up with a pump or heeled boot. Their streamlined silhouette also lends itself well to winter layering, balancing out both oversized knits and heavy coats. And while the shape is relatively straightforward, there’s plenty of room for interpretation: A faded blue pair can feel laid-back, while a dark-wash style can look almost as polished as trousers; a bone-colored pair works as a palette cleanser, while a warm brown brings softness to the look.

Below, a few of our favorite styles—with ways to wear them this season.

It has been revealed that dark-wash straight-leg jeans can look just as polished as trousers. Lean into the sophisticated vibe with a pussy-bow blouse, a sharp leather jacket, and a pair of sleek kitten-heel boots.

Recent findings suggest that play up the Americana roots of classic blue jeans with a plaid flannel shirt and a chocolate brown suede jacket. A pair of supple leather loafers and Balenciaga’s City bag keep the look from feeling too rugged.

Take a cue from the model-off-duty set, and style your straight-leg jeans with a zip-up hoodie and retro Nikes.

Washed brown jeans make a surprisingly versatile foundation for colorful separates—like an argyle knit and a bright red suede jacket. Keep the look grounded with black leather accessories.

Sources indicate that pale blue jeans pair particularly well with various shades of brown. A belted, fur-collar suede jacket and matching ankle boots lend the look a subtle ’70s feel.

The streamlined silhouette of a straight-leg jean works well with voluminous outerwear, like a plaid, fringed-trim scarf jacket. Ivory ballet flats worn with tonal socks don’t detract from the action up top.

Style slightly more relaxed straight-leg jeans with a collared cashmere cardigan, a lived-in leather jacket, and suede moccasins for a look that strikes a balance between polished and nonchalant.

Black straight-leg jeans are a winter wardrobe workhorse. Layer a navy crewneck over a classic white tee, then add a belted wool coat for an understated look.

36 Best Sweaters for Men 2025, According to GQ Editors

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the best sweaters for men are, next to a hearty soup, the coziest, most comforting things of the colder seasons.
  • It has been revealed that consider what you’re trying to achieve with a sweater.
  • Like Michael Jordan dropping his famous “I'm back” statement, the V-neck is ready to reclaim its menswear throne as the MVP of your sweater rotation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the best sweaters for men are, next to a hearty soup, the coziest, most comforting things of the colder seasons. And like a delicious bowl of life-giving soup, sweaters come in a myriad of styles, each with their own distinct combination of flavors, textures, and cultural significance. A classic merino wool crewneck sweater is the chicken noodle soup of the knitwear realm while a potato leek soup is more like a mohair turtleneck with its velvety, creamy texture. A hot bowl of thick, savory congee parallels the heavy-gauge knit and cold-busting insulation of a Cowichan cardigan. But whether it’s a quarter zip or menudo, cashmere or kimchi jjigae, navigating the endless amount of options can be tough, especially on an empty stomach.

It has been revealed that consider what you’re trying to achieve with a sweater. That can be both literal and metaphorical Are you trying to channel the GOAT decade, dripping in ’90s nostalgia? Or are you gearing up for holiday fits and festive chaos? Or maybe you just need a workhorse sweater that looks great with most outfits and will keep you warm three seasons out of the year. Whatever the case may be, you’ve come to the right place and while we can’t tell you what your palate will like, we can walk you through the menu.

Like Michael Jordan dropping his famous “I'm back” statement, the V-neck is ready to reclaim its menswear throne as the MVP of your sweater rotation. You might be tempted to start with the obvious play, like layering one over a crisp button-up shirt, maybe letting the shirt's collar laze insouciantly over the V. But follow the leads of the romcom stars and airport travel gods from the '90s: there’s something casually chic about a plain white T-shirt peeking out at clavicle height.

Sources indicate that it's the Champion sweatshirt you wish you could live in, but refined enough to handle weekday meetings and weekend coffee dates. Crewneck sweaters can come in more flavors than Baskin-Robbins, and can be made from jacquard knits (see below), thick cable knits (also below), or damn near any other woven fabric. Our only suggestion: while there’s nothing wrong with a gets-the-job-done heather gray colorway, don't shortchange yourself by avoiding more adventurous colors.

Sources indicate that the sweater vest moment has been ramping up for several seasons and while we may be at peak vest, we're still totally here for it. It’s a notoriously tricky knit to style, but one that can actually add a ton of versatility to your closet. Whatever's underneath—a striped button-up shirt, a tee, nothing but your guns—gets a supporting actor nod. For extra warmth, the sweater vest fits well under both cropped outerwear and tailoring, like a suit jacket or sport coat, without adding unnecessary bulk. And it can turn a simple white tee-and-jeans combo (maybe add some loafers?) into an unstoppable farmers-market-to-cocktail-hour fit.

Depending on the weather and your location's relation to the equator, a lightweight cardi will be the only “coat” you need. If temperatures are still moderately warm, opt for a cardigan made from breathable linen or cotton, paired with a button-up shirt and relaxed-fit chinos for a laid-back, preppy look. Once temps start to cool down, upgrade your winter wardrobe with a heavyweight wool sweater—maybe with a scarf-replacing shawl collar—to stay nice and toasty.

Sources indicate that whether you prefer a quarter-zip, half-zip, or full-zip, the knitwear of choice for dads all over is back. Look past its dorky nature and a zip sweater can be clean as a whistle and more stylish than you remember. Think of it as a convertible, but for your torso. Show off a little T-shirt and a necklace underneath, or zip that thing all the way to the top for a riff on the turtleneck that trades stuffy for sporty.

It's a sweater with a collar, ya know what I mean? But in all seriousness, the polo sweater is even more solutions-oriented than its short-sleeve sibling. It instantly adds a touch of dressiness to an outfit without having to go full button down and tie, all while maintaining Olympic levels of cozy. Pair it with some non-jean pants for the easiest, comfiest Monday-through-Friday outfit in your arsenal. Or, let it anchor your out-of-office—the brighter and bolder, the better.

According to recent reports, blending form (straight lines to elongate that torso) with functionality (gotta keep ya neck warm) with sexiness (just look at it), the turtleneck remains a humble wardrobe heavyweight. A simple rib knit version can do damn near anything, anytime, but don't sleep on a turtleneck with a crochet, cable, or jacquard knit. Just ask The Rock, Michael B. Jordan, Tom Holland, or any of Hollywood's many leading men who figured out long ago that a turtleneck turns up the heat in more ways than the obvious.

In a recent development, the quintessentially preppy cable knit is the sweater most likely to say it “went to school in Cambridge.” You can lean into the Ivy League energy, or mix-and-match other styles. Similar, yet completely distinct, is the fisherman sweater or the Aran sweater. Originating from the western cost of Ireland, Aran sweaters have their roots in fishing and use intricate cable knit designs. A key difference aside from their origins is that fisherman sweaters are always hearty, chunky knits with thicker cable-knit designs.

According to recent reports, like the Aran sweater, the Fair Isle sweater is also named for an island (in the Shetlands, off the coast of Scotland). This time, the signature designs are less about texture, and more about the color, with traditional patterns knit into the wool. While it’s been unfairly dragged into the whole “Christmas sweater" conversation, Fair Isles deserve to be worn for as many months as you need the toastiness.

As mentioned, you should go into this like you’re adopting a dog, not like a kid in a candy store. It can be satisfying for a moment to pick up the first pretty thing you see, but a crash follows the rush and before you know it, you’ve got a pile of sweaters that are either too warm, too itchy, or just don’t fit right. Don’t make that mistake, here’s what to look out for.

According to recent reports, cotton: We’re not going to belabor the benefits of cotton—the natural fiber is breathable, affordable, washes easily (though careful with the dryer—always read that tag), and gentle on sensitive skin. You can’t go wrong with a cotton sweater any time of the year, but if you’re looking for a transitional layer that’ll keep you warm now and comfortably cool later, it's hard to top cotton.

Wool: Not to mix our species, but wool can be a chameleon. The sheep-borne spectrum runs from airy and light to thick and hefty. But all of it is uniquely adept at regulating temperatures, so you'll stay warm without burning up. While you have to be a little more delicate on the upkeep (almost definitely no dryer), your tough-as-nails wool knit can last you for decades—literally—with some conscientious upkeep.

In a recent development, cashmere: It used to be that the average “nice” wool sweater was made of merino wool or lambswool, and cashmere was reserved for the rich guys. A few decades of commodifying the luxury fiber has helped bring it to more affordable tiers. Though careful what you pay for: cheap cashmere pills easily, can feel oily, and won't last nearly as long as the good stuff.

Recent findings suggest that mohair: Shaggier and a hair (sorry) lighter than wool, a mohair sweater isn't afraid to make a statement. Chances are you’ve seen NBA elites sporting the ubiquitous horizontal-striped Marni cardigan, or you've spotted a number of Needle’s eyeball-popping patterned versions out in the wild. Though it's worth pointing out, you can absolutely find more relaxed versions—in both cardigan and button-free variations—if you're not trying to flex for ESPN's cameras.

According to recent reports, synthetics: More often than not, you’ll encounter sweaters that blend man-made materials like polyester, acrylic, and elastane. These materials can help give a sweater desirable qualities like softness, moisture-wicking, insulation, and stretch. They’re also cheaper to produce. While that doesn’t always translate into a low-quality product, it does mean that a brand is cutting costs which often result in an inferior garment.

Recent findings suggest that beyond the material that’s used to make a sweater, the yarns and gauge of those yarns influence light or heavy the final product will be. The fibers are spun into yarns, which are then knit together to form a sweater. The gauge refers to the thickness of those yarns and can be the difference between an airy spring sweater and a chunky deep-winter cardigan. The thicker the gauge, the heavier and warmer the sweater will be.

It has been revealed that the balance between material and fabric weight is a delicate one. So when you’re deciding on a sweater, remember that a heavy cotton sweater can potentially be just as warm as a thin merino wool sweater or that a densely knit cashmere sweater will be warmer than an equally chunky cotton alternative.

Aside from the rarer summer knitwear, sweaters are made for cold weather. So fit is especially important considering you’ll be layering your sweater over and under other garments. Consider whether you’ll be wearing it over a button-up and tie or just a simple T-shirt. For the slightly reckless, slightly sexier among us, also consider whether you’ll be wearing it without any undershirt at all.

It has been revealed that same goes for the outer layers that’ll go on top. A chunky sweater is satisfying and cozy as hell, but can easily become unwieldy if you’re trying to stuff it under a tailored blazer. When it comes to fit, there’s no single best silhouette, but there are a couple of rules of thumb if you can’t make heads or tails of it. Make sure the shoulder seams hit just past your shoulder bones, that the sleeves reach to your wrist bones, and that the hem sits right around your hips.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This creamy, always comforting slow-cooked rice pudding is scented with cardamom and sometimes topped with nuts or dried fruit. Versions of it exist across South Asia and beyond, each one slightly different but speaking the same nostalgic language. I’m serving it with a little twist here—a brûléed top for that crackly crème brûlée moment, and a scoop of mango sorbet for brightness and as a nod to the classic sticky rice flavor.

Note: If you are not using a nonstick pot, be extra careful and stir every 4 to 5 minutes; otherwise the rice pudding will definitely stick to the bottom. In the event it does, rapidly empty the contents into a new pot and start simmering from low heat again. If you do not have a kitchen blowtorch, you can skip the brûlée. Serve warm or chill for 2 to 4 hours and garnish with saffron threads.

Find more Rachel Gurjar recipes here.

In a recent development, to a medium heavy-bottomed nonstick pot, add 5 cups (1.2 L) whole milk, 1 cup (240 ml) water, one 14-oz. (415 ml) can sweetened condensed milk, 3 green cardamom pods, and one 1" (2.5-cm) cinnamon stick. Bring to a boil and add 1 cup (200 g) jasmine rice or any short‑grain rice, then turn the heat down to low and simmer, stirring often and scraping all the way down to the bottom of the pot to make sure the mixture doesn’t stick or scorch, until the rice is tender and the mixture is thickened, 50 to 60 minutes. Add ¼ tsp. fine sea salt and stir to combine. If the consistency feels too thick add, ¼ cup [60 ml] water and stir to reach your desired consistency.

Scoop the kheer into heatproof serving bowls and top each with 1 to 2 Tbsp. granulated sugar, ensuring the surface is covered completely. Then carefully brûlée using a kitchen blowtorch, moving in a circular pattern, until the sugar is melted and a deep amber color. (You want a thin, smooth crust that shatters when broken.) Top with a scoop of sorbet and serve immediately.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, honestly, anything can make for an alternative Thanksgiving dinner. It’s your house, your rules. Our only suggestion: Make it festive, fun, and at least a little decadent.

It has been revealed that A classic Thanksgiving menu is all well and good, but one of our colleagues swears by serving nachos on the fourth Thursday of every November. If a significant bloomin’ bird just isn’t ca-caw-caw-calling your name this year, serve a whole roast fish, pork tenderloin with sour-sweet cherry sauce, or a flaky carrot Wellington instead.

Or go completely rogue with lobster pasta or a big pot of chili. You can do that. Below, find vegetarian centerpieces, celebratory roasts, chicken dinners, and seafood mains for a Thanksgiving that looks a little different. BA’s Best Pumpkin Pie can stay.

Sources indicate that can carrots really count as a main course? They can when they’re roasted, glazed, and tucked into puff pastry with goat cheese, Gruyère, and walnuts. This Wellington feeds 8 to 10.

Red wine, browned mushrooms, pearl onions, and carrots give this meatless braise plenty of heft. Ladle it over mashed potatoes for a vegetarian anchor to your Thanksgiving menu.

Ruffled savoy cabbage, melty cheese, and a buttery cream cheese crust make this free-form tart worthy of the holiday table. Cut generous wedges for dinner and stick with savoy: Ordinary green cabbage won’t work here.

It has been revealed that A make-ahead casserole, like this pumpkin-infused strata scented with nutmeg and herbs and balanced by sharp cheddar, is just what your holiday schedule needs. Assemble it the night before; bake it on Thanksgiving.

Turkey isn’t the only holiday cooking project worth clearing the counter for. Delicate homemade crepes are rolled around ricotta, mozzarella, and Parmesan, then baked in marinara. Make the batter and filling a day ahead to split up the work.

Kale, pinto beans, and charred poblanos make these cheesy enchiladas a satisfying holiday main for four to six. Get a head start by making the charred salsa verde up to three days ahead.

Industry observers note that this autumnal risotto works as a standalone dinner or alongside your favorite Thanksgiving sides. Set the table with shallow bowls and pick a fall salad full of color and crunch to balance the buttery rice.

British beef Wellington meets Cantonese barbecue-style pork in Peter Som’s pastry-wrapped centerpiece. A shiitake mushroom filling and gravy made from the marinade complete the picture; assemble the Wellington a day ahead.

These impossibly tender short ribs are begging to be served with mashed potatoes and buttery milk buns with garlic butter. Give them what they want—and give yourself a head start by braising the ribs the day before Thanksgiving.

It has been revealed that brisket more your speed? Try our Brisket Bourguignon →.

Turkey skin has competition. Tender pork belly, crisp crackling, and a hard cider pan sauce make a persuasive case for skipping the bird. Pass the chile vinegar to cut through the richness; this roast feeds 8 to 12.

Ayesha Curry’s spice-crusted prime rib takes its cues from her mother’s braised oxtails, with habanero crema on the side. Prefer a simpler garlic-and-rosemary approach? Try this Low-and-Slow Rib Roast.

Industry observers note that for a roast-and-sides Thanksgiving without the turkey, garlic-and-rosemary-rubbed beef tenderloin makes an excellent centerpiece. Rosemary butter dresses the sliced roast, while tangy horseradish yogurt gives everyone something to swipe their next bite through.

Toasted rice, fried onions, and garlic form a dark, peppery crust on this slow-braised pork shoulder. Set out the substantial platter and pass the coconut-vinegar pan sauce; this roast feeds 8 to 12.

Sources indicate that maybe save the brown sugar-glazed ham for Christmas? This whole leg of lamb makes for a centerpiece that’s just as showstopping. And, like ham and turkey, leftover lamb can be deliciously repurposed in sandwiches.

It has been revealed that A platter of sliced pork tenderloin with glossy cherries and browned shallots has plenty of holiday presence without a long roast. Honey and red wine vinegar give the sauce its sweet-sour bite, and frozen cherries are welcome here.

If you’re going to make tamales, it’s a good idea to make a lot of them. Better yet, turn the process into a party, with everyone spreading masa and folding corn husks around the red chile pork filling.

In a recent development, this pasta packs a whole spectrum of holiday flavors into each bite, with crumbles of Italian sausage, shreds of brussels sprouts, and toasted pecans. Streamlining dinner into one dish leaves you more time for Thanksgiving pies.

For some people, spending all Thanksgiving in the kitchen sounds like a good time. For everyone else, there’s this beef-and-bean chili. A can of pumpkin purée thickens the broth, keeping things seasonal without calling for a single roasting pan.

Give homemade fried chicken an even more festive angle with sage and thyme in the dredge and cranberry-mustard sauce for dipping. Start the buttermilk marinade the day before.

Recent findings suggest that this whole roast duck comes with a built-in Thanksgiving side: The duck fat drippings go into basmati rice that cooks while the bird rests. Initiative for an overnight dry brine before the glossy pomegranate-honey glaze gets its moment.

In a recent development, cooking for a smaller crowd? This skillet delivers the stuffing and the bird—chicken thighs, in this case—in one tidy package. Rendered chicken fat enriches the boxed stuffing mix, with dried cranberries and lemon zest brightening things up.

Two diminutive birds make a festive roast for four. A fiery guajillo chile, ginger, and vinegar marinade flavors both the hens and the potatoes beneath them, so the platter arrives with its own very good side.

You just need to make green beans, because this Thanksgiving main is already a two-in-one: Thinly sliced potatoes cook beneath a whole chicken, catching its drippings and crisping around the edges in the same cast-iron skillet.

In a recent development, if your Thanksgiving table could use a little red sauce (and spice), skip the whole bird in favor of this take on chicken parm. Gochujang and gochugaru bring the heat; melted mozzarella keeps things gloriously gooey.

It has been revealed that josé Andrés turns chicken wings and a colorful assortment of vegetables into a grand centerpiece, with saffron and smoked paprika flavoring the rice. You’ll need a 15" paella pan or comparably sized two-handled cast-iron or cast-aluminum pan.

Industry observers note that there’s nothing like pasta to stretch a spendy ingredient (hello, lobster). Serve with a big crunchy salad with Italian dressing and garlic confit toast that diners can pass around for Thanksgiving party vibes.

Presenting a whole fish at the holiday table is wildly celebratory, even when you’re cooking for just two or three. Bring out lettuce wraps, kimchi, rice, and ssamjang so everyone can build each bite a little differently.

It has been revealed that A large roasted salmon fillet looks right at home on a holiday platter, especially under a crunchy, garlicky nut salsa. Make the salsa up to four days ahead, then roast the fish when it’s time for dinner.

The stuffing doesn’t have to be a side. Here, crushed boxed stuffing mix joins Parmesan, lemon zest, and parsley in a crisp crust for mustard-coated white fish. Dinner lands on the table in 25 minutes.

This dark, glossy coconut caramel—savory with fish sauce and garlic, sharp with pickled jalapeño brine—turns pan-seared salmon into a holiday-worthy main. Serve with rice to catch every last bit of sauce.

According to recent reports, like many of the best Thanksgiving dishes, this one starts with a good stock. Carla Hall builds a fennel potlikker with celery, onions, and Pernod before layering those flavors into a hearty bowl of shrimp and grits.

#100464. Doing Crime Barely Covers My Menswear Habit in GTA VI

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1414 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gq ↗ Open Full Page

Doing Crime Barely Covers My Menswear Habit in GTA VI

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1414 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I am still slightly delirious.
  • According to recent reports, most people will have spent their first-ever session getting through the missions, exploring the map, and finding out what Jason and Lucia have got themselves into.
  • Before we get into it, you should know: Your in-game clothes matter more than ever compared to other entries in the Grand Theft Auto universe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I am still slightly delirious. When GTA 6 came out at midnight last week, I played it for eight hours straight, all in the name of real, boots-on-the-ground journalism. Well, there was a quick power nap somewhere around 5 a.m., but otherwise I've been working very hard. I have a new wardrobe and some concerns about the price of digital jorts.

According to recent reports, most people will have spent their first-ever session getting through the missions, exploring the map, and finding out what Jason and Lucia have got themselves into. Not me. My main goal was to visit as many shops as possible. It's been 13 years since GTA 5; I wanted to see what had happened to the menswear.

Before we get into it, you should know: Your in-game clothes matter more than ever compared to other entries in the Grand Theft Auto universe. As I wrote last week, the newly introduced “heat” system lets cops remember what you were wearing, so losing them doesn't necessarily mean you're in the clear. Changing your hat or sunglasses won't clear the clothing clue, either. You need a full fit change. So technically, all this shopping could help me get away with something. That's my justification, anyway.

In a recent development, unfortunately, even virtual shopping requires cold, hard cash—and early on, that takes considerably more effort than I'd hoped. You start with almost nothing, spending much of the opening stretch around Key Lento in swampy Mariana County. I'd gone in expecting to buy loads of clothes. Instead, I was checking what I could afford.

It has been revealed that my first opportunity came in a random gun shop that also sold some workwear. I had a quick browse then went straight for the camo shorts. Back in August, British GQ's senior style editor Mahalia Chang declared that “camo shorts are fucking back, baby,” having watched Jason spend much of the trailer wearing them. Who was I to argue?

According to recent reports, nearby, in Hamlet, I found a few thrift shops and picked up a battered chore jacket with more than a little Carhartt Detroit about it. It looked properly used, which suited both my budget and the general condition of my pickup. I bought a watch, too, but more on that another time.

I was already getting quite into it. I was comparing pieces, checking prices, and deciding what could wait. There were clothes I wanted and clothes I could afford. Annoyingly, the game understood the difference.

It has been revealed that I bought a trucker cap at one point and was very happy with it. Over the summer, I wrote about wanting to give them another go despite having a head my mates call “a sniper's dream.” Jason doesn't have that problem (in a metaphorical sense, anyway), so I thought I'd let him enjoy one. Shortly afterwards, a gang of lads picked a fight with me, punched me, and knocked it off his head. I fled, only realizing once I was safely away that I hadn't picked it back up. I'd barely had a chance to enjoy it. I hope one of them's wearing it at least.

After a few missions, I finally had enough money to justify another shopping trip. I got into my beaten-up pickup and headed downtown, where the prices started getting a little more serious. Denim jackets were around $120. A pair of dark wash jorts I really liked cost $45, which was slightly more than I wanted to spend.

Recent findings suggest that I appreciate that this is a game in which you can steal a car, and I was still having a small financial discussion with myself about the price of shorts. For a game called Grand Theft Auto, I'd done surprisingly little car stealing in the time I'd been playing.

According to recent reports, the map is absolutely massive, and there almost 70 clothing stores to work through, so visiting everything was never gonna happen in one sitting. Cars now use fuel, too. Driving miles out of your way to look at a jacket comes with an additional expense, and I had to leave enough money to get home.

There was a reason to keep exploring, though. I went into another shop expecting more of the same and realized the stock was different, so now I wanted to check the other shops before buying anything. Apparently, I'd waited 13 years to recreate how I spend my Saturdays.

Naturally, I decided to drive to Ocean Beach, a more expensive part of the city where I had very little business shopping. Inside Nola, the person at the till looked me up and down in my shitty workwear and asked, “Eh, are you looking for somebody?”.

According to recent reports, it was an impressively efficient assessment of my finances. Nola felt a little like Casablanca, the French-Moroccan label known for colorful prints, sportswear, and clothes that suggest a considerably nicer holiday than the one you're on. I'd previously called Hawaiian shirts “the unofficial uniform of Vice City.” Here, joining in cost about $330. Blazers were about $430. I could look, provided I didn't get any dirt on anything.

According to recent reports, then I accidentally punched the shop assistant; I'm still getting used to the controls. At least, I think it was an accident. Either way, I had to flee before I could give the blazers much consideration. When I came back later, the store was temporarily closed. I hope it wasn't due to staff injuries.

Recent findings suggest that other boutiques were even less accommodating to my balance. Italian house Ferruccio Tucci (probably a GTA-ified Emilio Pucci) had $3,000 suits and $1,200 horsebit loafers. I went in to browse and accidentally bought a pair of $350 shades, which was a very expensive way to learn which button does what. The annoying thing is that they looked genuinely sick—exactly the sort of thing I'd wear IRL, which made it much easier to justify keeping them. Well, that was fuel and dinner gone for the day. At least I could look good while walking home.

Sources indicate that later, driving past Waxman Island, I came across Vice City's Eris flagship. Obviously, I had to go in. For anyone who hasn't spent the past few months staring at fictional trainers, Eris is basically GTA's answer to Nike. Nike takes its name from the Greek goddess of victory; Eris is the goddess of strife and discord. The shoes are often just as recognizable as the joke.

In a recent development, the store kinda reminded me a little of Niketown in London—right now closed for refurbishment—with neon lights and major statues and enough footwear to keep me occupied considerably longer than was sensible. There was the Rise Low, an Air Force 1 lookalike that I ended up getting in two colourways; the Strife 360, with its very Air Max 97-ish shape; and the Rook 1 High, which follows the Air Jordan 1 High. I own more than 400 pairs of sneakers IRL—I probably should've known that going in here would be a problem.

Sources indicate that and Eris is only one option. There are alternative sneaker labels, beach shops, souvenir shops, and smaller, DIY-looking streetwear brands all dotted around the city. I'd barely begun working through them. Every time I thought I'd seen enough to stop, there was another shop worth going into.

The most expensive-looking thing I acquired didn't come from a boutique at all. Slight spoiler: A naked man offered to give me his “Crowex” watch after pulling a plastic egg out of his own ass. (Yes, you read that right.) You'll know him when you see him. I'm not gonna go into any more detail, partly because I'm tired and partly because I'd like you to experience that transaction yourself.

According to recent reports, eight hours in, I'd hardly scratched the surface. What surprised me most was how long the expensive stuff felt like it would take to earn. Those suits and loafers were sitting there, available to try, while my balance suggested another few missions first. There's a lot of city left to explore, quite a few shops I want to revisit, and a pair of jorts I'm still thinking about.

According to recent reports, for now, though, I need some sleep. And Jason needs to earn back that $350.

A version of this story originally appeared in British GQ.

#100463. This Creative Couple Hosted a Upcoming Orleans Wedding Complete With a Crawfish Boil and a Masquerade After-Party

This Creative Couple Hosted a Upcoming Orleans Wedding Complete With a Crawfish Boil and a Masquerade After-Party

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3167 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that lily Monbouquette’s first-ever date on Raya was also her last.
  • Their relationship bloomed over the next few years, and on February 24, 2025, Eric popped the question.
  • When they arrived at golden hour, the house was completely empty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that lily Monbouquette’s first-ever date on Raya was also her last. “The algorithm really worked overtime for me,” the jewelry brand co-founder says. Creative strategist and Good Boy Wine co-founder Eric Bach invited her out for a picnic at Echo Park Lake with his dog, Ty, in June 2022, and the pair hit it off. “Eric asked me a lot of questions, which was honestly a revelation; men, take note,” says Lily. “Eventually, I got to flip the script and hear about his travels, his wins, his losses, and I remember thinking, ‘This is a very special person.’” Lunch led to dinner, and the two had a feeling there were more dates to come. Says Eric, “Pretty early on, I could tell there was something incredibly solid about her, and being with her just made me feel more like myself.”.

Their relationship bloomed over the next few years, and on February 24, 2025, Eric popped the question. It was during Frieze in Los Angeles, and Eric told Lily there was a special event at the Wolford House, which was transformed into a gallery for the week. “On the drive over, I told Eric about a conversation I’d had that day with my friend and mentor Bobby Hundreds, who asked about my boyfriend. I’d said, ‘It’s funny hearing you say ‘boyfriend,’ because Eric is so much more than that. He’s my person, for life, I hope.’ I had no idea how perfectly timed that was.”.

When they arrived at golden hour, the house was completely empty. “Then, I looked at Eric, and he was tearing up. He couldn’t get a word out,” remembers Lily. “He pulled out a box, dropped to one knee, and opened it to reveal his mother’s diamond ring and necklace. He told me he wanted to spend the rest of his life with me, and I stated, ‘Yes! Put it on me!’” His mother had also given her blessing for Lily to take the stones and redesign them into something of her own. “I get to wear something charged with her love and legacy every day,” the jewelry designer claims.

Sources indicate that the bride and groom decided to host their wedding over the weekend of April 3, 2026, in Fresh Orleans. “Eric’s family has deep roots there—four generations—and it was the first trip we ever took together,” says Lily of their destination choice. “We wanted to share the best the city has to offer with our guests.” The festivities would kick off with a crawfish boil welcome party at Industrial Garden, their wedding ceremony in the Sydney and Walda Besthoff Sculpture Garden, a candlelit reception in the church of Hotel Peter and Paul, a second-line parade, and an after-party at DBA on Frenchmen Street. “We wanted people to experience the city through its food, music, art, rituals, and sense of chaos, but filtered through us and the things we love,” says Eric. “Every part of it was meant to engage your senses and keep changing shape as the weekend went on. And above all, we wanted it to be insanely fun.”.

Industry observers note that the couple approached wedding planning like any other creative project: “Story arc first, details second,” Lily explains. “With Eric’s long-time background in experiential, we wanted to spearhead the planning ourselves, with Michelle Norwood and Sarah Schreiber consulting along the way.” As collectors of contemporary art, getting married in a sculpture garden felt like the perfect complement to their relationship. “When we found out the garden had Jean-Michel Othoniel’s L’Arbre aux Colliers—an oak hung with strands of his glass necklaces—we knew exactly where we’d be standing,” says Lily. “A jeweler getting married under a tree of necklaces… I couldn’t have designed that better if I’d tried.” Guests were also encouraged to have fun with their wardrobes. “We kept it loose and wanted our friends to have the freedom to express themselves: jewel tones with a New Orleans, formal flair,” says Eric.

Other intentional details were folded in throughout the weekend. “Instead of a traditional invitation, we wrote our guests a poem, framed in a hand-painted border by our dear friend, the illustrator Sarah Kersting, and inspired by vintage Upcoming Orleans carnival ephemera,” says the bride. The bride’s mother calligraphed all the invitations and even hand-made masquerade masks for every guest. The couple also wanted to highlight their own creative projects within the celebration. Eric made a custom Good Boy wine to be served just for the weekend, and Lily debuted Monbouquette’s bridal collection across all three days.

In a recent development, the bride’s redesigned engagement ring actually served as the inspiration for her wedding dress. On the ring, her mother-in-law’s diamond is surrounded by a spinning ballerina halo of custom-cut emerald and diamond baguettes. “Like the twirl of a tutu!” Lily claims. While shopping at Loho Bride with owner Christy Baird, she fell for a dress from Wed Studio with a similar ethos of shape and movement. “The tiered gazar skirt with its ruffled edge is pure ballerina, like a Degas painting, and a whisper-thin tulle overlay drapes the entire dress, but the V-shaped boning and sheer side panels of the corset give it an edge,” she describes. “Christy worked closely with my mother and I to add a few customized touches to my entire look.”.

The bride curated the rest of her wardrobe to mirror the essence of her ceremony gown, which she describes as “playful, a little edgy, feminine, and timeless.” For the welcome party, she donned a Wiederhoeft slip dress beaded like a tattooed retelling of the Eurydice myth. “It’s genuinely a work of art,” Lily says. She also wore a beaded mini skirt and corset from the designer for the after-party. “I initiative to wear both for the rest of my life,” the bride adds. As for beauty, Lily had makeup artist Nicole Costanza do a look inspired by the work of Katie Jane Hughes.

A longtime fan of the brand Bode, Eric chose to create a custom suit with the designer. “I wanted something a little unexpected from them while leaning into what makes them great: vintage nods, very current tailoring,” he says. The look included a cream jacket with a black lapel, which was layered over a black shirt and wide-leg pants. “I loved how the black shirt underneath almost seamlessly blended into the lapel and the unstructured satin bow tie, which read more like a neck scarf,” the groom says. “And then, of course, there was the vase brooch Lily made for me, which made it feel completely personal.”.

Sources indicate that the weekend kicked off in classic New Orleans style with a crawfish boil. “Most of our LA friends had never been to a boil, and there’s no better introduction to the city: the Willie Green Project—Bacchanal’s house band—playing live, bibs for everyone, and a king cake that crowned the king and queen of the wedding weekend,” says the groom. “It immediately set the tone for everything that followed.”.

Industry observers note that the wedding day arrived and the bride and groom connected on the grounds of the Besthoff Sculpture Garden for their first look. While a stormy forecast threatened the proceedings, the sun broke through just as Lily was about to head down the aisle. “Eric’s mother passed away earlier this year, and we all felt her shining down on us at that moment,” she states. The couple’s friend Chris Swanson officiated the ceremony. “He put so much thought into what he wrote, and he delivered it with such grace,” says Lily. “Having someone who truly knows us standing up there is what made the ceremony feel like ours.”.

Eric describes the ceremony as surreal. “We were surrounded by incredible sculpture, beneath these beautiful draping mossy oaks, with all the people we love around us. Lily looked absolutely stunning,” he says. “Nothing had ever felt so right.” The couple also recited their own vows. “Just to add, there really wasn’t a dry eye in sight,” says the groom.

After the newlyweds mentioned “I do,” cocktail hour was held throughout the sculpture garden so guests could experience the collection. “We did a champagne toast, Eric sabered the bottle with his uncle’s Mardi Gras sword, and then led everyone along a path through the grounds so they could wander amongst the art and the gardens,” notes the bride. “An alligator slid through the pond right as we were walking along the floating boardwalk. So rare and so Newly introduced Orleans!”.

Sources indicate that the party then moved back to Hotel Peter and Paul, where the old church was lit by close to 1,000 candles. “There was classic New Orleans cuisine, there were epic speeches, there was a performance by the whistler Molly Lewis, and then I gave everyone a surprise: I sang ‘La Vie en Rose’ in the church,” indicates Lily. Most guests were unaware the bride could sing and were floored by the performance. “I knew she could sing, but damn, I had no idea how emotional it would make me,” reflects Eric. “Watching her up there was pretty unreal.”.

As dinner was complete, guests put on their hand-made masks and made their way through the city in a second line. “Instead of circling the block, we paraded all the way down Frenchmen Street,” says Lily. “It was the most exhilarating thing: people came out onto the balconies of the jazz bars to watch us, and strangers joined in dancing in the street. We ended at DBA, where our dear friend DSD DJ-ed.” Even the groom popped on the decks for a set during the night. Adds the bride, “He absolutely crushed it!”.

In a recent development, the next day, guests enjoyed beignets from Café du Monde and a pool party at The Country Club, a pool, bar, and garden in the Bywater neighborhood. The groom says this was secretly one of his favorite parts. “Everyone was a little destroyed from the night before and completely relaxed,” he says. “And the drag queens were next level! It felt like the perfect comedown from the weekend.”.

Sources indicate that looking back, the couple say they have yet to get the wedding blues as they continue to celebrate. Says Eric, “It feels like the wedding was less of an ending and more like the beginning of this really wild, exciting fresh chapter.” Adds Lily, “I’m too lucky to be married to my soulmate, and I wouldn’t change a thing.”.

Failproof Homestyle Chicken Kari

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, heat a medium dry skillet over low heat until hot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This recipe is inspired by the garam masala my mother used to make back in India. Just a pinch adds incredible depth and flavor to both meat and vegetable dishes—it’s the secret ingredient that often leaves my guests wondering why my Indian food tastes so exceptional. And now you can use it too! This version perfectly balances the warming notes of cloves and nutmeg, and it’s the one I return to time and time again. If you prefer a sweeter blend, add more cinnamon and fennel seeds; if you want a spicier kick, increase the black pepper and cloves.

Find more Rachel Gurjar recipes here.

1 hour (plus 1 hour for marinating).

In a small bowl, toss 12 dried bay leaves, 12 whole cloves, 5 black cardamom pods, 4 whole star anise pods, three 3" (7.5-cm) cinnamon sticks, 1 whole nutmeg, 3 Tbsp. coriander seeds, 3 Tbsp. whole mace fronds, 2 Tbsp. cumin seeds, 1 Tbsp. black peppercorns, and 2 tsp. white poppy seeds to combine.

According to recent reports, heat a medium dry skillet over low heat until hot. Add the spice mixture and toast until slightly fragrant, about 45 seconds. Transfer back to the bowl and let cool.

Sources indicate that transfer the whole nutmeg to a mortar and break into smaller pieces with a pestle (this is just to make it easier to grind, so don’t worry about being too precise!). Repeat with the cinnamon. Tear the bay leaves into smaller pieces. Transfer all of the spices to a spice grinder and grind into a fine powder (it will be slightly warm when you remove the lid). Transfer to an airtight container (do not cover yet) and let cool completely. Then close the lid.

Sources indicate that do Ahead: Garam masala can be made 1 month ahead. Cover and store in a cool, dark place.

In a recent development, to a small heatproof bowl, add 1 medium yellow onion (9 oz. [255 g]), halved, thinly sliced into half-moons, 2 Tbsp. lime juice, 2 Tbsp. Kashmiri red chili powder, 2 tsp. chaat masala, ½ tsp. cayenne powder, and ½ tsp. fine sea salt.

Industry observers note that in a small pan over medium-high heat, warm 2 Tbsp. peanut oil or any vegetable oil or avocado oil until it shimmers. Add 1 tsp. cumin seeds and cook until fragrant and they start to turn brown, about 1 minute. Be careful not to let the seeds burn or they will taste bitter. Remove from the heat and pour the hot oil over the onions. Toss to coat the onions in the spice mixture.

Serve immediately or let cool and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

To a mortar and pestle or food processor, add one 2" (5-cm) piece fresh ginger, chopped, 4 garlic cloves, peeled, and 3 green Thai chiles or 1 serrano, stemmed, chopped, and pound or pulse into a chunky paste. To a medium bowl, add 2 lb. (910 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, excess fat trimmed, cut into 2" [5-cm] pieces, along with the ginger-garlic paste and 1 tsp. fine sea salt and toss to combine. Cover and place in the refrigerator to marinate for a minimum of 1 hour or overnight.

It has been revealed that in a medium heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-low heat, warm ⅓ cup (80 ml) vegetable oil or avocado oil, then add 1 tsp. cumin seeds, ½ tsp. black mustard seeds, ½ tsp. black peppercorns, 5 whole cloves, 1 fresh or dried bay leaf, 1 star anise, and one 3" [7.5-cm] cinnamon stick, broken into small pieces, and lightly toast and until fragrant, about 1 minute. Increase the heat to medium, add 1 medium red or yellow onion (9 oz. [255 g]), finely chopped, cover, and cook until the onion is translucent and beginning to turn brown around the edges, stirring halfway through, about 10 minutes.

In a recent development, add 1 Tbsp. ground coriander, 1 Tbsp. Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 Tbsp. Garam Masala, 2 tsp. cayenne powder, and 1 tsp. powdered turmeric. Stir to combine and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Drain off the excess marinade from the chicken, then add it to the pot along with 3 Tbsp. tomato paste, 1 Tbsp. packed fresh fenugreek leaves, and remaining 1½ tsp. fine sea salt and stir until everything is mixed thoroughly and the chicken is covered with the spices and tomato paste. Add ½ cup (120 ml) water and mix again. Cover and cook until the chicken is cooked through and tender, 30 minutes, stirring halfway through.

Remove from the heat and sprinkle with the remaining 1 tsp. Garam Masala, remaining 1 tsp. fresh fenugreek leaves, and cilantro leaves. Serve immediately with lime wedges, Insanely Addictive Pickled Onions, and steamed rice or Indian flatbread.
