📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that when you’ve won a Super Bowl ring, made three Pro Bowl appearances, and played a key role on one of the most dominant defensive squads ever—the Seattle Seahawks’ 2010s-era Legion of Boom—what do you do next? For Michael Bennett, the answer was to head back to school.

After completing his 11-year NFL career in 2020, the 41-year-old enrolled at two institutions—the University of Hawaii and Seattle’s Heritage School of Interior Design—to study architecture and interior design, respectively. “I’m a student of whatever I do,” Bennett tells me. “My best quality—and probably my worst quality—is that the things I love to do, I try to become the best. I play tennis five days a week. I’m trying to go to Wimbledon. And design and architecture are like that.”.

It has been revealed that all that effort is paying off. Through his design practice Studio Kër, Bennett debuted an 11-piece collection of avant-garde furniture inspired by the African diaspora in 2024, which was well received by critics. He’s now hard at work on his sophomore line, alongside a spoken-word album and the occasional bespoke garment.

In a recent development, that last side quest should come as no surprise, because Bennett has some of the most distinctive personal style I’ve ever seen on a pro athlete–current or former—with a particularly clean headwear and accessories game. Here, Bennett tells me all about the skills he carried over from football into his new career, what fatherhood has taught him about masculinity, and the song he listens to every day.

Michael Bennett: I’ve been playing football my whole life, man. After winning so much, I dug deep. I had already conquered the body. How do I conquer the mind? At what point am I being selfish? I’m missing so much of my kids’ lives. I’ve already been to the highest of the high. Am I going to leave my family with a broken man? That was really the question. Am I chasing ego or am I chasing something else? In reality, a lot of us are just chasing the ego, to be remembered, scared of the death of what [your life] was rather than [embracing] the growth that can be.

Recent findings suggest that people want to keep others in a certain box because that’s the way that they understand them. That’s in any relationship. If you started to date somebody when they’re 20 and you turn 40 and they start to change, you’d be like, “You used to like your eggs like that.” People don’t allow others to transition; won’t allow people to actually experience growth. Often you’re meeting people in a time where they’re just starting to learn who they are. Over time you start to really develop who you are.

It has been revealed that the truth is it doesn’t matter if people take you seriously, [as long as] you take yourself seriously. What are you doing to practice your craft? Artists are like, “Oh, my practice, my practice.” I never really understood what that meant until I started doing my own practice. I practiced on the field and I can practice the body. But really, if you want to be taken seriously intellectually, then you have to practice the mind. Sometimes practicing the mind is also connected to the body. In football, yeah, you are connected to the mind in a certain way. But it isn’t always like learning to be a lawyer or an architect or an artist—to be a thinker, you’re doing something completely different. And it’s just allowing yourself to transition. Man, truthfully, you got to say fuck everybody.

I think it’s one of the most intellectual sports in general. Tennis is one of those sports where it’s about the angle, the quick twitch. You’re by yourself. With football, it’s the amount of moving parts. People overlook the amount of detail that it takes to run a team—practicing and going through a play 3,000 times before you actually get it. The best players I ever met were the smartest when it came to the sport. They were the PhDs of their craft.

It’s taught me vulnerability. It made me a better human. In some ways, my daughters have allowed me to mature. The sport of football requires so much masculinity. I’m not saying that all masculinity is toxic, [but] it’s more about, how do you hunt but still be gentle? The true samurai doesn’t strike, but knows he can.

According to recent reports, what my daughters have allowed me to do is develop my whole humanity. To have a daughter is so special—women are very special. As an athlete, people come back from injuries, but to see a woman come back from giving birth is a whole other level of love. My daughters have been my greatest accomplishments in my life. I never made a Super Bowl trophy. There’s always another winner. But there’s only one Peyton, there’s only one Blake, and there’s one Ollie. As a maker, those are the most special things that I could make.

In 2019, I was really into Booker T. Washington and W.E.B. Du Bois and [their debate over] the “Talented Tenth.” [Booker T. Washington believed that] intellectualism should never get away from the idea of making. I got into design because I’ve always been involved in politics, and politically, I started to realize that everything came down to design.

Shirt and pants by Studio Kër. Shoes by Collegium.

In a recent development, whenever I spoke out about police brutality or on critical issues in America, that was really where I started to think about design as this language—this form of resistance. How can I change the system? It starts with design. Where I grew up, a non-gentrified area that was low income, it’s like you could see that there was no empathetic way of thinking about design. The definition of architecture for me is empathy for space. That’s what led me to this idea of these African diaspora forms and languages that I will use as my form of resistance.

Recent findings suggest that I’m working on a upcoming collection of furniture. The first collection I did was called “We Gotta Get Back to the Crib,” which to me was really about getting back to the essence of Blackness. A lot of times we talk about Blackness and it’s always connected to traumatic experience. But to me, it was more about how can I connect to these true levels of love, these things really shaped my culture, my family, my mother, my grandmother, and everything that was beautiful about being Black? This next collection is about African brutalism. How can I bring these things that are seen in the ghetto in America and in West Africa and then turn those into ideas about furniture? A lot of times what I’m dealing with as a designer is this idea of abstraction. How can I pull and reference something in such a sweet way? Like how Virgil designed shoes with references, leaving crumbs to this unspoken past. As a designer, that’s what I’m trying to do.

Yeah, I got a spoken word project.

As an athlete, if you talk about your cars or you talk about your jewelry, the way that you gained it doesn’t have that kind of Jay-Z effect—you didn’t hustle to get that. You played to get that, which is different from somebody hustling to get that. With spoken word, I think about Gil Scott-Heron or The Last Poets. They’re talking about critical challenges. My perspective is really about humanizing the Black experience and the Black man. My stories and what I’m trying to tell with this music, E-Nigg-Ma, is so much about Black culture, Black design, Black features, this idea of what America is trying to suffocate about Blackness and not let it breathe.

In a recent development, cuff by Dries van Noten. Ring by Olithica. Watch by Patek Philippe.

Music. When I’m designing, beautiful sounds are really key to the way that I think. My number-one song that I always listen to is Miles Davis’s “Flamenco Sketches.” It’s my daily listen. Those are the sounds that I need to hear: the horn, the riffs, the in-between.

My studio inspires me, just the way light hits. It’s the simplest things. Seeing my family movies. My wife inspires me with what she’s designing.

It has been revealed that my great-grandpa, Hall Mack, everybody talked about his fashion. People still talk about his style. He was the first person I saw dry cleaning everything. His style was impeccable. When I look back at a period of style that I liked, it’d be the years of the Birth of the Cool. People like Miles, Sidney Poitier, everybody was just fresh.

I’ve always been connected to style. People always call me “Runway Mike.” They say, “Bro, you wear more Margiela than anybody I know.” I design my own clothes. [Style] is a part of who you are. I love the idea of fashion. I want to design a fashion show. Yo, Wales Bonner, let me design something for you! I want to be backstage.

According to recent reports, over time I just found me. That takes so much time. I feel like one of the most beautiful things is Instagram and this ability to share things, but one of the worst things is Instagram and the ability to share things. Because there’s a part of us that starts to mimic [what we see] in a way that isn’t true to us. We start to judge ourselves on other people’s experience.

It’s cool to see things, but it’s also cool to experiment with what you feel good in. “Yo, this is what I look good in. I don’t care what nobody claims, I feel good.” That’s what true fashion is. I buy Prada because I actually like it. That’s the development of who you are and your taste—when you buy things for the love of it. Like, “Man, I really love the shoulder on this.” I’m not buying anything to be seen in it. I’m buying it because I respect the process.

Recent findings suggest that the thing that’s exciting about fashion now is getting away from logos and getting back to beautiful garments. Margiela and Prada are two of my favorite brands of all time—Prada is just so detailed. Jil Sander is nice. I like Toteme.

Recent findings suggest that “My skin goes through so much between filming, travel, and wearing makeup for hours,” she says. “By the end of the day, I really want something that feels rich and helps my skin look refreshed. After using them, my skin feels like glass.”.

Glowing from the inside out, her recent appearances—be they in character on our TV screens or in late-night talk show clips on our phones—are proof both of RéVive’s results and the confidence that comes from feeling good in one’s own skin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Buzzy as they’ve become over the past several years, air fryers are really just small ovens with fans built into them, i.e., convection ovens that circulate hot air around your food. Our years of testing air fryers (and we’ve used over two dozen in that time) have taught us that there are plenty out there that can give you crispy-enough results—but the very best air fryers churn out not only golden brown French fries and crispy-skinned chicken wings, but tender fillets of salmon and even whole roast chickens at the touch of a button.

It has been revealed that air fryers can take a few forms; the robot-esque basket-style models are probably what come to mind when you think of an air fryer, but there are versatile countertop convection ovens that add bake, broil, toast, and slow-cook options to the air fryer functionality. Some even dehydrate and steam too. And most recently, more bowl-style air fryers have started to hit shelves, which swap a slide-in basket for a glass container and top-down, air-frying lid.

The best for all varieties of air fryer needs are below.

Updated 11/23/26: There may not be a more popular Black Friday sale item than an air fryer. And all our favorites have discounts this week, including our overall top Cosori pick for less than $100. High-tech options from Breville, Cuisinart, Instant Pot, and Ninja are deeply discounted, too.

Clearview 4-Quart Glass Basket Air Fryer.

Vortex Plus 6-Quart ClearCook Air Fryer.

Ninja SL401 DoubleStack XL 2-Basket Air Fryer.

Instant Vortex Slim XL 6-Quart Air Fryer.

Most air fryers fit into one of three categories: oven, basket, or bowl.

In a recent development, A countertop convection oven, or air fryer–toaster oven, combines most of the crisping power of the basket-style air fryers you know and love with the multifunctionality you get from a toaster oven or countertop oven. Generally, the “air frying” function is achieved with a perforated slide-in rack, which usually means lots of cooking surface, but the racks are usually shallow and can require careful tossing or flipping of whatever you’re cooking, depending on the dish. But air fryer ovens, like the Breville Smart Oven Pro with its 13 different cooking modes, can do a lot, making them bona fide do-it-all kitchen appliances.

It has been revealed that basket-style air fryers aren’t as versatile as air fryer ovens, but they’re also less expensive and take up less space. They also tend to deliver better final results on traditional air fryer stuff like crisping up small foods that require shaking (tater tots, French fries, or Brussels sprouts), for which a handled basket is far easier to maneuver. Minuses are that they can be hard to clean and are limited in square inches inside the basket. They’re also sometimes made of plastic or nonstick-coated materials, which may not appeal to some consumers.

Recent findings suggest that bowl air fryers offer some of the best (and worst) of both worlds and also some unique benefits. Most of these include a heat-resistant glass bowl acting as the basket. Some models operate much like basket air fryers, with the glass container sliding into the base unit, while others opt for a “lid” that sits on top and houses the air frying mechanism. The glass baskets make these very easy to clean (included crisping trays are another story), however their functionality for shaking and pausing to flip foods can be cumbersome. But many come with lids for the glass containers, letting them double as prep and storage containers too.

Capacity: 6 qt.Wattage: 172510 Cooking functions: Air Fry, Roast, Broil, Frozen, Preheat, Reheat, Dehydrate, Proof, Bake, and Keep WarmColor: WhiteWeight: 11.5 lb.Dimensions: 11.8" x 14.4" x 11.9"Warranty: 2 years.

Industry observers note that what we love: The 6-Quart Cosori Turboblaze Smart Air Fryer impressed us in every test, producing evenly browned and crispy frozen sweet potato fries, juicy chicken breasts, and perfectly cooked brussels sprouts. It has a straightforward digital interface that allows you to easily set the time and temperature and an impressive array of preset programs (Air Fry, Roast, Broil, Frozen, Preheat, Reheat, Dehydrate, Proof, Bake, and Keep Warm).

According to recent reports, A few things set the Turboblaze apart from the competition (including the previous longtime winner of this test, the Instant Vortex Slim). Most notably, it consistently produced the crispiest food of any air fryer we tested in record time. That may have something to do with the fact that there’s more space between the crisper plate (where the food sits) and the bottom of the basket than there is in some of the other top-performing models we’ve tried, which allows for better air circulation.

Another standout feature is its variable fan speeds, which adjust automatically depending on the cooking function. Unlike most air fryers that use this tech behind the scenes, the Turboblaze indicates you the fan speed right on the display. Air Fry, for example, is one of four “turbo modes,” running the fan at full blast (speed 5), while Bake uses a gentler speed 3 to avoid disrupting delicate foods. Low-temperature settings like Dehydrate and Proof drop all the way down to speed 1.

The Cosori Turboblaze is also a real value pick. The top performer in its price range (100–150) by a wide margin, it’s powerful, versatile, quiet, lightweight, and easy to clean (the brand says both the nonstick basket and cooking tray are dishwasher-safe, though we recommend hand-washing anything with a nonstick coating).

The model we tested includes smart features, meaning you can control it remotely or use voice commands via the VeSync app. If that’s not your thing, Cosori also sells a non-smart version for about $10 less.

Sources indicate that what we’d leave: Our gripes with this model are minor. It’s slightly annoying that you have to press a release button to pull the basket out. And while the greater amount of space between the crisper tray and basket bottom contributes to better airflow (and thus better browning), it means food is more likely to fall through while cooking.

Capacity: 2.1-qt.Wattage: 9004 cooking functions: Air-Fry, Bake, Roast, ReheatColors: Gray, red, white, greenWeight: 4.9 lb.Dimensions: 10.1" x 8.3" x 10.5"Warranty: 2 years.

If you’re on a tighter budget, have very little counter space to spare, or are mostly crisping up food just for yourself, consider the Cosori Lite 2.1-Quart Mini Air Fryer.

What we love: This compact air fryer did a beautiful job crisping and browning small servings of frozen tater tots and fries, sliced zucchini, and veggie burger patties (two at a time, max). Depending on where you buy, it will only costs $50–$60 (as of publish time)—not at all bad for a lightweight, quiet, digital air fryer with four easy-to-use presets (air-fry, roast, bake, and reheat). It’s easy to tuck into a cabinet and to clean. Like the Cosori Blaze, the Lite has a nonstick basket. Again, while the manual claims the nonstick basket is dishwasher-safe, we always recommend hand-washing anything with a nonstick coating.

What we’d leave: Per its name, it’s quite small—don’t expect to be cooking enough food for more than two people in this thing. It also won’t remind you when it’s time to shake your food, so you’ll need to keep an eye on the timer yourself (luckily, the digital display makes this pretty easy).

If you want an air fryer with maximum versatility and have some counter space to spare, spring for the Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro. Breville makes a few different models (which can be found in the kitchens of many of our editors), but this one is the best combination of performance and value.

What we love: This midrange model has been our top pick for years now because of its versatility, build quality, intuitive design, and consistently strong performance in testing.

According to recent reports, in testing, the Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro delivered reliably great results. It excelled at foods that need to be laid in a flat, even layer across the crisper tray (think veggie burgers or salmon fillets), but also handled frozen fries, tots, and sweet potato fries well. Its interior is roomy enough to fit a quarter sheet pan or 13x9" casserole pan, which means it can effectively double your oven space (or eliminate the need to turn on your full-size oven altogether).

This model is also a favorite among BA staffers and Test Kitchen editors, as well as award-winning cookbook author Nik Sharma, who developed some of BA’s favorite air fryer recipes. “I prefer toaster-oven-style to basket-style air fryers, because they’re easier to use for more common tasks like baking, toasting bread, and roasting more efficiently,” Sharma says.

In a recent development, what we’d leave: As with most oven-style air fryers, it’s harder to toss or shake small foods mid-cook compared to a basket-style machine. We also found that, in general, food benefited from a higher cooking temperature (and often slightly longer cook time) relative to the basket-style winners.

Capacity: .5 cubic feetWattage: 18005 Cooking functions: Toast, Bagel, Broil, Pizza, Bake & Roast5 Air-frying functions: Air-Fry, Fries, Wings, Bacon, Crispy ReheatColor: Stainless steelWeight: 15.8 lb.Dimensions: 15.7" x 16.9" x 10"Warranty: 2 years.

If you like the idea of going the air fryer–toaster oven route but (1) don’t have the space for the Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro or (2) don’t want to shell out $400 in pursuit of crispiness, here’s some good news: Breville offers the Smart Oven Air Fryer Compact, which is essentially a smaller, cheaper version of our top pick.

What we love: As with most Breville products, the Smart Oven Air Fryer Compact feels thoughtfully designed, with stainless-steel finishes and a solid build. There are fewer niche modes than the Pro—no Dehydrate or Proof—but it does include four air-frying-specific presets in addition to a standard Air Fry setting.

According to recent reports, we found using the Compact intuitive (the guide printed on the inside of the oven door helped). We also appreciated the “bit more” button, a feature borrowed from Breville’s toasters that adds a touch of extra cooking time when your fries are looking just a touch underdone.

This model performed comparably to the Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro in most of our tests, producing juicy chicken, evenly browned cubes of tofu, and crispy veggies. We still prefer the larger model for its versatility and additional functionality, but this little oven would make a worthy addition to any smaller kitchen.

In a recent development, what we’d leave: While the Compact did well in most tests, it struggled a bit with frozen sweet potato fries. This largely came down to overcrowding due to the smaller capacity: While we tried to fit an entire bag’s worth on a single tray, the unevenness with which the fries browned is a good example of the fact that, unlike a basket fryer, countertop oven-style air fryers are best used to cook things in a single layer.

It has been revealed that as mentioned, there’s a guide to oven inserts and placement on the inside of the oven’s door, but this is easy to miss, and these suggestions did not appear in full in the manual. Because of this, one tester accidentally cooked chicken with no tray underneath the wire basket to catch the drippings, which resulted in a smoking-hot mess.

It’s also worth noting that one of the major benefits of opting for an oven-style air fryer tends to be capacity, but the Compact wasn’t able to fit more food than our top basket-style pick.

The Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Compact (L) is much smaller than the Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro (R).

Clearview 4-Quart Glass Basket Air Fryer.

Capacity: 4 qt.Wattage: 16005 Cooking functions: Air Fry, Bake, Broil, Recrisp, Keep Warm, plus custom settingsColors: Black, Toasted Oat, Sage, TahiniWeight: 12.75 lb.Dimensions: 13.75" W x 12.75" D x 11.25" HWarranty: 3 years.

It has been revealed that fresh on the market in 2026, Cuisinart’s ClearView series of air fryers truly delivers on its name with the introduction of a glass basket model that also sports a viewing window on the top of the unit (the line also features a larger, 9-qt. non-glass model). Unlike other glass air fryers we tried, this one operates more like the basket-style most people expect when they think of an air fryer.

Recent findings suggest that what we love: The ClearView got high marks across the board in our tests comparing glass air fryers head-to-head, almost always offering up the winning results. The controls are easy to navigate, and the functions are intuitive with beeps to remind you to flip or shake your food when your cook is halfway through. In addition to the usual Air Fry, Bake, and Reheat functions, Cuisinart’s also offers a Keep Warm. Plus, there are two programmable custom presets if you’re cooking the same foods frequently.

The crisper plate is nonstick, coated in PFAS-free ceramic, making it a breeze to clean with a little soap and water (or just throw it in the dishwasher). The glass basket is also dishwasher-safe. The ClearView doesn’t have any kind of mesh or grate covering the heating mechanism. We’ll continue to see how this fares over time, but in the meantime it’s nice not worrying about another greasy, perforated plate to clean. Lastly, the ClearView 4-Quart Glass Basket Air Fryer also comes in four colors—Black, Toasted Oat, Sage, and Tahini—and, as with all countertop appliances, it’s nice to have some kind of choice behind black plastic and stainless steel.

What we’d leave: The cord wrap post noticeably sticks out from the back of the unit. While this is probably great for airflow safety, it adds inches to a machine that’s also tall. And unlike some of the other glass air fryers we tried, Cuisinart’s bowl is oven or microwave safe. Granted, the point of the bowl is to air-fry, but if you’re using to carry your lunch into the office after cooking the night before, reheating is a little trickier.

We won’t go down the PFAS rabbit hole and get deep into the concept of “nontoxic” cookware right here and now (we've got other articles for that), but given the way the concept has come front and center we know some people want an air fryer with a PFAS-free nonstick basket—and for that, we recommend the Cosori Iconic.

What we love: It has similar features and produces similar results to our top pick, the Cosori TurboBlaze, churning out crispy-skinned salmon and beautifully browned Brussels. Like the TurboBlaze, the Iconic allows you to choose between five different fan speeds, which means it's equally adept at turning delicate kale into crispy chips without blowing them around the basket as it is cooking hefty bone-in chicken breasts to bronzed perfection.

And for those looking to eliminate PFAS from every inch of their kitchen, it has both a PFAS-free ceramic nonstick-coated basket and crisper plate.

What we’d leave: Aesthetically, it may not be for everyone as this stainless-steel air fryer looks a bit spaceship-like. But the real downside is the price, which is practically double that of the TurboBlaze.

In the long run: The Cosori Iconic has seamlessly fit into the life of BA’s head of video, Dan Siegel. The speed is what won him over: “I shave 25% or more off any package-recommended cooking time and achieve perfect browning and crisping on every cook. The nonstick surfaces of both the basket and the included rack are remarkably easy to clean, making this my go-to appliance. My toaster oven probably misses me.” He mostly uses it for his two kids, occasionally scaling up to cook chicken breasts for his family of four, which takes two batches. (“It’s not huge.”) Despite the mirror-like stainless-steel finish, upkeep has been simple: “I haven't had any issues; I really only touch the top and the basket.” And then there’s the look. "It looks grown-up, like an actual appliance and not a significant plastic toy without looking industrial. The MacBook of air fryers.".

According to recent reports, we have spent hours and hours over the past few years researching, testing, and retesting popular air fryers from top-name brands, including Breville, Cuisinart, Ninja, Philips, and Cosori. Here's how we put each appliance to the test:.

When evaluating each model, we looked for a few key qualities:.

4-Quart Vortex 6-in-1 Mini Air Fryer.

Recent findings suggest that this model from Instant Pot is a great option if a full-size (6-qt. or more) air fryer feels too big for your space or lifestyle, but our winning mini model (2-qt. limit) is too small. There’s a lot to love here, including the intuitive controls and presets, the viewing window and built-in light, and the ceramic nonstick interior coating. In testing, we found it did a decent job crisping everything we threw at it, though its performance didn’t quite match the winning Cosori Turboblaze.

Instant Vortex Slim XL 6-Quart Air Fryer.

According to recent reports, this model from Instant was a previous top pick, and we still think it’s an excellent air fryer. Its design, although compact, offers a significantly larger cooking surface area than comparably sized air fryers thanks to the shape of its basket. In practice, this meant our tester was able to fit an entire extra veggie burger patty (six total) compared to models of a similar size and generally cook more food in each batch without sacrificing any of the airflow that makes air-fried food so crispy.

Vortex Plus 6-Quart ClearCook Air Fryer.

Sources indicate that if a basket-style air fryer is what you’re after and you like the idea of being able to monitor what you’re cooking, the Instant Pot Vortex Plus ClearCook is definitely worth considering. This model performed nearly identically to our old top pick, the Instant Vortex Slim (probably because it’s a very similar build). The major difference—besides the ClearCook’s dimensions—is that it has a cooking window located at the front of its basket, plus a button that switches on an interior light, sort of like a traditional oven. This makes tracking the progress of your tots, fries, or chicken wings possible without removing the basket and disrupting the cooking process. Considering that providing a certain level of brownness is one of the chief concerns in air fryer cooking, this really comes in handy. A few more bonus points for the ClearCook: It adds Dehydrate to its list of functions and can hold temperatures as low as 95°F (the low end of the Vortex Slim’s range is 120°F). The ClearCook also happens to be $30 cheaper than the Slim at full price. On the downside, the square shape of the ClearCook’s basket fits one less veggie burger patty than more elongated baskets. It’s also a bit bulky.

The Typhur Dome 2 is notably spacious compared to other basket-style fryers, with 139.5 square inches of cooking surface that fits a 12" pizza, 20 chicken wings, or 11 large chicken thighs per batch, and a digital panel with 15 presets plus a companion app offering more settings, self-cleaning, and one-touch recipes. We used to recommend the original Typhur Dome as a top pick for extra-large capacity, but after testing the Dome 2, which replaced it, we felt its performance didn’t quite merit a spot on our top picks: When filled to capacity, it took much longer to properly cook and crisp food than most other basket air fryers, and 11 bone-in chicken thighs took upward of 45 minutes to get truly golden, a major red flag given that cutting cooking time is a massive reason to choose an air fryer over the oven. That said, the Dome 2 cooks food evenly and does eventually get very crisp, so if you’re feeding a large family and have counter space to spare, it may still be worth the investment.

Industry observers note that the Philips almost took a top spot—almost. It’s got a generous capacity, the control panel is easy to navigate, and it performs well with minimal user intervention. In other words, you won’t have to do a lot of shaking or stirring to get crispy fries from the Philips. This model did have a smaller yet heavier basket, and it’s loud and harder to clean due to a bunch of interlocking parts. It’s a good air fryer, but with its higher price tag, we feel like there are better deals on this list.

According to recent reports, this newer model from Philips has a lot going for it: sleek touchscreen interface, helpful viewing window, and a whopping 16 settings. It did very well in our testing, producing crispy tots, tofu, and fries, but we preferred the design and the interface of the Cosori and Instant models. If you’re looking for an air fryer with a window feature, we’d recommend going with the Instant ClearCook (slightly cheaper at the time of writing) unless you find this model at a discount.

The Dreo ChefMaker isn't just an air fryer—it's also got probe cooking capabilities and app compatibility that make cooking proteins pretty effortless, and is a personal favorite of senior editor Olivia Tarantino. For the purposes of this article, though, we mainly tested its air frying abilities. We found that while the Dreo performed well, the winning TurboBlaze produced crispier, more evenly-cooked results all while ringing in at a third of the price. That stated, if the probe cooking feature intrigues you, this fryer might be worth a try.

Industry observers note that our Place partnered with James Beard Award–winning chef and cookbook author J. Kenji López-Alt on this updated version of the Wonder Oven, which features eight cooking functions, a touchscreen interface, and a roomy three-tier 30-liter capacity. Like all of Our Place's products, this little oven is an aesthete’s dream—but looks aside, it impressed us. It’s incredibly powerful, able to crisp brussels sprouts, tofu, and fries up to twice as fast as the winning Breville. It produced tender salmon with potato-chip-like skin in just seven minutes. Despite its smaller footprint, it’s large enough to fit a quarter-sheet pan, making it a good option if you want to save a few inches of counter space.

Industry observers note that all that said, while the Wonder Oven Pro is generally well-designed, a few features were annoying to use. The touchscreen isn’t the most responsive. But the bigger issue we had was with the preheating cycle. Preheating this oven to 400°F took 8–9 minutes from cold, which is already slower than the Breville’s 4–5. But more importantly, the Breville (like most regular ovens) takes less time to preheat when it’s already at temp. The Wonder Oven Pro, on the other hand, seemed to kick off a whole newly introduced several-minutes-long preheat cycle even when it had just been heated, only after which the timer would start.

Cuisinart Air Fryer Oven 6-Qt Basket Stainless Steel Air Fryer.

In a recent development, the Cuisinart was easy to use, didn’t whirr too loudly, included a nice preheat feature, and was about the same price. We also really liked the viewing window you could use to check the progress of your food. However, its deeper square-shaped basket has less surface area than something like the Instant Vortex Slim’s rectangular one, which limits its capacity.

Ninja SL401 DoubleStack XL 2-Basket Air Fryer.

In a recent development, the DoubleStack takes the idea of a dual-basket air fryer to a whole upcoming level—literally. Like the Vortex Slim, the DoubleStack’s design prioritizes using vertical space. It’s skinny with the baskets stacked on top of each other instead of side by side like most other dual models. This makes it narrow and tall instead of wide, but not so tall that you can’t nestle it under your cabinets. Despite its space-saving design, you don’t lose out on actual cooking space. The baskets are big enough to fit a chicken, and the wire racks in each mean you can really maximize how much you’re cooking. (Though you do need to remain mindful of not overloading it with food, otherwise you’ll block the airflow and mess up the whole air-frying process.) You can also program the baskets separately and utilize the machine’s Smart Finish feature—which delays the start of the basket with the shorter cook—to have a whole meal ready at the same time. The one thing we didn’t like was the somewhat confusing interface.

AeroLucen 5-quart Glass Air Fryer.

Sources indicate that like the Cuisinart ClearView we recommend above, this glass air fryer operates like a traditional basket air fryer, in fact even more so as it features a front-mounted basket handle with slide-in operation. It’s a sleek-looking machine with a glossy top that illuminates when powered on with all of your touch-surface buttons. And we like that’s is relatively compact at just over 9.5" tall, making it great for in-cabinet storage. In the glass category, it performed nearly as well as the Cuisinart across the board with just a few cases of less even results, but we’re really nitpicking. What we didn’t like was the mesh-style crisping plate, which is tedious to clean and sits awkwardly on some jutting posts inside the basket, (though its design does offer a high and low position for maximizing space or airflow). That mesh is repeated on the underside of the heating element, something we don’t look forward to cleaning after a few dozen oil-evaporating cooking cycles. The internal light is intended to help you see what you’re cooking, but it glows red, which isn’t so helpful when you’re trying to keep an eye on browning.

Of the lid-style glass bowl air fryers we tested, this one was the easiest to maneuver with a fold-away handle that makes removing the top easy for flipping or shaking in the middle of cooking. With fine-tunable controls, it nailed crunchy skin on chicken thighs and crispy brussels sprouts with tender centers. More delicate dishes like salmon didn’t get where we wanted on the first try, and tofu cubes required more time than the recipe allotted to get anywhere near crispy enough. It fell short, as a lot of the glass bowl fryers did, on frozen fries, yielding uneven results and underdone portions when using the settings suggested on the back of the bag. We wish the “flip” alert was more than just a light, and it’s a little odd that the “Dehydrate” setting is listed as a bonus because you have to long-press another button to use it. The attached feet also mean the glass bowl can’t be put in the oven or microwave, but it is dishwasher-safe and comes with a lid. Plus, the whole fryer and basket setup is designed to nest inside itself for storage. And of this style of meal-prep-friendly air fryers, it’s the best version.

Instant Vortex Plus 4-Quart Air Fryer.

This Instant Pot air fryer model is if you need something with a smaller capacity. The rectangular shape of its basket made it easy to fit plenty of food inside. It is sleek and has a short profile, which are nice features too. The Vortex Slim just offered better performance.

This is Ninja's basic basket air fryer. It’s lightweight and simple to use, and it does a nice job crisping up fries. The round shape of its basket, though, makes it less versatile than other models on this list. If you’re trying to cook raw proteins or a tray of vegetables, you give away a lot of space with a round basket.

While the Dash looks cute with its retro silhouette and poppy colors, it just didn’t perform that well. Sweet potato fries came out soggy and greasy. Tofu cubes got crisped on one side but were raw on the other, and the round basket could only fit one veggie burger. The two dials, controlling time and temperature, also prevented us from getting more specific in the cook settings.

Panasonic FlashXpress Air Fryer Toaster Oven.

This oven-style air fryer from Panasonic performed well in our testing, but we found it frustrating to use for a few reasons. It has 12 different functions, but they come with very little on the display as to what each of these functions truly means. The Air Fry mode only allowed us to select temperatures between 410℉–445℉, which seemed quite high for certain foods. We also disliked the automatic preheating period that we couldn’t bypass even if the oven was already hot (this was particularly annoying when we just wanted to tack on an extra few minutes after finishing a cooking cycle). If you want to do that, you have to take the extra step of once again pressing the start button after the preheating process in order to start the timed cook cycle.

Recent findings suggest that like all of DTC darling Our Place’s products, the original Wonder Oven is cute. Unfortunately, it failed to impress us enough to earn a recommendation here. While it did fine at cooking tater tots and french fries, it produced unevenly browned, ultra mushy zucchini and tofu that never quite got the crisp exterior we were looking for. The analog controls are aesthetically pleasing, but make selecting an exact temperature impossible (and knowing when the unit is at temperature impossible too). It did, however, make a shockingly good fillet of crispy-skinned salmon.

Rather than a typical basket system, the Crispi consists of a glass container and a PowerPod that sits on top. The idea is that you can store your food directly in the glass containers, and Crispi sets include as many as three basket sizes (with more available). While most food did get crisp in the Crispi (you’d hope so with a name like that!), it took longer to do so than in a standard basket air fryer, and we found that food cooked somewhat unevenly. We tested this unit twice, the second time head-to-head with other glass air fryers, and our biggest gripe remains that there’s no precise temperature control—instead, you must choose between four preset modes (Max Crisp, Bake, Air Fry, and Recrisp). We thought that lack of precision made this model less versatile, and remembering which mode to use for which temperature number recommended on the bag of frozen fries or other foods wasn’t very user-friendly.

In a recent development, the Typhur Sync has lots of bells and whistles, like a wireless probe thermometer (with a built-in charging port), app compatibility, a PFAS-free basket, and nine total programs (including the three found only in the app). In testing, though, it failed to produce as impressive results as the winning Cosori. The fries browned, but many remained soggy, the salmon skin failed to crisp, and the Brussels sprouts didn’t quite get as golden as we’d have liked. While some of this might be solved by tinkering with time and temperature, at $160, we just didn’t feel this air fryer was worth the splurge.

It has been revealed that in its defense, Magnifique’s Glass Air Fryer has some thoughtful features: two sizes of glass baskets (4.5-qt. and 2.5-qt.), each with lids, and a silicone base that’s easy to remove for cleaning and oven or microwave cooking (something Cuisinart and Ninja can’t match). It’s also the only glass air fryer we tested in this round that could possibly hold a small pizza with an 8.5" diameter crisper plate. However, there are more than a few aspects that weren’t as user-friendly. The stainless-steel crisper plate (no nonstick coating whatsoever) was the most difficult to clean by far, not only because of that lack of coating but because of the perforation pattern as well. The instructions specifically say don’t use scouring pads, but a gentle scrub with a plastic pad was the only way we could remove all the residue. There’s no reminder to flip or shake your food halfway through, a pretty standard-matter beep on many other units, and when you do take the lid off, you have to actually hit Start again to keep going, something other fryers do automatically. Results, especially with frozen foods like fries, were uneven, and fine-tuning is near impossible as its interface only allows for four preset cooking modes with no customization. If you’re following a recipe, you’ll have to remember which mode gets to which general temperature range and hope for the best.

Sources indicate that what is an air fryer? Is it just a convection oven?

Recent findings suggest that an air fryer is a countertop oven that uses hot air, circulated by a fan, to give foods crisper textures than you can achieve in a regular oven or toaster oven. What makes an air fryer a “fryer” is a built-in convection fan that blows the hot air around the food to crisp it up. It’s the combination of heat and moving air that produces the kind of crispy exterior you’d otherwise get from deep-frying or pan-frying. But unlike a deep fryer, an air fryer requires far less oil to achieve the desired effect—and it doesn’t leave your house smelling like a grease trap for days or weeks. So, technically speaking, yes, air fryers are just small convection ovens, but the most classic form of air fryer isn’t usually oven-shaped, rather more like egg or block with a slide-out basket on the front.

Whether you’re a purist and only consider products that contain baskets to be true air fryers, or you find the term air fryer to be stupid marketing jargon for a convection oven is up to you to decide. For the purposes of this review, we’ve included both toaster ovens that contain convection or “air fryer” settings and basket or bowl air fryers.

What accessories should I buy for my air fryer?

It has been revealed that there are a few extras you can buy to optimize your frying experience—things like an olive oil sprayer (so you can crisp without spilling oil on the heating element), parchment paper liners, and an instant read thermometer. For more of our favorite air fryer accessories, head right this way.

According to recent reports, alaina Chou: I’ve been testing air fryers and other small appliances for Bon Appétit and Epicurious since 2023. In that time, I’ve cooked countless batches of salmon, brussels sprouts, and frozen fries in pursuit of an air fryer that delivers on the lofty promise of deep-fryer-level crispiness without the need for a vat of hot oil. And I’ve blown out the power in the Test Kitchen numerous times in the process (sorry, Test Kitchen editors).

Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau are continuing their Venetian holiday in style.

As the California Gurl and Mr. Canada traipsed through the Italian city today, Perry opted for a pop star’s take on prep. Bundled up in a Fair Isle sweater and black double-breasted coat, she added a pair of rectangular transition lenses, heeled penny loafers with white socks, and a cashmere argyle scarf from And Daughter, the latter tied under her chin à la Sophia Loren. (When in Italy, after all!).

Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau in Venice.

Trudeau, on the other hand, looked the part of an off-duty politician in a chore coat, fitted pants, and boots. But it was his baseball cap—emblazoned with a red maple leaf—that really brought his patriotism home.

At the opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art.

Industry observers note that the pair, who have been linked since the summer of 2025, have often embraced an opposites-attract approach in their couple style. While Perry tried her hand at first lady dressing at the World Economic Forum in Davos in January, she’s returned to her pop star roots. Just take the sculptural silver Christian Siriano dress she wore to the opening of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in September, or the camel cashmere set—plus Ralph Lauren hat, sunglasses, and over-ear headphones—for her arrival in Venice. Trudeau, to be fair, has met her halfway: the former PM went tieless at the Lucas Museum and arrived in Venice wearing a “will yap about books” T-shirt.

All the same, though they are clearly willing to change for each other, it looks like Katy Perry and Justin Trudeau are sticking to what they know during their Venice getaway.

Industry observers note that A substantial, billowing cloud of meringue tops this crimson beauty and acts as a sweet reprieve from the tart cranberry curd. The vibrant filling is made even more sour with a generous amount of lime juice. Think lemon meringue pie but holiday-ified. Use our Perfect Pie Crust as the base to create a sturdy-flaky foundation, and be sure to start the pie the day before you blueprint to serve it, as the curd requires several hours of chilling to set into a sliceable texture. Cut into it too soon and it will run onto your plate, creating a messy—albeit delicious—slice.

According to recent reports, we never make pie dough without a metal bench scraper. Our favorite is from Gestura. Use the scraper to cut butter, fold dough and nudge it into shape, transfer it from counter to plastic wrap, trim edges, cut strips, and, sure, scrape flour off your counter.

It has been revealed that welcome to Bon Appétit Bake Club, a community of curious bakers. Each month senior Test Kitchen editors Jesse Szewczyk and Shilpa Uskokovic share a must-make recipe and dive deep on why it works. Come bake and learn with us—ask questions, share pics, listen to our podcast, and lots more here. And don't forget to join the Bake Club Group chat over on Substack.

3 hours (plus 30 minutes for freezing and 5 hours for chilling).

Whisk 1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour, 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ¼ tsp. baking powder in a large bowl to combine. Add 2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces, and rub into dry ingredients with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy). Add 10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash with your fingers into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea-size).

Recent findings suggest that make a well in the center of mixture and pour in ¼ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute, then knead in bowl a couple of times to bring dough together (some dry bits may remain).

Turn out dough onto a surface lightly dusted with rice flour or all-purpose flour and dust top of dough with flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold dough in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again. Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting with more rice flour as needed to prevent sticking. Pat into a ½"-thick disk and wrap tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.

Let dough disk sit at room temperature 5 minutes. Roll out dough on a lightly floured surface to a 12" round, about ¼" thick. Brush excess flour from dough and wrap around rolling pin. Transfer to a 9"-diameter pie pan (such as East Fork Spun Iron Pie Dish). Unfurl into pan, then lift edges and allow dough to slump down into pan. Trim, leaving about a 1½" overhang. Fold overhang under so crust is flush with edges of pan and crimp as desired with lightly floured fingers. Set pan on a rimmed baking sheet and prick bottom and sides of crust with a fork in several places. Freeze, uncovered, at least 30 minutes and up to 2 hours.

According to recent reports, place a rack in lower third of oven; preheat to 400°. Line crust with a sheet of parchment paper and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake crust, tenting edges with foil if browning too quickly, until edges are set and look dry, 20–25 minutes. Carefully lift out parchment paper and weights and continue baking crust, gently pressing bottom and sides occasionally with a flat-bottomed measuring cup if puffing up, until bottom looks dry and is golden, 20–25 minutes more. Transfer pan to a wire rack and let crust cool.

Do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

Bring 1 lb. fresh or frozen cranberries, 1½ cups (300 g) granulated sugar, and ¼ cup water to a boil in a large saucepan, then reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring often, until cranberries soften and burst and most of the liquid has evaporated, 10–15 minutes. Let cranberry mixture cool.

According to recent reports, transfer cranberry mixture to a blender; reserve pan. Add ⅔ cup fresh lime juice and ¼ cup (32 g) cornstarch and blend on high speed until smooth. Scrape purée back into pan (not over heat) and add 3 large eggs, 2 large egg yolks, 1 Tbsp. vanilla extract, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt. Place over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until mixture bubbles and thickens to a pudding-like consistency, about 4 minutes. Remove pan from heat. Add ¾ cup (1½ sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces, and whisk until melted and combined. Strain curd through a fine-mesh sieve, pushing with a rubber spatula, directly into crust. Smooth into an even layer and cover with plastic wrap, pressing directly onto surface. Chill pie at least 4 hours and up to 1 day.

Just before serving, beat 6 large egg whites, room temperature, ¼ tsp. cream of tartar, remaining 1¼ cups (250 g) granulated sugar, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment on medium speed until foamy and sugar is dissolved, about 5 minutes. Increase speed to high and continue to beat until stiff peaks form, about 3 minutes more.

In a recent development, turkey is the star of Thanksgiving dinner, but it can also be the star of dessert if you stretch your imagination enough. This idea first gained popularity on TikTok, using chocolate-dipped strawberries, marshmallows, pretzel rods, and melted chocolate to create these adorable little treats.

According to recent reports, they're so simple to make: To make a leg, you spear two mini marshmallows with half a pretzel rod, then use kitchen shears to trim the edges into a long oval shape. Repeat for a second leg, then cut one mini marshmallow diagonally in half to make the wings. You'll stick these to the strawberry with a dab of melted chocolate (which acts as your glue), then let that sit to adhere. All that's left is a quick bath in melted chocolate.

So yesterday, even though it was still a balmy 68 degrees in NYC, it was no surprise to see Chalamet cheering on his beloved Knicks at Madison Square Garden in yet another excellent down-filled jacket and blizzard-ready boots.

According to recent reports, sitting courtside, the Dune star wore a combination familiar to just about anyone who’s endured winter on the East Coast. The jacket was a dusty pink number from Goldwin, the cult Japanese outdoors brand founded back in 1950. It cuts a sharp silhouette despite packing some serious down insulation, and the windproof, water-resistant nylon is designed to ward off rain, sleet, and snow. The muted exterior has a subtle sheen—not quite Cam’ron pink, but certainly not your average black puffer. But these pull-ons were, in fact, from menswear favorite Merrell, built for some truly cold and ugly weather. The outer suede is water-resistant, the lining is insulated, and the rubber outsoles boast some serious traction. Plus, the very gorp-y utility cord at the heel lets you cinch them extra tight. Like the advanced-level dresser he is, Chalamet tucked his baggy black pants into the boots, making sure his footwear got a chance to really shine.

Once again, Chalamet has turned practical winter clothes into an A-list look. While a pink puffer might not be every guy’s idea of cold-weather dressing, there’s something to be said for a winter coat with a little personality. Was celebrity row’s resident heartthrob a few weeks early with this ensemble? Sure, but when that first serious snowfall hits, he’ll be extra ready.

The Body is Netflix’s latest buzzy teen psychodrama, and it’s not surprising why. The show, a cross between The Craft, Jennifer’s Body, and Cruel Intentions, follows a group of Catholic high school cheerleaders who sacrifice a newcomer in a pact with Satan to secure a spot in regionals. But when their sacrifice works too well, all of the girls on the team—and the town at large—are left with religious hysteria.

It has been revealed that the show promptly caught fire on social media following its arrival on November 11, leaving fans praying for a second installment, but will it return? Here’s everything we know about season 2 of The Body.

The Body has not been renewed for a second season yet by Netflix. The streamer typically waits a few weeks after a show’s premiere before sharing a season renewal announcement.

No cast members have been confirmed for season 2 yet, but fans are hoping that Kristina Bogic, Sara Boustany, Geena Meszaros, Nnamdi Asomugha, Louisa Krause, Shirley Chen, Jackson Kelly, Sofia Wylie, Kyra Pierce, Phallon Pierce, Marcel Ruiz, Orlando Norman, and Gabby Windey all return to their roles.

Recent findings suggest that season 1 ends with a few cliffhangers that leave the window open for a potential season 2. In the final episode, Anya finally confesses to head priest Father Franklin (Nnamdi Asomugha), and Grace finally wakes up, with her first words being “I’m God.”.

Recent findings suggest that some fans have interpreted Anya’s confession as being the reason why Grace finally wakes up. Gammell didn’t confirm the theory, but she told Deadline, “That’s a fire take...that is Maddie’s prophecy, and if there’s a season 2 we’ll be all over that.”.

Elsewhere in Gammell’s Deadline interview, she opened up about Tyler and Lisbeth potentially sleeping together, which could possibly become its own season 2 plot. “I think if they sleep together, it’s like another great mystery of the show. None of us were there, so none of us really know what happened in that room,” she added. “But I do think Geena has a joke that Lisbeth’s first kiss was the mouth-to-mouth with Grace when she was trying to resuscitate her. So, I don’t know how fast she’s going. She’s just a baby.”.

In an interview with Swooon, Gammell noted that the ending of The Body was “a tease and a setup of everywhere that we wish to go next season, if we’re so lucky to get one.”.

Industry observers note that some of the cast members already have ideas on what they’d like to see happen should The Body receive a season 2 renewal. “We love to pitch stuff to Quinn [Shephard] and Gina [Gammell], like probably too much. They’re so receptive,” Boustany told Swooon, while Bogic added, “We’re all so close, and that was also the tone on set. It was very welcomed [to pitch ideas].”.

The Body season 2 has no release date yet, so fans will have to stay tuned for updates.

Geena Meszaros is in the cat sweatshirt.

Worn by her polarizing character Lisbeth in Netflix’s new Catholic school drama The Body, the white crew-neck pullover Meszaros took from set—and is now sporting on our Zoom call—is a key bit of the show’s iconography. The gray kitten’s big green eyes gaze slightly upward, a single paw emerging from under her chin. It’s the perfect veneer of innocence; she could either beckon you closer or pounce.

According to recent reports, depending on which corner of The Body fandom you find yourself in, Lisbeth is either an innately evil villain or an Ethel Cain–coded antihero. (The singer-songwriter herself recently weighed in on the show via her Tumblr account: “i fear lisbeth is, in fact, my biological little sister.”) At the beginning of actress-turned-director Quinn Shephard’s series, which is set in 2004, we understand Lisbeth immediately as an outsider. She watches the Lions dance team—headed by queen bee Anya, played by Kristina Bogic—float by in their matching track pants with ill-disguised greed. She moves like someone not totally in control of their limbs. She has no eyebrows. (Well, okay, they’ve just been bleached to the gods.).

Recent findings suggest that the actress grew up in Calgary, Alberta, a shy kid obsessed with Dakota Fanning who was too scared to ask to go to the bathroom. “I was really a nervous, hyper-aware-of-everything child,” Meszaros notes. “Then, with my friends, I was always really goofy and would put on weird little personalities.” When I ask her age, she demurs. “I don’t know if the world is ready to know. I’m scared…I play young.” She laughs.

Geena Meszaros as Lisbeth in The Body.

It has been revealed that even over Zoom, it’s obvious from her mix of humor, plaintiveness, and clear self-possession why she was cast as Lisbeth. (“I think I’ve embraced the weird a little bit more outwardly,” she says of her own growth since her teenage years.) She almost decided to be a painter instead of an actress. On her Art by Geena Instagram account, she shares self-portraits and thoughtfully bizarre scenes from real life. (In one, her mom’s Italian greyhound gnaws on a Barbie doll.) While filming The Body, she painted a portrait of herself as a skull with lipstick on. “That was a representation of how I felt while I was filming. I was kind of dead, a little bit ill, but having a great time.”.

According to recent reports, the eyebrows both isolate Lisbeth and imbue her with a sort of strange power. (The show’s makeup artists got the look by bleaching them every two weeks. “I was sure I was going to lose my eyebrows, but then when I dyed them back at the end, they were actually so much fuller than they used to be,” Meszaros reports.) By the end of season one, she has the dance team girls in a spiritual chokehold, weaponizing their Catholic guilt against them. But this is no straightforward revenge arc; she is complicated but also deeply cruel, deftly sussing out weakness.

According to recent reports, the show’s rapidly growing audience, needless to say, has had its takes—and Meszaros has seen some of the discourse. That Lisbeth comes from a lower-class background, that she has faced more than her fair share of religious trauma at the hands of her mother, that she is essentially the head of her household after the death of her father, don’t totally seem to justify her behavior in the court of online public opinion.

Yet Meszaros has also recognized an vital truth about contemporary cultural criticism by way of fandom. “There’s a lot of people that cannot separate the character from the actor, which is fascinating to me,” she notes. “I’m like, ‘Yeah, she does some bad things, but she’s not real. Don’t worry. She’s not out there in the world.’” Still, she loves seeing what people come up with in their analysis. “A lot of people think she’s drugging her mom. I’m like, ‘No, that’s not a thing.’ But I do enjoy all the crazy theories anyway. It’s fun, and I’m just happy that people are debating things and that it left them with questions that they’re having fun putting together.”.

Industry observers note that meszaros points to one moment that she herself found tough to take: “That one scene in episode five with Maddie [Shirley Chen], I struggled with that as much as people watching did,” she states, referencing the exorcism of Maddie’s “demon of gluttony”—her eating disorder—which Lisbeth has manipulated her into thinking is a sin. “But I still had that empathy for Lisbeth. I think I had to [in order] to play her, and I do think she’s just gone through so much that you can’t really expect her to be a perfect human being.”.

According to recent reports, “It’s not her most redeemable scene, but I try and tell myself that people like Maddie might be really triggering to Lisbeth because [Lisbeth] used to be really devout, and I think she sees a version of herself that she is still grappling with,” Meszaros continues. “Her mom speaks to her in the way that she’s speaking to Maddie, and it all just comes out in a desperate moment… trauma gets passed down through generations, and I think it can get passed through friendships, too.”.

Recent findings suggest that meszaros thinks back on her own childhood experiences. “Growing up, I actually used to sort of befriend people who bullied me. I would make myself small if I knew somebody was a threat to me,” she indicates. “The way that Lisbeth gets power is by observing the girls and molding herself into them. I really feel like she mimics people…she’s making herself not a threat in such an extreme way. It’s gaining trust, I think. It’s kind of the flip of [my experience] almost, where she starts out small, and then she slowly makes herself bigger.”.

Sources indicate that throughout her season-long quest for belonging, Lisbeth also repeatedly reminds us she’s just a teenage girl finding her way. In one viral scene, she enjoys a particular queer rite of passage: googling “girls kissing” on the internet. (As my lesbian roommate put it, that’s one step before taking an “am I gay?” quiz.) When I ask if Meszaros thinks Lisbeth is on the queer spectrum, she giggles. “I mean, I think everyone is on a queer spectrum.” On the show or in the world? “In the world.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I think she’s definitely curious,” she says. “Her little hookup with Tyler didn’t seem all that buzzy.”.

In a recent development, if the show is renewed for a second season—which seems likely—she’d like to see “what relationship Lisbeth will have with sex. Is it going to be a power thing? Is it going to soften her? I don’t know. But yeah, she could totally be somewhere on the spectrum.”.

As The Body continues to enjoy its run as the number one show on Netflix, Meszaros is looking forward to actually having a minute to process the success of the show, and her increased visibility. “This role truly was a dream role, and now I have to figure out what my next dream role is going to be,” she notes. “I am really excited to just go back and spend time with family and be normal for a little bit.” She also plans to hang out on her sister’s “massive plot of land in the middle of nowhere” this winter: “I think it’d be nice to just go and hibernate. Maybe turn off my phone for a while.”.

The Best Frozen Lasagna, According to Our Taste Test

📅 18 Feb 2010 | ⏱️ 3 min read (658 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bonappetit

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Frozen lasagna is a meal for when you just don’t have it in you.
  • For this taste test, we sampled nine varieties of store-bought meat lasagna, cooking each from frozen and concealing the brand names from our tasters.
  • After grumbling our way through several contenders and questioning mankind’s ability to produce a decent supermarket lasagna, Trader Giotto’s Family Style Meat Lasagna restored our faith with a hearty meat sauce and genuinely tasty noodles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Frozen lasagna is a meal for when you just don’t have it in you. For when you need the comfort of pasta, cheese, and sauce, but you’re not prepared to spend hours boiling, sautéing, and layering. And that’s okay. A great frozen lasagna might not hold a candle to BA’s Best Lasagna, but at the very least it should hold together, with distinct layers, plenty of sauce, gooey cheese, and bouncy pasta.

For this taste test, we sampled nine varieties of store-bought meat lasagna, cooking each from frozen and concealing the brand names from our tasters. Three stood out: Trader Joe’s tasted the closest to homemade, Marie Callender’s was a solid backup, and Rao’s was our favorite for a single serving.

After grumbling our way through several contenders and questioning mankind’s ability to produce a decent supermarket lasagna, Trader Giotto’s Family Style Meat Lasagna restored our faith with a hearty meat sauce and genuinely tasty noodles.

Recent findings suggest that why it won us over: Trader Joe’s frozen lasagna had a homemade vibe. There were distinct layers of pasta, cheese, and meaty sauce. The cheeses—ricotta, mozzarella, Romano, and Parmesan—each pulled their weight. And the noodles had a fresh bounce. “There’s a whole tomato!” exclaimed senior editor Kelsey Jane Youngman upon finding a chunk of diced tomato in her sample. Other tasters complimented the bright aromatics—fennel was prominent, backed up by oregano and basil. The evenly distributed ground beef and pork were the cherry on top.

Trader Giotto’s Family-Style Meat Lasagna, 32-oz.

More great frozen foods at Trader Joe’s →.

Industry observers note that big Lasagna would have you believe you’ll always want to cook a frozen lasagna for a crowd, but sometimes it’s about you and you alone. The 9-oz. Rao’s Made for Home Meat Lasagna is just enough for a single serving—and it doesn’t sacrifice flavor.

Why it won us over: Our tasters were excited to report that Rao’s delivered on structure. While other lasagnas were soupy, floppy, or otherwise unbalanced, Rao’s stayed intact, layer on top of layer, as we ate. It had sturdy (but not tough) noodles, a tomato sauce that was full of umami, and herbal accents that didn’t overpower. Some tasters noted a robust beefy flavor; others were more focused on the garlic and onion. Everyone went in for a second bite.

Rao’s Made-for-Home Meat Lasagna, 9-oz.

Maybe you don’t live by a Trader Joe’s—our condolences—and Rao’s proves elusive. You still deserve a serviceable frozen lasagna. Marie Callender’s Lasagna With Meat Sauce offers a sweet and tangy tomato sauce punctuated by well-seasoned meat and noodles that hold their shape.

According to recent reports, why it won us over: This contender avoided many of the pitfalls other brands fell into. It had a solid tomato sauce that was just slightly sweet and tangy, and the meat—both beef and sausage—was flavorful and varied enough in size to give each bite some dynamism. The pasta sheets were springy, not gummy. And while it wasn’t drowning in dairy, there was enough cottage cheese and mozzarella to make itself known.

Marie Callender’s Lasagna With Meat Sauce, 10.5-oz.

Sources indicate that we cooked each lasagna from frozen according to its package instructions. While most contenders offered both oven and microwave directions, we stuck with the oven. Tasters sampled each lasagna without knowing which brand they were trying, evaluating each for flavor, texture, and structural integrity. Although Giovanni Rana’s Meat Lasagna is sold refrigerated, we froze it before baking, following the brand’s instructions for cooking from frozen.

It has been revealed that the best frozen lasagna should deliver on the fundamentals of structure, flavor, and texture—a tall order for many of our contenders. That meant distinct layers; sheets of pasta that were bouncy, not flimsy; tomato sauce with concentrated flavor and enough body to cling to the pasta; meat that stood out instead of getting lost; and cheese—or many cheeses—that added milky flavor and melty cohesion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My holidays were split between regions growing up. We spent Thanksgiving at my dad’s side, and Christmas with my mom’s. With my mom’s Alabama and Texas roots and my dad's Missouri and Kansas roots, that meant that Christmas dinner was a Southern affair and Thanksgiving was a Midwestern feast. Both holiday spreads had a fair amount of overlap of dishes (casseroles galore), but I have to say: A classic Midwest Thanksgiving has a special place in my heart.

According to recent reports, what makes a Midwest Thanksgiving, you may ask? All of the classics are present, plus a few surprising favorites that, in my house, no holiday is complete without. We think beyond the turkey, sometimes skip mashed potatoes for a cheesy casserole, and have to be careful not to fill up on all the rolls (butter and honey better be on the table). Ready to celebrate Midwest-style? Here are some recipes that your holiday won’t be complete without:.

Recent findings suggest that made with canned pineapple, pistachio pudding, and Cool Whip, this retro crowd-pleasing dessert “salad” will take you straight back to the ’70s with just one bite. It’s the perfect recipe to throw together if you don’t have a ton of time, but you need to take something to that potluck or family gathering.

Industry observers note that thanksgiving is equally about food and football, so this tailgate-inspired stuffing is a no-brainer. Filled with beer cheese sauce and topped with crispy bacon, this twist on the classic holiday side is so irresistible, it’ll be gone long before halftime of that first Thanksgiving Day game.

Pepper Jelly & Cream Cheese Bites.

It takes less than than 5 minutes to pour some pepper jelly over cream cheese and place some crackers around. These bites are slightly more elevated without many more steps. It’s for those that want to feel like they are putting some effort into their appetizer without it being difficult or time-consuming.

Sources indicate that don't be fooled by the name—the only thing deathly about this casserole is how absolutely delicious it is. This cheesy, creamy casserole is a staple at every holiday in my Kansas home, and Thanksgiving is no exception. Yes, we often have mashed potatoes too.

For this recipe, we ditched canned cream of mushroom soup and went for fresh instead. It's not how my mom makes it, but trust me—by sautéing mushrooms with sliced onion in butter, you're building a base with some serious depth of flavor. Cook the mushrooms enough that they get a little caramelized, and you'll really be good to go.

Get the Green Bean Casserole recipe.

No matter the holiday, one thing is for sure: Deviled eggs will be making an appearance. Variations are always welcome (looking at you, harissa deviled eggs), but if grandpa is going to have a happy Thanksgiving, then this classic recipe better be present.

Get the Classic Deviled Eggs recipe.

Sources indicate that strawberry pretzel tart, AKA strawberry pretzel salad, might sound a little strange, but trust us—it strikes the perfect balance of whimsical and classic, sweet and salty. The pretzel crust proves to be an ideal complement to the rich cream cheese layer and the sweet strawberries with their Jell-O glaze.

Turkey usually rules the roost at Thanksgiving, but it's not the only centerpiece present at many Midwestern holiday tables. Depending on how many family members are coming, my family has been known to prepare a turkey and a ham—it's the best of both worlds!

Industry observers note that we’re certainly not opposed to roasted Brussels sprouts, but we also love giving them the traditional Thanksgiving treatment—plenty of butter, cream, and cheese. This method upgrades even the most humble vegetables while still allowing them to be the star of the show.

According to recent reports, this sweet party dip is the perfect way to add that little extra something to your fruit spread, but your dipping options don't stop there! With just 5 minutes of prep, this is the easiest dessert that any party will be thankful for. Plus, you can easily make it ahead and travel with it, making it an ideal potluck recipe.

Sources indicate that these Thanksgiving potato skins are piled high with leftovers, but they’re so good, they just might deserve a place in your holiday spread. The hollowed-out potatoes are an excellent vessel for extra-creamy mashed potatoes, stuffing, turkey, and dollops of cranberry sauce.

Essentially, this is chicken Alfredo, but with a few extra decadent add-ins, like cream cheese, garlic, and punchy spices like nutmeg and black pepper. When you’re craving the classic but have to serve a crowd, this is the recipe you should make.

It has been revealed that A cheese ball is peak party appetizer nostalgia, and these cheese ball bites are here to put a new, shareable twist on the classic. They’re so simple to make, only require a handful of ingredients, and are super versatile based on what you have on hand.

It has been revealed that I'll clarify that when I say stuffing, I'm actually referring to dressing. Traditional stuffing should be stuffed inside the turkey and cooked in there, but in my family, we've always called it stuffing. By cooking your stuffing in a baking dish, you get crunchy, buttery pieces of bread on top and soft, bread pudding-esque pieces underneath.

Industry observers note that what’s the best kind of potato? A loaded baked potato, of course. With this in mind, we combined the two superstar spuds into one glorious dish. Sweet Potato Casserole With Marshmallows.

Most sweet potato casseroles have only marshmallows or pecans. Don't even think about making this mistake. Topping with a pecan streusel and then marshmallows helps this Thanksgiving casserole stand out above all the rest.

If you’re not into creamy, melty macaroni and cheese with a wildly satisfying cheese-pull, then you might want to find another mac recipe. Sorry, but this slow-cooker macaroni and cheese is just too darn dreamy.

The finished casserole won't be quite as decadent, but it will still be delicious.

Whisk 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, ¼ tsp. baking powder, and 1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour in a large bowl. Add 2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces, and rub in with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy). Add 10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea size). Make a well in the center and pour in ¼ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute. Knead dough in bowl just to bring together (some dry bits may remain).

Turn dough out onto a lightly dusted surface and sprinkle with all-purpose flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again. Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting dough with more flour as needed to prevent sticking. Pat into a ½"-thick disk and wrap tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.

Sources indicate that do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

In a recent development, when dough is almost done chilling, cut 1 medium head of savoy cabbage (1¾–2¼ lb.) in half and cut out triangular core at bottom; discard. Separate leaves and tear into pieces about the size of your palm. Transfer about half to a large bowl and set aside.

According to recent reports, melt 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 medium white or yellow onion, thinly sliced, and season generously with kosher salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and starting to turn translucent, about 5 minutes. Add remaining 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter and ¾ tsp. cumin seeds (if using) and cook until butter is melted. Add remaining cabbage leaves and cook, stirring occasionally, until onion is translucent and lightly browned and cabbage is wilted, 18–22 minutes. Transfer to a large plate or a small baking sheet; chill in fridge or freezer until cool.

Place a rack in bottom third of oven; preheat to 400°. Whisk 2 garlic cloves, finely grated, ⅓ cup heavy cream, 2 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a measuring glass to combine. Pour cream mixture over reserved raw cabbage leaves and toss with your hands to coat. Add 5 oz. Gruyère or sharp cheddar, coarsely grated, and toss again to combine.

Sources indicate that unwrap dough and roll out on a lightly floured sheet of parchment paper to a 13–14" round (some dough will extend beyond the parchment). Transfer on parchment paper to a baking sheet.

Spread cooked cabbage mixture over dough, leaving about a 1½" border around edges. Fold dough up and over filling, folding and tucking as needed to make a rustic border. Pile raw cabbage mixture on top of cooked cabbage mixture to make a dramatic heap. (It will look ridiculously high at first but will cook down when it bakes.).

Bake galette 25 minutes. Rotate baking sheet front to back, reduce heat to 375°, and bake until cabbage and crust are deep golden brown, 25–35 minutes. (If cabbage seems to be browning too much, reduce heat to 350° toward the end.) Let galette cool on baking sheet at least 1 hour and up to 4 hours before serving.

Do Ahead: Sautéed cabbage can be made 1 day ahead. Transfer to an airtight container and chill. Tightly wrap undressed raw cabbage in plastic and chill.
