#100421. How to Make Whipped Cream Perfectly, Every Time

📅 27 Jul 2017 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1408 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Bonappetit ↗ Open Full Page

How to Make Whipped Cream Perfectly, Every Time

📅 27 Jul 2017 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1408 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bonappetit

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that if you love a low-effort, high-reward kitchen assignment, learning how to make whipped cream is a walk in the clouds.
  • In whipped cream, and in life, the key challenge is knowing when to stop.
  • To make whipped cream at home, all you need is cold heavy cream, a large bowl, and a whisk.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you love a low-effort, high-reward kitchen assignment, learning how to make whipped cream is a walk in the clouds. The only ingredients are time and heavy cream. You can use an electric mixer, a whisk, or a mason jar and strong-armed devotion.

In whipped cream, and in life, the key challenge is knowing when to stop. Desserts like Strawberry Eton Mess or Triple Chocolate Mousse Cake fare best with silky, unsweetened, soft-peaked whip. Others, like this show-stopping Berries and Cream Mille-Feuille, gain structure from sturdier peaks.

To make whipped cream at home, all you need is cold heavy cream, a large bowl, and a whisk. You can also use a handheld mixer or a mason jar and some elbow grease (more on that later).

If you’re opting for a bowl-and-whisk combo, choose your tools wisely. Cream roughly doubles in volume as you whip it, so use a bowl with three to four times the capacity of your liquid. A large balloon whisk, rather than a narrow sauce whisk, helps incorporate plenty of air into the cream.

It has been revealed that be strategic in the dairy aisle too. Heavy cream and heavy whipping cream contain at least 36% milk fat and can be used interchangeably. Skip anything labeled simply “whipping cream”—or, heaven forbid, “light cream”—which contains less fat and won’t hold its loft as well.

According to recent reports, for a basic batch, start with 1 cup cold heavy cream, which makes about 2 cups whipped cream. For lightly sweetened whipped cream, add 1 Tbsp. powdered sugar; for vanilla whipped cream, add ½ tsp. vanilla extract or paste.

With your equipment and ingredients in hand, there are only five steps and infinite possibilities.

Sources indicate that because whipped cream is usually eaten with or as dessert, you might not need to sweeten it at all. To keep flavors balanced, we tend to serve whipped cream au naturel with Bourbon Caramel Apple Pie or Diner-Style Rice Pudding.

But there are no hard-and-fast rules. Maybe you love sweetened whipped cream, or you’re serving it with something less sugary—like, say, a bowl of tart blackberries and torn mint leaves.

According to recent reports, for lightly sweetened whipped cream, start with about 1 Tbsp. sugar per cup of cream. Powdered sugar dissolves easily and contains a little stabilizer (usually cornstarch), which can lend the whipped cream some extra holding power. Some cooks prefer the cleaner flavor of granulated sugar, which takes a little longer to dissolve. Either way, add the sugar before you start whipping.

If you’re gazing at a bowl of fluffy, ethereal whip and thinking, “Could I make this even more enchanting?” the answer is yes. There are two primary ways to make flavored whipped cream: infuse or stir.

Kitchen professionals and advance planners tend to cold-infuse. Combine your cream with flavorings like rice (for a creamy Horchata) or bourbon (to take a classic pumpkin pie over the top), then store it in the fridge anywhere from three hours to overnight. Strain out any solids before whipping.

You can also add simple flavorings, like vanilla extract, a small splash of liqueur, cocoa, ground spices, citrus zest, or coffee syrup, before you start whipping. For heavier or chunky additions, such as toasted nuts or chopped chocolate, use a rubber spatula to gently fold them in once the cream is whipped.

Peaks are the shape your whipped cream takes when you pull the whisk out of the bowl and hold it upright like the Statue of Liberty’s torch.

Sources indicate that soft peaks are cloudlike and slump over when you lift the whisk. Stiff peaks stand upright and hold their shape. Somewhere in between are medium peaks, which have enough structure to hold a shape while remaining soft and supple.

Most Bon Appétit recipes, such as these Mix-and-Match Fools, involve whipping cream to soft peaks. That velvety texture is our go-to when we’re dolloping whipped cream atop pecan pie.

According to recent reports, but we aren’t always such softies. Medium peaks help this Ginger-Raspberry Icebox Cake keep its shape. And old-fashioned chocolate mousse involves whipping batches of cream into stiff and soft peaks: The former is folded into the chocolate mixture for structure, while the softer stuff tops the dessert.

There’s more than one way to whip.

It has been revealed that by hand: Our preferred method, whipping cream by hand requires the most time and effort, but it also gives you optimal control over its final texture. Even if you use a mixer to get your whipped cream started, switching to a whisk for the final few moments makes it easier to stop exactly where you want.

It has been revealed that in a Mason jar: No whisk? No mixer? No problem. To make whipped cream with your bare hands, put a container with a tight-fitting lid, large mason jar, or leak-proof cocktail shaker into the freezer for five minutes. Get the heavy cream very cold and make sure you have ample headspace in your vessel of choice. About one cup of liquid in a four-cup container is a good amount.

Secure the lid and shake it like you mean it. For the creamiest results, a consistently assertive pace is better than intermittent spurts of brute force. When the liquid stops sloshing and starts feeling and sounding heavier, open the lid and take a peek. If it looks underwhipped, close it back up and keep shaking.

According to recent reports, good news for meal preppers: You can make whipped cream hours in advance. Err on the side of underwhipping it during your prep. Store the lightly whipped cream, covered, in the fridge for up to four hours before serving, then give it a few energetic whisks to bring back its bounce right before you dollop it onto dessert.

You can also freeze whipped cream (no, seriously). It takes a bit of effort, though. Line a baking sheet with parchment, then pipe or scoop spoonfuls of whipped cream onto it. Freeze until the whipped cream nuggets are solid, then peel them off the parchment and store them in an airtight bag in the freezer for one to two months. When you’re ready to serve, let them thaw at room temperature for about 15 minutes.

Instant vanilla pudding is the key to luscious, long-lasting whipped cream.

Need it to hold up longer? Instant vanilla pudding mix is one of BA’s favorite shortcuts for stabilized whipped cream. For every cup of heavy cream, add 1 Tbsp. instant vanilla pudding mix (call it pastry cream powder if anyone gives you sass) and 2 tsp. powdered sugar, then whip as usual. The modified starch in the pudding mix absorbs excess moisture and helps prevent the cream from separating, keeping it fluffy for up to 24 hours.

It has been revealed that for something tangier, sour cream adds both flavor and body. Our Pecan Cream Pie whisks ¼ cup sour cream into 1 cup heavy cream; the sour cream cuts the richness while helping the topping hold its shape.

According to recent reports, in any case, your dinner party guests don’t have to sit quietly as you furiously whisk their dessert topping to order. Prep work never tasted so sweet.

Recent findings suggest that if your whip isn’t coming together quite right, don’t fret. Simple solutions abound.

This is probably a temperature concern. Cold cream whips more readily and holds onto the air you’re incorporating more effectively, so it comes together faster—and stays fluffy longer. Pop the bowl, whisk, and cream back into the freezer for five minutes, or into the fridge for up to 30. Once everything is cold, resume whisking.

Another possible culprit is the fat content of your cream. Opt for heavy whipping cream or heavy cream over half-and-half or other heavy cream substitutes.

Industry observers note that if the cream is just a little too stiff or starting to look grainy, add a splash of chilled heavy cream and slowly whisk it in. Add more, a little at a time, until the texture smooths out.

Keep a close eye on it: If you whisk for too long, you’ll end up with a bowl of butter.

Editor’s note: This story was originally published in 2017 by Julia Black. It has been substantially updated with fresh reporting and additional advice from the Bon Appétit archives, including contributions by Amiel Stanek, Christina Chaey, Rochelle Bilow, and Elyssa Goldberg.

Tech Report: “Do You Like It? Would You Wear It? Would You Buy It?”—An Oral History of Marc by Marc Jacobs

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4018 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that in the 2000s, Marc Jacobs was the high-low king of fashion.
  • Behind Marc by Marc was a small team encouraged to follow its instincts, with creative direction by legendary stylist and photographer Venetia Scott, who had been consulting on the main line since 1997.
  • According to recent reports, and, oh, the stores.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in the 2000s, Marc Jacobs was the high-low king of fashion. A decade after he propelled grunge onto the runway with his landmark collection for Perry Ellis, he was the first creative director at Louis Vuitton, and LVMH owned a majority share of his business. Meanwhile, he was selling $2 condoms in matchbooks alongside wares in every category: rarefied lace-trimmed cocktail dresses for the well-heeled, shrunken denim military jackets for downtown girls, and of course, those ubiquitously irreverent tchotchkes on Bleecker Street for everyone in between. Ineffable cool across all price points was the name of the game, especially with the launch of Marc by Marc Jacobs in 2001, which loomed large over the booming contemporary market of the era. It was so Kirsten Dunst. It was so Alexa Chung. And at the same time it was so me circa my first trip to NYC with a five-dollar lipstick pen and not much else in a branded shopping bag.

Behind Marc by Marc was a small team encouraged to follow its instincts, with creative direction by legendary stylist and photographer Venetia Scott, who had been consulting on the main line since 1997. Together, they trawled vintage shops and film costume warehouses for inspiration. But, perhaps most of all, there was Robert Duffy, the shrewd fashion executive who was Jacobs’ co-founder and longtime consigliere, tasked with turning the designer’s whimsical runway impulses into dollars and cents. They were the Saint Laurent and Pierre Bergé of a upcoming generation, and together they built a manufacturer that was both creative and commercially viable. Introducing Marc by Marc Jacobs was a perfect example of their dualities coming together to produce harmonious results.

According to recent reports, and, oh, the stores. Jacobs’s shops helped transform a once sleepy stretch of the West Village into a destination, with six outposts within walking distance of each other. Among them was the Marc by Marc Jacobs accessories store, the pièce de résistance for tourists and broke fashion kids alike. Whether it was your first trip to Upcoming York or your tenth, you lined up on Bleecker. Tote bags came stamped with the most iconic run-on sentence in fashion history: Jacobs by Marc Jacobs for Marc by Marc Jacobs in Collaboration with Marc Jacobs for Marc by Marc Jacobs. With a simple tongue-twister, Jacobs let us all in on the joke.

Marc by Marc Jacobs was folded into Marc Jacobs in 2015, but it lives on as a moment of accessible cool that can’t be replicated. For those who worked on it, its magic was in the freedom they were given to create. Twenty-five years after it was first introduced, we spoke with members of its creative team about the vintage hunts, the last-minute fittings, and how they were able to recreate the downtown cool around them for the runway.

It has been revealed that in a serendipitous turn of events, Vogue learned that there are plans underway by to revive the Marc by Marc Jacobs label, sometime next year. While details are currently under wraps, this is the place for updates on the beloved brand that had an outsize imprint on fashion in the early aughts.

Lauren (the Marc by Marc fit model), Frederic Tremblay, and designer Susanne Deeken.

Backstage at the London show held at Claridge’s.

Venetia Scott began working with Marc Jacobs on the main collection in 1997. By the time Marc by Marc was taking shape, she had become a central creative collaborator and operated as the creative director on a day-to-day basis with the team.

Industry observers note that venetia Scott, Creative Director (2001-2015)Joe McKenna had been [styling] the Marc Jacobs runway. He suggested that I would be good to take it over, and Nian [Fish] from KCD also thought so. I had just had my daughter about three weeks before, and had gone down to Cornwall. And then my agent rang and said, “Will you go and meet Marc Jacobs and Robert Duffy?” They ended up coming to London, and then that was it. I started that September. When I was assembling my team, I brought Alister Mackie to style men’s. Frederic Tremblay and Aude Tabet were already on the team. Fred was focused on the army aesthetic and denim. Susanne Deeken came in to do summer dresses. Irene Chung did the shoes.

We needed accessories for the show. I knew Katie Hillier from London, and she had been doing necklaces and stuff for Luella’s shows. So I got her to come out to make stuff, strings and beads. Eventually we’d put a small run in the Marc by Marc shop, and then later, it grew into bags.

Alister Mackie, Menswear Consultant (2003-2014)I started on the Marc Jacobs main line around 2001, when they showed men and women together. In spring 2003, we started putting men into the Marc by Marc show. Venetia would set the narrative. At the first meeting, she would have spoken to Marc, and this story of who these kids were would be laid out by Venetia. We would then have to go off and find a boy that was relevant to that. This was really driven by character, which made it unusual, and it made it a lot of fun.

Venetia ScottThere was not really a strategy behind a lot of it. It sort of evolved as it went along. [Co-founder] Robert Duffy was very much like, “Let Marc do what he needs to do, and he will do it.” We never hit our deadlines. I remember Marc saying, “It’s great, we do what we want to do, and it seems like people like it.” I think we were lucky to be able to work in that vacuum without a lot of people dictating what the needs were of the line.

Frederic Tremblay, Senior Design Director (1999-2008)LVMH was seeing the contemporary market brewing. Our price point was a fraction of the main collection, but we took the essence of what Marc was. There was this big opportunity for department stores, who were also telling us, “We’ll give you tons of square footage because this is what we’re seeing as the next thing, but there’s nobody there.” Co-op was happening at Barneys, so we were one of the first big brands.

Backstage at the spring 2006 Marc by Marc Jacobs show.

Industry observers note that venetia ScottMarc was the author of the collection, and so we would have conversations, decide where we were going with it, and then I would work doing the research on fabrics or prints. And then I would go to Paris or to New York, and take him the research that I had done. Marc by Marc was a little group of us, and it was much more like a collaboration.

Camille Bidault Waddington, stylist (2000-2014)Venetia was styling the Marc Jacobs show and was working on the Marc by Marc collection through the season. I was coming for the last two weeks to style the show with her and the team. I was doing looks, but she had the final word. Sometimes it was a fight, but a gentle one. Marc was obviously coming to see us, also to have a breather in the middle of the sophisticated [main collection] prep. We were the kids.

It has been revealed that frederic TremblayMarc would review the collection ahead of the show and suggest pieces we were missing. It was always a great little thing that maybe when we were in the moment, we weren’t necessarily thinking about it, but he would come out and be like, "You know, you need this now." And we were looking at it, we were like, “Yep!”.

Senior design director Frederic Tremblay and Venetia Scott trying on clothes during a research trip in London.

Venetia ScottWe’d go to L.A. for the Rose Bowl Flea and the costume houses, or we’d go to Paris, Antwerp… We’d choose a different place every season. Our thing was always, as a group, “Do you like it? Would you wear it? Would you buy it?”.

It has been revealed that camille Bidault-WaddingtonAt the beginning, we were customizing stuff to accessorize the looks, and invented crazy bits and bobs with Katie Hillier, or used things from markets and punk shops. It was very, very free.

According to recent reports, frederic TremblayWe amassed these amazing vintage pieces, and then we had a model coming in to try on pretty much everything. We started doing a bit of a look with the vintage, and that was our starting point. Those amazing costume rental places are truly magical. You’ve got to see Home Depot-size warehouses where you have to go on those industrial ladders, and there’s three, four rows of clothes, rows and rows. I think we just let our gut tell us where to go in the aisles.

Aude Tabet, Design Director and Director of Product Design, Little Marc Jacobs and Marc by Marc Jacobs Swimwear (1999-2015)We reworked prints, color, and artwork based on the vintage pieces we’d found, either internally or using a print studio. I still go by the Marc by Marc color palette we developed. It’s ingrained.

Backstage at the fall 2005 Marc by Marc Jacobs fashion show.

Venetia ScottIn the beginning, it wasn’t an idea to do a cheaper line. It was, let’s make some things that we all want. Marc’s always liked that high and low mishmash of things. Marc and Sofia Coppola were good friends, and other people around him would do this good mix of wearing the bouclé jacket with a silk shirt, with a pair of jeans, with a pair of flats. So that was natural.

What was great was building this gang of cool girls. One might be in a jumpsuit, one might be in jeans and a T-shirt, one girl’s in a summer dress, but they all look like the same gang.

Camille Bidault-WaddingtonThe point was to represent what cool girls would wear. Models at the time had supercool style, and we were inspired by them, from Kirsten Owen to Angela Lindvall and Tasha Tilberg. They were super-stylish, and we wanted to capture the Latest York streets too—the musicians and the It girls.

It has been revealed that alister MackieSometimes it’s quite hard to fit the men into a women’s story, but it was a fun challenge to make it believable that these girls and boys were together. Fall 2007 (above) was these sorts of winter college kids who were also really grungy. It was very much that character that we kept going back to.

According to recent reports, camille Bidault-WaddingtonSince I’m French, sometimes I thought we were a bit much, but I was then going downstairs with Alister Mackie, who was styling the boys, and actually noticed people in New York were pretty daring. So that was the kick to go back up and add a hat here or a triple sock there.

Recent findings suggest that alister Mackie[Marc Jacobs HQ on] Spring Street was like the kingdom, and everyone was always there. There was a whole floor of ladies sewing, like a factory, so loud and intense. The whole thing was vibrating. Military coats were getting made up to the last minute, all this food arriving, and all these shoes in the corridors.

Irene Chung, who did the shoes, would fly from Italy with batches. Then she’d fly back and get more because Marc wanted to see all the options, and everything had to be just so perfect. It was this very theatrical experience to be part of.

In a recent development, aude TabetOur first show was for spring 2001, but our first fall show (above) was my favorite: Dark denim, the coolest girls, slightly English styling, and very Bohemian. It felt almost like the American version of Katharine Hamnett [the English designer known for her mix of tailoring and a vintage-inspired look that was revolutionary at the time].

Camille Bidault-WaddingtonThe music was very experimental, indie, and daring. Frédéric Sanchez was coming up with upcoming bands or weird choirs or film soundtracks. And we were blasting them. Some journalists got annoyed, but it was very fun.

Sources indicate that for fall 2007, the brand presented its collection at London Fashion Week. Here, behind-the-scenes shots from the show, held at Claridge’s Hotel.

Another backstage shot from the Marc by Marc Jacobs fall 2007 collection.

Marc by Marc Jacobs’ legacy lives on in some of its most ubiquitous products, like the Moonboots and the Souris mouse flats, first launched in 2002 and soon a cult favorite that would live on for decades and have recently found a newly introduced life with a new wave of whimsy enthusiasts.

Hillary Duff seen wearing the Marc by Marc Jacobs signature mouse slipper in 2008.

In a recent development, venetia ScottThe original mouse shoe is a pointy one, which was done for the Marc Jacobs collection around 1998 with a [bow] that potentially looked like whiskers. And so Marc called it the mouse shoe. The more literal mousey thing with whiskers is what it later became.

Tote bags emblazoned with “Jacobs by Marc Jacobs for Marc by Marc Jacobs in Collaboration with Marc Jacobs for Marc by Marc Jacobs” became another signifier of Jacobs’s tongue-in-cheek approach to the brand.

Frederic TremblayThat was Marc realizing the repetition of his name and the number of lines was getting a little silly. It was just something, kind of, funny, you know? Marc has that ironic thing. He just came up with that, him and Robert.

Amid the designer denim boom of the 2000s bolstered by the likes of Diesel, True Religion, and 7 For All Mankind, Marc by Marc denim launched alongside the first collection for spring 2001. The following February, Vogue reported that its creased jeans were flying off retailers’ shelves.

Aude TabetWe did a creased pair of jeans for our denim launch. The jeans were creased as if they had been folded always on the side, like this forever. That was what we called our “San Francisco SF” wash. It was a mid-pale blue with a gray cast, developed in L.A. And we did all those drummer boy jackets with it.

The main collection and Marc by Marc shared a photographic and visual language, shaped by photographer Juergen Teller and Scott, and later Mackie.

Venetia ScottRight at the beginning, when I worked on Marc Jacobs, Juergen and I were together. Juergen would come over and stay in Latest York. The conversation came up that there wasn’t any budget, but “maybe when you go back to London, you could photograph Kim Gordon?” And “Venetia, you could take a dress, and you could go to the Shepherd’s Bush Empire, where she’s performing, and she’ll put the dress on,” and “Juergen, you take some pictures of her up on stage or backstage in the dress.” It was just a conversation that didn’t ever really go through lots of tiers of people to be able to get any permission. We just did it.

Early on, there wasn’t any money for those ads. It was just something that we wanted to do. And then it carried on like that, really, as a conversation of who it could be, who’d be a good person this time. Sometimes Juergen would come up with an idea [or see a upcoming actress], like, “Who is she? Oh, I think the girl who’s just been in that film.” And it would be Samantha Morton. Or Dakota Fanning, who I’d just seen in a film when she was tiny, and thought she was the most amazing thing. “Maybe we could shoot her?” We’d just say, “Yes, let’s do that.”.

Often Juergen would go off and do the Marc Jacobs campaigns on his own. And then Marc by Marc, we usually used who we thought had been the best girls in the show, or who seemed the most right for it. It’d be maybe three or four of those girls, and they’d often do the shoots. It was more models that had been used on the runway.

Alister MackieSometimes I went with Juergen on trips, and they were phenomenal. We were going to Milan, to Venice, to upstate New York, and we went on these very, very lo-fi trips with him and the models.

It has been revealed that in 2010, the New York Times called Jacobs’ West Village retail footprint a monopoly. In other cities, from L.A. to Lisbon, the stores felt like anchors of cool, devoted to a high-low mix that epitomized fashion at the time. Under Duffy’s leadership, Jacobs’s world opened up to the masses via the accessible “junk” operation: an ever-changing assortment of novelties for people who couldn’t afford the clothes.

Sources indicate that aude TabetI moved to the West Village in ’92. The Mercer Street store was the nucleus—this crazy, beautiful, minimal location in that former garage. You would just want to be there, sit in a corner, and people-watch. Before Marc was there, Bleecker was very sleepy. There were a couple of antique stores. Then Marc went there and ended up opening a few stores, and that changed all of Bleecker. Every place where Marc went and opened up retail, everyone followed.

Sources indicate that frederic TremblayA lot of the ideas for the trinkets came from Fiorucci [the popular 1970s brand and store known for carrying an eclectic mix of high-end clothes alongside novelty trinkets and small gifts and where Jacobs worked as a teenager]. Marc would often talk to us about that reference. He would go to the Fiorucci store by Bloomingdale’s, and they had a lot of that stuff too—products that were satellite to the main brand of clothing or accessories, those little things that anyone could afford.

Industry observers note that alister MackieWhat we made was really for the show, but Robert and the merchandising team made all these products, which were really fun and successful, and then they put them together in the stores. Somehow, one elevated the other, and one made the other more fun. The people who worked in the shop represented Marc as much as we did, or the people in the office and the models. Everybody had the same kind of positivity and welcoming spirit.

Camille Bidault-WaddingtonIt was very, very cool to sit on the bench at Balthazar and see so many people walking by, wearing Marc by Marc. It was very cool because it was a collection on its own, not a variation of the other line. It was deep, not just a commercial version.

It has been revealed that venetia ScottYou’ve got your little haul of a tote, and this and that and the other, all for under 50 bucks. It was a fun idea, a bit like Biba in the ’70s, where you could get a T-shirt for very little money or buy a poster to stick up in your room at school. But I think the cheap products that were Marc by Marc, in the long run, probably didn’t do us any good. What we were doing was something very different. We were doing boots that you could sit on the pavement, kick about, and have fun in. They’d get better and better. It wasn’t meant to be a cheap version of something expensive. It was meant to be what it was.

According to recent reports, alister MackieMarc threw these huge parties, and it was very early on for that kind of branding, having these great parties and everybody wanting to be part of it. Chloë Sevigny and all these fabulous women were around—all that was part of the magic of the brand.

In a recent development, marc’s parties were the talk of the town, and he took it to the extreme. In Venice, he was a pigeon. And then the Arabian Nights, he was camel toe. He took it to this other kind of level of surrealism.

Those parties were also part of the myth of the brand, because everybody was going. It wasn’t exclusive. Everyone in town wanted to be there. That was part of the expansionist generosity of Robert and Marc at that time.

Heidi Bivens, Justin Theroux and Marc Jacobs’ then-boyfriend Lorenzo Martone front row at the spring 2010 Marc by Marc Jacobs show.

Rachel Zoe, Lorenzo Martone and Brad Goreski at the spring 2009 Marc by Marc Jacobs show.

Marc by Marc Jacobs, spring 2009.

Recent findings suggest that by 2013, the contemporary market that Marc by Marc Jacobs had helped define was crowded with competitors, including Alexander Wang, 3.1 Phillip Lim, and Rag & Bone. That year, as Katie Hillier and Luella Bartley were appointed to lead its next chapter, Duffy acknowledged that the line had lost some momentum. “The competition has become too great,” he told WWD. “We rested on our laurels, and it hurt us.”.

It has been revealed that venetia ScottWhen it got really substantial, then we were asked to do things like, “Oh, somebody’s got, you know, this brand’s got some [legging trousers called] treggings.” And we’d all think, “Well, we don’t want to do treggings.” And I think that was, for me, that was sort of maybe where it lost its way a little bit, and the identity was not as clear as it had been in the beginning. Before, when we were just doing what we wanted to do, that seemed to sell well.

Frederic TremblayAround 2006, 2007, Topshop became a thing. Zara and H&M started to get more momentum. They took a lot of our market. We started feeling like, okay, we really need to offer something different. We weren’t the only ones in contemporary to feel that. We couldn’t really compete.

Recent findings suggest that venetia ScottOther brands could do that army jacket in a second, and have it out in the shop at the same time that we would. So I think all that contributed to it probably not having the sales that it had once had. I think it was time for a refresh. Katie and Luella came in, and I continued with them to consult on the process. They set up a London studio, and we all worked together on the show and the styling.

In May 2013, Katie Hillier was named creative director of Marc by Marc Jacobs, with Luella Bartley joining as women’s ready-to-wear design director. Their debut for fall 2014 brought an edgier, London-inspired vision to the brand, but it didn’t last long. In March 2015, it was revealed that Marc by Marc Jacobs would be absorbed into Marc Jacobs, bringing contemporary and luxury products together under one name. “We believed that fashion could exist at lots of different prices,” Jacobs told WWD at the time.

Beginning with spring 2016, the consolidated label incorporated lower-priced pieces alongside its runway collection, a strategy Jacobs later acknowledged “didn’t really work.” Given the extensive retail footprint of the Marc by Marc Jacobs line, rather than the main line, much of its exposure was lost to customers, leaving space for other brands to replace it.

Venetia ScottThe [pieces] have a character that you don’t find if you go to a high street store. They still are around, what is it, 20 years later? They still look great.

They had all these extra details that you discovered as you wore them. You’d have a piping on the inside of the cuff, which was some little candy cane stripe. They were quite honest clothes, I think.

Aude TabetI wear those pieces from time to time, and I love the emotional connection. I love how disruptive it was. In a good way, positive, disruptive.

Industry observers note that frederic TremblayI’ve been doing mentoring at SCAD, and there are students who will have picked something in a vintage store that’s Marc by Marc. They kind of know what it is, but they don’t really have the whole story about it. They don’t know about the real impact it had when it was made. So it’s always fun when one of the students wears one of those pieces, and I can tell them a little bit about it.

Breaking: This week: Lame duck kicks off with Hegseth impeachment effort

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thomas Massie of Kentucky told CQ Roll Call in late October that the Hegseth impeachment resolution would come up in the first week of the post-election lame duck session.
  • The lame-duck session of Congress kicks off this week as the House is expected to consider a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth while the Senate seeks to advance a bipartisan deal on permitting reform.
  • Last week’s midterm elections saw Democrats claim sizable majorities in both the House and Senate in the new Congress, and among the immediate questions is whether the demoralized GOP will face attendance woes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Departing GOP Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky told CQ Roll Call in late October that the Hegseth impeachment resolution would come up in the first week of the post-election lame duck session. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

The lame-duck session of Congress kicks off this week as the House is expected to consider a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth while the Senate seeks to advance a bipartisan deal on permitting reform.

Last week’s midterm elections saw Democrats claim sizable majorities in both the House and Senate in the new Congress, and among the immediate questions is whether the demoralized GOP will face attendance woes.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the expected next speaker of the House, mentioned Sunday that he would support the Hegseth impeachment.

According to recent reports, “I'm a hard 'yes' on the Hegseth resolution,” Jeffries noted on ABC’s “This Week.” “The so-called secretary of Defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. Pete Hegseth has got to go.”.

Sources indicate that departing Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., told CQ Roll Call in late October that the Hegseth impeachment resolution would come up in the first week of the post-election lame duck session.

Sources indicate that it’s also orientation week on Capitol Hill for upcoming members of Congress. House orientation got underway Sunday.

The Senate, meanwhile, looks to take up a bipartisan permitting bill that has the backing of President Donald Trump.

“This Landmark Permitting Reform Legislation will codify our America First Energy Agenda, and ensure that we can build Pipelines, Mines, and Power Plants faster than ever before, lowering Energy Costs for American Families, and creating High Paying American Jobs,” Trump posted on Truth Social.

Senate negotiators over the weekend released text of an amendment seeking to address remaining concerns.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m grateful for the input throughout this process from Senate and House colleagues, environmental and labor organizations, and Tribal leaders. Our manager’s amendment improves [the bill] and addresses the thoughtful feedback we have received,” Senate Environment and Public Works ranking Democrat Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island remarked in a statement. “Now it’s time to pass this bill so we can lower costs, juice the clean energy economy, build substantial things again in America, reduce pollution, and create tons of new well-paying union jobs.”.

Beyond the permitting bill, the Senate Republican majority may seek to use its remaining time trying to confirm more of Trump’s nominations before the control of the floor agenda passes to the Democrats.

In a recent development, "We've got the farm bill, the NDAA, and we have that third reconciliation bill that we need to get across the finish line, and there are so many things that we need to get done and buttoned up," including nominations, departing Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., mentioned in a weekend Fox News interview. Blackburn, one of the Republicans who had success at the ballot box, is now governor-elect of Tennessee. But it's an open question how long lawmakers will want to stick around.

There’s also the matter of an imminent fight over funding the government and laying the groundwork for the newly introduced Congress. Republican leadership elections are scheduled for Tuesday, while Democratic leadership elections are expected in December. Democratic senators-elect are due on Capitol Hill Monday and Tuesday, according to the office of Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y. Schumer is widely expected to be the majority leader in 2027.

There have been some calls for Senate Republicans to delay their elections, though current Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota has been widely expected to remain as the Republican leader.

“One of the things I learned in business and the Army is that after a failure, you have to start with honesty, transparency, and accountability,” Sen. Dave McCormick, R-Pa., mentioned in a Sunday night statement. “As I’ve shared with Leader Thune, I don’t believe we should move to leadership elections until we have digested and debated the lessons of the midterms and how to move forward.”.

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., has also been circulating a letter calling for a delay, and he has argued the election should not be held, in part, because the makeup of the Senate Republican Conference is not yet final. Senate races are still not called in Alaska and Mississippi.

Recent findings suggest that absent this week will be Sen. Christopher S. Murphy, D-Conn., who recently had a stroke.

It has been revealed that “The doctors are very encouraged by the progress I’ve made so far. In order to take my recovery seriously and get back to work on the quickest timeline possible, I will be spending several weeks at a rehabilitation center after being discharged from the hospital today,” Murphy said in a Friday statement.

But leftovers reach their most perfect form in a sandwich, where all the components play off one other for a few transcendent bites.

These Thanksgiving sandwiches make the most of what you’ve got, whether that’s a few slices of turkey or enough stuffing and cranberry sauce for an encore. Go all in with a gooey melt, load a pita with spiced turkey and crunchy vegetables, or give turkey the chicken salad treatment. Recent findings suggest that these leftover turkey sliders have a lot going on, in the best way. Picture: melty cheese, cranberry mayo, garlic butter, turkey, mashed potatoes, and more where that came from.

Give your Thanksgiving leftovers the club treatment by layering turkey and cranberry sauce with crisp bacon and lettuce. And don’t forget that middle slide of bread. We’re not animals, after all.

Need a break from heavy Thanksgiving fare but still have turkey to use up? Shred it, toss it with butter-bloomed spices, and tuck it into a pita with a bright, tangy slaw.

Recent findings suggest that in this play on a turkey club, the middle slice of bread gets swapped out for leftover stuffing fried in bacon fat. (We repeat: stuffing fried in bacon fat.).

Industry observers note that turkey and cranberry sauce already have a salty-sweet thing going on. Why not play that up by swapping plain bread for custardy French toast?

Sometimes it’s best to keep a leftover turkey sandwich simple. Turkey, cranberry sauce, cheese, and fresh sage, pressed until golden, give you all the flavors of Thanksgiving in four ingredients (plus bread).

Though the recipe calls for cooked chicken, you guessed it—you can swap in leftover turkey seamlessly. The apple and fennel both provide lots of crunch and freshness.

Another chicken banger that works beautifully with leftover turkey. Boosted with red curry paste, tangy from Greek yogurt, this mixture is as good stuffed into lettuce cups as it is tucked between sliced bread.

This recipe sticks close to the classic turkey club, with one simple twist: a punchy, verdant herb mayo that comes together in seconds in the blender.

Sources indicate that roast turkey, tangy sauerkraut, melty Swiss cheese, and a tangy sauce? Heaven. Bonus points if the rye bread you use is studded with caraway seeds.

#100414. The Carnivore Diet Is Peak Protein Extremism. How Healthy Is It Really?

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1371 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gq ↗ Open Full Page

The Carnivore Diet Is Peak Protein Extremism. How Healthy Is It Really?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1371 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, you know your obsession with protein has gone too far when you’re waiting in line at Erewhon for a raw meat smoothie.
  • In a recent development, eating raw organs is a step too far, but maybe you’ve heard about the benefits of the carnivore diet and you’re curious.
  • Maybe plant-based eating leaves you gassy and unsatisfied.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you know your obsession with protein has gone too far when you’re waiting in line at Erewhon for a raw meat smoothie. The speciality drink was created by Paul Saladino, who regularly preaches the benefits of following an animal-based diet. If you look inside the blender, you’ll find kefir, beef organs (like liver, heart, kidney, and spleen from Saldino’s Heart & Soil line), and “immunomilk,” which is freeze-dried cow’s colostrum. Yum. Saladino may be an outlier, but he certainly isn’t the only person pushing a meat-heavy diet. Brian Johnson, aka the “liver king,” follows an extreme ancestral carnivore diet, eating a pound of raw liver a day.

In a recent development, eating raw organs is a step too far, but maybe you’ve heard about the benefits of the carnivore diet and you’re curious. According to a 2026 study published in Nutrients, the number of posts about the carnivore diet on Instagram is in the millions—and they didn’t even look at TikTok. Interest surrounding the carnivore diet has shown no signs of slowing down.

Maybe plant-based eating leaves you gassy and unsatisfied. You can’t help that you like wings. Before you take vegetables off the table completely, it’s crucial to know what the carnivore diet is and how it impacts health, both short-term and long-term. As experts explain here, it’s not all bad. But there are some important risks to be aware of.

Industry observers note that the aforementioned Nutrients study on the carnivore diet explains that there isn’t one standard definition of what the carnivore diet actually is, but generally speaking, it’s a diet where you only eat minimally processed animal foods, including organ meats, fish, seafood, eggs, animal fats, and full-fat dairy. Plant-based foods are eliminated entirely.

Recent findings suggest that while eliminating foods like fruits, vegetables, and whole grains is extreme, Pouria Sefidmooye Azar, PhD, RD, a registered dietitian and assistant professor at the University of Central Arkansas, says the carnivore diet isn’t all bad. He says that short term, many people lose weight eating this way.

In a recent development, “Protein is more satiating than carbs and fats, so people following the carnivore diet often stay full for a longer amount of time, which means they reduce their caloric intake,” he says. Logically, it makes sense. If you’re eating foods like beef, chicken, and salmon, you’ll be less likely to dig into the pantry for snacks than if you ate a bowl of noodles.

It has been revealed that dr. Azar claims it’s crucial not to conflate weight loss with getting healthier. He says that by eliminating plants, you’re going to miss out on a lot of important nutrients the body needs. You can probably guess the substantial one. Yep, fiber. “"If you’re cutting out every plant food, you're not getting fiber or phytonutrients, which are protective compounds found only in plants,” says Chris Vogliano, PhD, RD, a registered dietitian and global food systems expert.

Sources indicate that while you might not suffer any consequences of this immediately, both dietitians say that continuing to eat this way can mess up your digestion. You need fiber for good poops, plain and simple. Dr. Azar states that we also need fiber to feed the healthy gut bacteria in the microbiome. This is crucial for supporting mental health, immune health, and minimizing the risk of chronic diseases and cancers.

Recent findings suggest that dr. Azar specifically calls out the connection between a high-meat, low-fiber diet and the risk of colorectal cancer. For example, a 2015 Oncology Reviews study shows a connection between red meat consumption and colorectal cancer risk, while a 2026 European Journal of Cancer study called low fiber consumption a major risk factor for colorectal cancer.

Sources indicate that considering that men are at increased risk for heart disease (the number one cause of death in the U.S.), it’s important to know how the carnivore diet can impact your cardiovascular health. Spoiler alert: It’s not good. “I would not recommend the carnivore diet as a healthy, long-term eating pattern,” says Sunny Intwala, MD, MBA, preventive cardiologist and the director of Prevention & Wellness at Northwell Health.

Dr. Intwala explains that this is because meat doesn’t just contain protein; it has a lot of saturated fat too. He states that diets centering around red meat increase LDL cholesterol and blood pressure in a few short weeks. This, he says, can contribute to inflammation and plaque buildup that increases the risk of heart attack and stroke.

As someone who studies how the way we eat impacts the planet, Dr. Vogliano points out that the carnivore diet is pretty horrible for the environment. “From a food systems lens, a meat-only diet on a global or even national level would carry massive environmental costs from land, water, and greenhouse gas emissions. This is regardless of whether the meat is conventionally raised, organic, or even regenerative. There’s just not enough land to produce that much meat,” he states.

Okay, we need plants. But what about the Brian Johnsons and Paul Salidinos of the world preaching the benefits of eating raw meat? If you are going to eat meat, are there benefits to eating it raw?

Both dietitians say no, emphasizing that there is no scientific evidence showing that raw meat is more beneficial in any way than eating cooked meat. “Liver is a nutrient-rich food and a great way to get vitamin A, vitamin B12, folate, and iron. But you can get that from cooked liver; you don’t have to eat it raw,” Dr. Vogliano says. In fact, he emphasizes that eating any meat raw increases the risk of foodborne illnesses like Salmonella and E.coli.

According to recent reports, dr. Azar warns against pulling a Rocky and eating raw eggs either. “The protein in raw eggs is between 50 and 60% digestible. But the protein digestibility in cooked eggs is over 90%,” he says. A study from the ‘90s in The Journal of Nutrition backs this up.

It’s worth noting that this isn’t the same for meat. A 2015 study in the same journal found that the cooking time for meat didn’t impact protein digestibility very much. So while you may get the same amount of digestible protein from raw meat as you would cooked meat, your risk of foodborne illness is greater.

Sources indicate that decades of scientific research make it clear that a plant-free diet is not a healthy diet. If you’re a meat lover, you might be wondering just how much meat you can get away with eating without compromising your health.

Dr. Azar’s advice is this: Meat can still be your primary protein source. Just eat some plants along with it. “If you love meat, you can still eat foods like beef and chicken, but you also need to eat fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and nuts and seeds because there are some nutrients you just can’t get from meat,” he claims, adding that only eating meat will lead to nutrient deficiencies.

Dr. Vogliano delivers a dietary message you’ve likely heard many times before: The healthiest diet is a diverse one. “We know from scientific research that the more plant foods our diets consist of, the more insurance we have that we’re getting the nutrients the body needs,” he indicates. Because of this, he advocates for a primarily plant-based diet and only eating meat occasionally.

It has been revealed that different governing bodies have slightly different recommendations when it comes to how much meat you can eat while still maintaining a healthy diet. The American Institute for Cancer Research says to keep red meat under 18 ounces a week, or roughly three portions a week. The American Heart Association doesn’t give a specific serving recommendation for meat, but says to mostly get protein from plants, fish, and seafood.

Recent findings suggest that dr. Azar emphasizes that there isn’t one universal way of eating that works for everyone. One diet may make one person feel energized and leave someone else feeling exhausted. What is vital, he notes, is making sure you’re getting all the nutrients your body needs. And what we know for sure is that you can’t do that by just eating meat.

Gravy-Braised Turkey

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (562 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cooking a whole turkey is a commitment.
  • This recipe will defy everything you have probably done to cook a turkey until now.
  • For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cooking a whole turkey is a commitment. Between the schlepping, trussing, and constant babysitting, it’s a serious investment—and one that doesn’t always pay dividends. For a more laid-back affair, and one that practically guarantees success, might we suggest turkey legs cooked directly in gravy? Yes, in the gravy.

This recipe will defy everything you have probably done to cook a turkey until now. The first key step is searing the whole turkey legs for optimal browning. Now you are ready to create a base for the gravy with all those drippings and toasty bits left in the pot. No need to make a full-on roux either: Just sprinkle in the flour over the melted fat, whisk to combine, and slowly pour in the broth. Once the gravy is done, in goes the turkey and aromatics for braising. The rest is you worrying about something else, because that turkey will cook itself.

For more Thanksgiving recipes, tips, menus, and inspiration, head to our 2026 Thanksgiving Hub.

In a recent development, place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 325°. Season 4 whole turkey legs (thigh and drumstick; about 6½ lb. total), patted dry, all over with kosher salt and freshly ground pepper. Heat 3 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large braiser or Dutch oven over medium-high. Working in 2 batches if needed to avoid overcrowding, arrange turkey legs, skin side down, in pot and cook, undisturbed, rotating pan on burner a few times to ensure even browning, until browned underneath and they easily release from pot, 8–12 minutes. Transfer turkey legs to a rimmed baking sheet, arranging skin side up. (No need to brown other side; turkey will still be raw at this point.).

Sources indicate that add more oil if pot looks dry; arrange 2 large oranges and/or lemons, halved, and 2 heads of garlic, tops trimmed to expose cloves, cut side down in pot and add 3 large shallots, peeled. Cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 2–3 minutes. Transfer each to baking sheet with turkey as they are done (it’s okay if some fall apart slightly).

In a recent development, add 6 Tbsp. (¾ stick) unsalted butter to pot and cook until melted. Sprinkle in ⅓ cup (42 g) all-purpose flour and cook, stirring constantly, until no pockets of dry flour remain, about 1 minute. Gradually pour in 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth, stirring constantly to combine. Bring to a simmer and cook until gravy is just starting to thicken, about 2 minutes. Stir in 3 Tbsp. Worcestershire sauce and season with salt and pepper.

Nestle turkey legs into gravy, skin side up, then tuck oranges, garlic, and shallots around, arranging oranges and garlic cut side up. Add 1 small bunch thyme (about 10 sprigs), tied with kitchen twine, and cover pot tightly with a lid or foil. Braise 2 hours. (If your pot is too small to comfortably fit everything, transfer gravy to a 13x9" baking dish before adding turkey legs and aromatics.) Uncover pot and continue to bake until turkey legs are deeply browned, meat shreds easily off the bone, and gravy has thickened a little, 45–55 minutes.

Let turkey and gravy cool slightly before serving. Transfer to a platter if desired. (If gravy has excess fat on top, skim off with a spoon and discard before serving or spooning over legs on platter.).
