💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in my mind and, I think the minds of many others, Peloton has always been a stationary bike brand.
  • It has been revealed that nevertheless, Peloton actually has been making treadmills since 2018.
  • In a recent development, the upcoming Tread Flex, however, heads in a slightly different direction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in my mind and, I think the minds of many others, Peloton has always been a stationary bike brand. The Bike, after all, was its first product, turning the Peloton name into a catch-all term for at-home cycling that we now hear everywhere, from broadcasts of the Tour de France and Giro d'Italia to television sitcoms. (A running gag online is that Peloton's upscale, soothing video workout content is worlds away from The Office's Dwight Schrute leading a group of stationary riders off an imaginary cliff.).

It has been revealed that nevertheless, Peloton actually has been making treadmills since 2018. The first Tread delivered the same proposition as the Bike: premium hardware that looks good enough to bring out of the basement, as well as access to interactive, instructor-led runs and HIIT classes on a massive, immersive screen. Over the years, Peloton has brought improvements to that first Tread: larger screens, voice controls, AI-informed movement tracking for form analysis and coaching.

In a recent development, the upcoming Tread Flex, however, heads in a slightly different direction. It has a simpler belt, simpler speakers, a smaller screen. It's $1,300 cheaper than the next step up, and $4,500 cheaper (!) than Peloton's slat belt-equipped Tread+ Vision. Its affordability isn't even its main selling point, however, because the Tread Flex has a nifty final trick: it folds up to save space.

In a recent development, could these space and money-saving tactics make the Tread as popular as the Bike? Well, I run nearly every day, and ever since a tester Tread Flex demonstrated up at my door, I've been doing it indoors much more frequently. In my experience, here's what makes Peloton's latest worth considering.

It has been revealed that treadmills tend to have a problem that stationary bikes don't: the nicer they get, the bigger they get. Premium models have larger motors and roomier running platforms. In short, they're heavy. (The Tread+ Vision is a hefty 460 pounds.) The Tread Flex is 170 pounds less, and that's crucial to its ability to fold up, because that feature wouldn't be much of a selling point if it felt like adding a power clean to the end of every run.

In reality, stowing the Tread Flex is quite easy. You just lift up the running deck from the end and push it forward until a hydraulic cylinder locks into place. There's a pin clip to lock it. To drop it down, you push forward on the deck and then on the hydraulic support, then walk it back. At about 45 degrees, the hydraulics take over completely; you can go put on your running shoes while a gentle thump lets you know the deck is back on the ground.

According to recent reports, folding up the Tread Flex drops its area from about 16.5 square feet to half that. (The Tread+ Vision is around 19.25.) Just as importantly, I've discovered, is that lifting the deck brings the machine up onto a set of locking wheels. I've kept mine in a designated corner, but it's so easy to move that it wouldn't be much hassle to wheel it out and lower it for every workout, if your space required it. Get your cardio out of the way, then get your cardio out of the way.

Okay, so folding and moving a treadmill might be a pain if you're using it every day. But I suspect if you're running that often, you're doing some of it outside. I live less than an hour away from the Canadian border, and run on roads and trails five or six times a week all year round. Good layers get you pretty far, and there's a reason why run clubs continue to boom while SoulCycle-adjacent Mile High Run Club closed all its studios this year.

According to recent reports, treadmills are for something else. They're for a warm-up prior to lifting, or for bootcamp-style HIIT workouts that combine sprinting intervals with weight intervals. The prioritization value of time spent doing these doesn't seem to align with the space investment a treadmill requires if you don't have a pool house or big garage. (I have a sun porch-slash-mudroom where I keep firewood and ski boots in the winter and a napping couch in the summer.).

This is how, I think, the Tread Flex makes the ultimate proposition as the ideal home treadmill. A treadmill doesn't replace a usual running routine; it adds to it. On Monday I do my usual seven miles down the road and back on the river trails; on Tuesday I let Andy Speer kick my ass with sprints and kickstand deadlifts. (And, sure, when it's -10° and blowing in late January, I might run inside, now that I have the option.).

None of the above would matter as much if it came at the cost of quality. I've run on hotel treadmills that sound like your grandma's washing machine and feel similar to how they look, i.e., stomping around on hollow plastic. The Tread Flex may not have the cushioned slat belt the Tread+ Vision has, but it's definitely not that.

Sources indicate that what it does have is a spec that's right in line with top-notch treadmills. Its max speed is 12.5 miles per hour (a 4:48 mile, in runner's units), a 12.5% max incline grade (but no decline), and a 20-inch by 59-inch running surface that, though not cushioned, feels good to run on. The swiveling screen is nice and big at 21.5 inches, with HD resolution and a touchscreen interface. I particularly like how adjusting speed and incline is done with rolling knobs, which feel much better—and more natural—to engage with than buttons when you're gasping at threshold pace.

On top of that is Peloton's interactive experience: You can take live classes where you can pit yourself against others and get kudos from the instructor. The pre-recorded catalogue includes thousands of classes for yoga, Pilates, and meditation, in addition to strength and the running, cycling, and rowing the manufacturer makes machines for.

According to recent reports, the Tread Flex also provides personalized training plans, smart pacing guidance based on where you're at, automatically adjusting incline for classes, and of course leaderboards and an entire ecosystem of badges and achievements to earn, if you're into all that. For $50 per year, that is.

Oh, and did I mention it's a good-looking machine? It's sleek; an attractive, soft-edged Z with a minimal screen instead of a board of colorful buttons. Nobody's throwing around the word "console" to describe this thing. That's good; home gym setups deserve different consideration than gym rigs. If images of Crunch Fitness flash through your head every time you glance into the corner, something has missed the mark.

It has been revealed that where Peloton's Tread Vision treadmills are clearly high-end, the Tread Flex toes the line against mainstream consumer models. Its features match up with some of the most popular machines, and its price, while at the higher end of the spectrum, does too. But the Tread Flex gets there with more style, and with Peloton's huge ecosystem of live and archived class content.

Recent findings suggest that so, if we're looking at other treadmills out there, my quick answer is yes. The Tread Flex is the utilitarian Peloton Treadmill, but it's still a Peloton treadmill.

How you answer this question really requires asking yourself a series of other questions first. What do you want a treadmill for? How much do you want to invest? Do you want access to fitness classes—especially ones other than running—and are you okay with the $50/month subscription fee?

Recent findings suggest that form factor and access to classes and content are non-negotiables. The Tread Flex might be Peloton's new entry-level treadmill, but it's far from a simple running machine. Flex refers to that nifty fold-up feature, but also to this treadmill's ability to integrate into an exercise program that also includes strength training, HIIT workouts, yoga, and on and on.

It has been revealed that as a runner who prefers to log miles outside whenever possible, I was encouraged by how much I enjoyed running on the Tread Flex. The classes are fun, and Peloton's instructors are real pros, but even in Just Run mode, the Tread Flex proved responsive and comfy. It's getting dark around 4:30 PM these days, and my daylight windows for running on the well-used roads around me have narrowed like a Death Star trash compactor. It's nice to know I can snag seven miles after sundown if need be.

Well, if you aren't limited by space or cash, the Tread Vision and Tread+ Vision get you bigger screens, AI-enabled running form feedback and coaching, and a more cushioned, broader running area. If you just prefer running or walking on a treadmill to doing it outside, investing more heavily in a treadmill is worth considering (though the Tread Flex will still be great).

The Tread Flex's real competition is the NordicTrack Commercial 1750, which you'll find recommended on just about every treadmill buying guide on the internet. The machines are similar in function and specs, but there are some differences. The NordicTrack's running surface is two inches wider and one inch longer; it has a slightly more powerful motor; it can decline to -3% grade; its belt is slightly cushioned; it has a built-in fan; and NordicTrack's class and entertainment platform, iFit, is cheaper at $39 a month.

In comparison, the Tread Flex takes up slightly less space, has a higher max speed (12.5 mph over 12 mph), a steeper incline (12.5% over 12%), and a larger screen (21.5 inches over 16 inches). The rolling knobs to adjust speed and incline are nicer to use. My partner, who designs commercial and residential interior spaces, agrees with me that the Tread Flex is a better-looking machine.

Sources indicate that list price for the Tread Flex is $300 cheaper, but the NordicTrack seems to be perpetually on sale. So it might come down to looks, that 3% decline, or what class platform you'd like to buy into.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the last few years, lymphatic drainage has gone from an IYKYK technique to an all-out wellness obsession. Oft described as the “Cinderella of medicine,” the lymphatic system is responsible for collecting excess fluid from tissues, transporting immune cells, and carrying certain waste products away from cells. This system, however, doesn’t work on its own to get the lymph flowing. Lymphatic drainage is a more manual practice; you can try your hand at deep breathing or dry brushing, but few things offer offer as excellent lifting benefits as the best gua sha tools.

In a recent development, “The literal gua sha Mandarin translation is ‘to scrape sand,’” explains Lin Chen, cofounder of Pink Moon. “Gua sha tools have been used as a unique approach for holistic healing in China for 4,000 years. It has been traditionally used over the body to help aid in the movement of qi (which is energy flow), increase circulation, and release tension.” That mentioned, Chen continues saying that research shows that the practice was first used in the Paleolithic Ages, dating back to the Ming dynasty in China.

It has been revealed that “Gua sha is an effective technique for enhancing the face’s natural contours and reducing puffiness through lymphatic drainage,” explains Charlotte Yau, traditional Chinese medicine expert and founder of Muihood. The upward-scraping technique is meant to stimulate blood circulation, encourage collagen production, and reduce the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles, adds Yau. “While it doesn’t permanently change facial structure, it can create a more sculpted look over time by reducing fluid retention and enhancing skin elasticity.”.

Of course, when you’re shopping for your first one, the options can feel endless. “When choosing a gua sha, I think the material, shape and weight all matter,” notes Ava Lee, K-beauty expert and founder of byAVA. Ceramic and stone feel smooth and give you a gentler massage, while stainless steel stays cold, which helps with puffiness. “Ultimately, it’s about finding something that feels good to use and that you’ll reach for every day,” Lee says. Ahead, the best gua sha tools to add to your routine from Lanshin, Wildling, and more.

What are the benefits of incorporating a gua sha tool?

Industry observers note that “While its popularity in the US and Europe is largely tied to its ability to ‘sculpt’ the face, its healing capabilities extend far deeper!” Chen instructs, explaining that the gua sha is used for lymphatic drainage, addressing stagnant energy, promoting blood flow, soothing headaches, reducing inflammation, shortening acute illnesses like colds and flus, as well as releasing tension from head to toe. Daily gua sha practice has the ability to enhance not only your appearance (think reduced puffiness, contoured facial muscles, and improved skin elasticity), but your mental and emotional well-being. Just think of how calming it is to glide a roller or stone across your skin. What’s more, Chen says you can expect results instantly, though you should continue to use daily.

“Both steel and stone gua sha tools have their benefits, and the choice depends on personal preference and skin needs,” explains Chinese Medicine expert and founder of Muihood, Charlotte Yau.

In a recent development, curious how to use a gua sha? So you’re ready to try the restorative practice at home. Aside from the tool you choose, a proper technique is key to reap the anticipated benefits. Always start with clean skin, then prep with an emollient face oil or balm. “You also want to apply an oil that’s silky and doesn’t absorb right away or you might tug your skin,” Chen advises. With skin ready, keep the stone as flat and close to the skin as possible, gliding at a 15 degree angle to avoid any unnecessary friction. According to Chen, you’ll want to avoid passing over active breakouts, even if you just target the chest and neck to increase circulation and decrease inflammation. Perform slow strokes, in upward and outward motions, for about three to five passes, and you’re all set.

It has been revealed that yau recommends starting from the neck and moving upward to the jawline, cheeks, and forehead to promote proper lymphatic drainage. “For best results, use your gua sha three to five times per week. Daily use can enhance benefits, but overuse may cause sensitivity,” she says. Homemade Dog Treats With Applesauce and Cheese

📅 28 Apr 2025 | ⏱️ 3 min read (653 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that these homemade dog treats are crunchy, cheesy, and enthusiastically approved by my little curmudgeon.
  • Whole wheat flour provides structure plus fiber, while brown rice flour helps the biscuits bake up crisp.
  • I like Gouda for its aroma—it drives my dog into a frenzy—but sharp cheddar or Swiss will work too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that these homemade dog treats are crunchy, cheesy, and enthusiastically approved by my little curmudgeon. The recipe began with a dog biscuit from the December 2005 issue of Gourmet. While the generous quantities of butter, brown sugar, and salt in the original gave me pause, I used it as inspiration for these cracker-like treats, swapping in ingredients I’d discussed with my vet and knew my pup would love. I’m hoping yours will too.

Whole wheat flour provides structure plus fiber, while brown rice flour helps the biscuits bake up crisp. Old-fashioned rolled oats give the treats a pleasantly nubby texture. The dough comes together with an egg and unsweetened applesauce. Be sure to check the applesauce label for added sweeteners, especially xylitol, which is toxic to dogs.

I like Gouda for its aroma—it drives my dog into a frenzy—but sharp cheddar or Swiss will work too. Curly parsley and mint lend a fresh herbal note and mild breath freshening, but the real secret ingredient is a little anise seed. Sometimes called “dog nip,” anise has a scent that some dogs find irresistible. Fennel seed makes a fine substitute.

Can I make these homemade dog treats with pumpkin?

Absolutely. For a fall-inspired variation, use plain canned pumpkin purée instead of applesauce, oat flour instead of brown rice flour, sage instead of parsley, and sharp cheddar for the cheese. (Honestly, add a little salt and you could serve these on a Thanksgiving charcuterie board.) For your dog, though, skip the salt and be sure to use 100% pumpkin purée, not pumpkin pie filling, which contains added sugar and spices.

IF USING A FOOD PROCESSOR: Pulse 1 cup (113 g) whole wheat flour, ¾ cup (96 g) brown rice flour, ¾ cup (76 g) old-fashioned rolled oats, 1 tsp. baking powder, ½ tsp. ground fennel seed, and ½ tsp. ground ginger in a food processor to combine (about three 1-second pulses). Add 1 cup (4 oz.) shredded Gouda or sharp cheddar, ¼ cup curly parsley leaves and tender stems, packed, and ¼ cup mint leaves, packed, and pulse to incorporate (two to three 1-second pulses). Add ¾ cup unsweetened applesauce and 1 large egg, and pulse until a coarse dough forms, about 20 seconds. (You can roll out dough right away, but it’s much easier to work with it if you let it chill first.) Divide dough into two rounds and wrap each in plastic, or place in separate resealable containers, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes and up to 24 hours.

Industry observers note that IF NOT USING A FOOD PROCESSOR: Whisk 1 cup (113 g) whole wheat flour, ¾ cup (96 g) brown rice flour, ¾ cup (76 g) old-fashioned rolled oats, 1 tsp. baking powder, ½ tsp. ground fennel seed, and ½ tsp. ground ginger in a large bowl to combine. Add 1 cup (4 oz.) shredded Gouda or sharp cheddar and toss to coat the cheese. Finely chop ¼ cup curly parsley leaves and tender stems, packed and ¼ cup mint leaves, packed; set aside. Create a well in center of flour mixture. Add ¾ cup unsweetened applesauce and 1 large egg to well and mix with a wooden spoon, bringing flour into center until combined. Fold in chopped herbs. (You can roll out dough right away, but it’s much easier to work with it if you let it chill first.) Divide dough into two rounds and wrap each in plastic, or place in separate resealable containers, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes and up to 24 hours.

Bake dog treats, rotating baking sheets front to back and top to bottom halfway through, until cheese has bubbled up and treats have darkened slightly, 12–15 minutes.

Do Ahead: Dog treats can be baked, cooled, and stored at room temperature in an airtight container for up to 3 weeks or frozen for 3 months.

Massie moves to force Hegseth impeachment vote

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Thomas Massie, R-Ky., took to the House floor Monday to unveil a resolution that would impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and a vote on the issue could occur by Wednesday.
  • A draft resolution that Massie read aloud on the House floor on Monday accused Hegseth of eight violations of law or the Constitution, including that he violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution in his prosecution of the Iran war and acted illegally in military campaigns in Venezuela, Yemen, the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., conducts a news conference outside the Capitol on Monday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Sources indicate that rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., took to the House floor Monday to unveil a resolution that would impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and a vote on the issue could occur by Wednesday.

A draft resolution that Massie read aloud on the House floor on Monday accused Hegseth of eight violations of law or the Constitution, including that he violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution in his prosecution of the Iran war and acted illegally in military campaigns in Venezuela, Yemen, the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean.

Massie's resolution also charges Hegseth with disregarding protection of civilians in wartime and suppressing the free speech of a U.S. senator.

Massie unveiled his intention to file the resolution as a matter of the privileges of the House.

Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., will now have to rule as to whether the resolution constitutes a proper question of the privileges of the House. There is precedent from prior instances when impeachment was found to be valid as it relates to the House’s constitutionally granted powers.

It has been revealed that he must schedule a vote to occur within two legislative days. Assuming that the speaker rules that Massie's resolution is privileged, the House could vote on the resolution itself, or on a motion to table it or refer it to committee.

It has been revealed that if the House were to impeach Hegseth under this process, it would mark a historical anomaly. According to the Congressional Research Service, recent attempts to impeach an official as a matter of the privileges of the House have not resulted in approval of the resolution. Further, the measure alleges that Hegseth continued the war despite the House and Senate adopting in June a concurrent war powers resolution calling for the withdrawal of U.S. forces from the fight.

The House has only voted twice to impeach a member of the Cabinet. In 1876, Secretary of War William Belknap was impeached over allegations of corruption, and his abrupt resignation likely contributed to his acquittal in the Senate.

Grab a can of pumpkin and some baking staples, mix it up, then pop the bowl in the fridge. The next morning you’ll be rewarded with a lightly sweet, mousse-like treat that’s actually good for you—don’t forget to finish each bowl with a dollop of yogurt for a pumpkin-pie-with-whipped-cream vibe. Using an unsweetened soy or nut milk will keep the pudding more pumpkin-forward than dairy milk (and keeps the recipe vegan, of course), but any milk you have on hand will work here.

20 minutes (plus 8 hours for chilling).

Recent findings suggest that whisk one 15-oz. can pure pumpkin purée, 1½ cups unsweetened milk of choice, 2 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract, ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt, ¼ cup pure maple syrup, and ½ tsp. ground cinnamon or cardamom in a large bowl until smooth. Add 3 Tbsp. chia seeds and whisk to combine. Let sit 10 minutes. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that watch brands’ awareness among consumers is on the rise, and this moves in lockstep with overall positive associations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mixture of high-level customer service, personal experiences, and frictionless shopping has helped watchmakers improve their image and perceived value among consumers this year.

Recent findings suggest that watch brands’ awareness among consumers is on the rise, and this moves in lockstep with overall positive associations. In this scenario, established brands have strengthened their position, while smaller brands have found fertile ground to grow.

Despite pressure from higher gold prices and a strong Swiss franc that has forced watchmakers to raise prices across the board in recent years, respondents still consider watches a good investment, increasingly purchase them as gifts, and remain loyal to their brands of choice even when confronted with price rises.

The recent excitement around resale schemes, limited editions, in-person services, immediate stock availability and exhibitions spotlights an appetite for proximity, access and the human touch, offering opportunities for brands that can support customers across multiple touchpoints and build communities.

In a recent development, at the top of the innovation table, the best performers — Rolex, Cartier, Omega, Patek Philippe, and Tag Heuer — each maintained their position in the 2026 Vogue Business Watch Index, even improving their score. Rolex keeps its crown for overall consumer sentiment, achieving 99% aided awareness, and Tag Heuer boosts its aided awareness score by 2 percentage points. Despite Breitling, in sixth position, improving its overall brand awareness ranking from 72% to 73%, driven by improvements in aided awareness, the gap with Tag Heuer for overall awareness widened to 8 percentage points.

The most striking result of the Index is that 75% of the brands surveyed have seen their awareness score improve, bringing the overall average awareness score up by 1.6 percentage points, which means the public is more aware of the watch category as a whole and readily recognizes brands.

According to recent reports, chopard takes the crown as the top performer by improving its awareness score by 6 percentage points from 62% last year to 68% this year. It is followed by Longines, A. Lange & Söhne, and Vacheron Constantin, which improved by 4 percentage points, and Piaget, Audemars Piguet, IWC, and Movado, which improved their score by 3 percentage points.

Interestingly, this year the top five brands improved their overall awareness (combined aided and unaided awareness) score by 1 percentage point to an average of 90%, while the other 15 surveyed brands registered a higher increase of 1.8 percentage points. This means the challengers are putting more pressure on the top five, but with an average aggregated awareness of 58.4%, the gap is still wide.

The awareness ranking is particularly relevant because it reveals a strong correlation with brand equity, consumer sentiment, and purchase intent, particularly for the top five performers.

According to recent reports, but awareness alone does not translate into purchase intent across the board, as purchase intent far lags awareness. Rolex, the top performer, ranked first across all criteria, has only 38% purchase intent, but in a ranking methodology, becomes the “100%” player to which all other brands are indexed. Across the board, purchase intent is relatively flat vs. last year, with actual purchase intent sitting at 16% on average across all brands. This means that brands with relatively modest purchase intent, such as A. Lange & Söhne at 14%, perform above average when ranked (coming in at 58% in the ranking), given the economic pressures on purchase intent. Yet this methodology does expose just how competitive the landscape is. When we rank purchase intent, A. Lange & Söhne is comparable to IWC, despite the latter enjoying significantly higher brand awareness, with aided awareness sitting 25 percentage points higher. In contrast, brands such as Breitling, Hublot and Tudor display high awareness ranking scores (Breitling 73%, Hublot 66%, and Tudor 49%) but actual purchase intent of just 12% and 13%.

It has been revealed that interestingly, brand loyalty has increased to 64.3% vs 63% last year, as consumers resist the temptation to switch to a more affordable brand even if prices increase, with the 45-64 age group having the strongest resolve. Nevertheless, that same demographic demonstrates a higher propensity to explore discounts and resale options, still showing some price sensitivity.

Industry observers note that in 2025, Vogue Business asked luxury watch consumers about their watch-buying habits for gifting occasions in the Middle East. This year, we extended that question to all markets. The results reveal interesting motives for buying luxury timepieces, as well as how this varies by local culture.

Overall, key occasions include birthdays (34.1%), Valentine’s Day (29.7%) and Christmas (27.6%), as well as weddings and engagements, particularly for Gen Z (30%) and Gen X (31%). Interestingly, the 40% of luxury consumers who spend more on luxury watches (over $5,000 in the last five years) show a higher propensity to buy luxury watches as gifts for others across every occasion.

In a recent development, self-gifting has also become a prevalent trend. China is the leading market for personal birthday buys, at 55%, compared with 32% when buying for others. In the Middle East, self-purchasing for birthdays sits at just 32%. Instead, Eid is the leading self-gifting occasion, at 38% — far outpacing buying for others at 24%. This indicates many shoppers are taking advantage of seasonal deals for their own interests. The self-gifting trend also reveals interesting behavior for romantic occasions: a fifth (20%) of luxury consumers in the UK say they have bought themselves luxury watches as an anniversary present in the last two years — double the percentage of French consumers who’ve done the same (10%). Curiously, the opposite is true for weddings and engagements, where only 10% of UK luxury watch consumers shop for this occasion, but 17% of French consumers do. This highlights how nuanced gifting occasions are by market, and how the hierarchy of milestones and relationships differs across cultures.

For many years, watch brands have pursued partnerships with the automotive industry, but lately this association seems to be influencing the watchmaking business model, which is increasingly leaning toward the car-making industry’s emphasis on service, a greater focus on experiences and integrated resale options.

When it comes to executing the latter, interestingly, it is the youngest, independent brands such as Richard Mille, MB&F, F.P.Journe and Urwerk that have grasped the importance of owning their secondary market, which leads not only to better control over prices and the products’ retained value but also promotes proximity to clients who, in turn, tend to be more loyal to the brand, act as natural ambassadors, and form communities.

According to recent reports, the launch of certified pre-owned schemes has been one of the most significant milestones in the watch industry. While Cartier pioneered the concept in the 1990s, other watch specialists such as Vacheron Constantin and Rolex joined only in the last five years. At the end of October, Audemars Piguet introduced its “Watch Keepers”, its own certified pre-owned program, which will operate as a digital platform enabling sales at a fixed price as well as auctions. It is launching in Europe and Switzerland first before expanding into the United States.

Brand-owned retail platforms allow brands to retain customers who are loyal to the brand but seek more cost-effective options when prices rise. It’s a concern that affects nearly half of all luxury watch consumers, at 47%, with this rising by age as older shoppers say they will shop more for sales and discounts.

Last year’s Vogue Business Watch Index highlighted how brands with low awareness scores were associated with strong purchase intent. This insight is driving brands to purposefully cultivate their niche and strengthen their bond with clients through ad hoc partnerships, without venturing into high-cost, high-visibility collaborations.

Industry observers note that the most interesting success story is that of A. Lange & Söhne because, unlike all other brands surveyed, it is not Swiss but German — and its history, which began in 1845 in Glashütte, stalled between 1945 and 1990, when the brand was relaunched.

Industry observers note that from the start, A. Lange & Söhne has cultivated its difference, expanded organically, and gradually grown its base of collectors and buyers with a laser focus on products and selected partnerships. The brand forged strong links early on with prestigious cultural institutions in Dresden, the capital of Saxony, where Glashütte is located. These include the brand’s support for the Dresden State Art Collections (Staatliche Kunstsammlungen Dresden) and the Semperoper opera house, which have run for over 20 years. As part of these tie-ups, the brand supported the exhibition “Paula Modersohn-Becker and Edvard Munch. The Big Questions of Life” this year. Such partnerships show collectors who visit the brand’s manufacture how the brand is deeply interwoven into the cultural fabric of the area it comes from.

More recently, A. Lange & Söhne has built on that art legacy by partnering with car events such as the Concours d’Elegance in Hampton Court (UK), Como (Italy) and Newport, Rhode Island (US), known as Audrain Newport Concours & Motor Week. At the end of 2025, the brand opened two latest stores, one in London and one in Singapore, while in June this year, it opened its first store in Lisbon.

According to recent reports, other brands following this approach are Jaeger-LeCoultre, with 58% aided awareness, Piaget at 70% awareness, and IWC at 59%. For these brands, criteria such as “its products are a good investment”, “interesting story brand”, and “heritage” seemed to move the needle strongly in consumers’ perceptions.

It has been revealed that these brands have all followed the same restrained and laser-focused blueprint. Boasting an uninterrupted history since its founding in 1833 in Le Sentier, Switzerland, Jaeger-LeCoultre has privileged experiences and exhibitions. At the end of last year, the brand inaugurated its installation “The Dream Shaper” in Shanghai, which showcased over 70 archival pieces and celebrated the brand’s heritage in crafting ladies’ watches. The event was attended by the brand’s ambassadors, including South Korean actor Kim Woo-bin. This year, Jaeger-LeCoultre celebrated its signature Reverso design with a series of dedicated in-store experiences, “Reverso Stories”, as well as some limited-edition pieces presented during Homo Faber in Venice in September.

Piaget has strengthened its commitment to the arts by renewing its partnership with The Andy Warhol Foundation, which led to new limited-edition pieces this year. The brand also sponsors the Prix Solo Art Genève, a prize awarded to the best solo show during Art Genève. Meanwhile, IWC has cultivated its difference by continuing its association with Formula 1 and highlighting the uniqueness of its heritage with the launch of IWC. Curated — since the end of 2025, some IWC watches from the Maison’s museum have been selected for reproduction and sold in limited quantities.

Cartier staged the second part of its brand exhibition in Melbourne, Australia; Panerai unveiled a showcase in its hometown of Florence, while Patek Philippe brought its retrospective exhibition to Milan. The exhibition, which ran from October 2-18, showcased over 500 pieces and attracted 68,000 visitors. Analysts agree that such exhibitions not only boost the brand equity of the firm organizing them, but also increase the general public’s interest in watchmaking.

This year’s most significant trend was the relaunch of milestone designs that ticked most of the boxes that get consumers excited, namely vintage, heritage and limited editions.

One of the most recent examples is Hublot’s Classic Fusion Tributo, which the brand developed with its founder, Carlo Crocco, who also served as the unofficial ambassador for the occasion, marking the first time he has collaborated with Hublot since selling it to LVMH in 2008.

The new watch, launched in October in Milan this year, is an almost identical reproduction of the model that made Hublot famous in 1980. It features a gold case with screws that also serve as hour indices, mounted on a black rubber strap that, thanks to technological advances, is odorless and does not need to be infused with vanilla like the original 1980s version. The launch allowed clients to meet the brand’s founder and hear directly from him how the watch ended up on the wrist of King Constantine II of Greece, who also gifted one to his brother-in-law, King Juan Carlos of Spain, among other illustrious personalities such as Princess Caroline of Monaco, Elton John and Giorgio Armani.

Hublot’s executive team told the press at the launch that Gen Z’s interest in vintage pieces with a small dial prompted them to launch the project three years early, ahead of the model’s 50th anniversary.

Chopard’s relaunch of the original Happy Diamonds watch also marks the celebration of its 50th anniversary. At a party during Latest York Fashion Week hosted by brand ambassador Bella Hadid, Chopard introduced the new Happy Sport Heritage, reproducing the original cushion-shaped, golden case framing an onyx dial over which diamonds float freely, and mounted on a black leather strap. Chopard also seized the opportunity to relaunch the original Happy Sport designed in 1993 by the creative director and co-president Caroline Scheufele. Happy Sport was conceived as an evolution of the original Happy Diamonds watch and marked the first time diamonds were paired with steel.

CEO, Watches of Switzerland Group.

Recent findings suggest that in your latest annual report, client experience is mentioned as a growth pillar. What does it mean?

In a recent development, watches of Switzerland excels in two very different categories: one-time buyers and serial collectors who own hundreds of timepieces. This means we have to offer a variety of services to satisfy the very different demands of these two groups.

Industry observers note that for example, those who only buy one or two watches in their lives may welcome our financing options, as well as the education our salespeople provide to help them buy with confidence something they can treasure and pass on. For dedicated collectors, we focus on providing access to exceptional timepieces and bringing them closer to the brands and the world of watchmaking.

We regularly treat our best clients to manufacturer visits, take them to watch fairs such as Watches and Wonders, and secure exceptional watches. For example, this week, we are inviting them to discover all the timepieces recognized with prestigious GPHG watchmaking awards (Grand Prix d'Horlogerie de Genève), including the independent Rexhep Rexhepi and the gem-set Piaget Sautoir watch.

According to recent reports, watches of Switzerland’s Knightsbridge store. About half of the retailer’s business comes from supply-limited brands such as Rolex and Patek Philippe, and it uses AI to decide what else goes in its windows.

Sources indicate that stock availability is a top priority for clients. What do you do to ensure your stores have the right products?

About half of our business relies on brands such as Rolex and Patek Philippe, which have limited supply and are sold to customers who have waited patiently. But we use artificial intelligence tools to identify trends. For example, when customers browse our watches online, our tool ignores the brand and detects specific watch attributes, such as case size, price point, and strap material; these criteria help us adjust our stock accordingly.

How do you turn digital activity into a commercial opportunity?

Unlike other apparel items, watches can be appreciated even more online, as we can show minute details that are not visible to the naked eye, and we can even show the movement, the beating heart of a timepiece, which is often hidden. We, of course, offer online chats with experts, and one of our points of difference is that we own Hodinkee, the most trusted online watch magazine, with shopping links to our website.

Women are becoming more important for the watch industry; how are you supporting this growth?

In a recent development, our newly introduced store in Glasgow is a good example: the team there is led by a woman, and the salesforce is evenly split 50-50 between men and women. We also have three watchmakers in residence to service timepieces: one man and two women.

It has been revealed that the Vogue Business consumer sentiment ranking assesses brands based on consumers’ opinions and willingness to buy. The criteria analyzed range from basic brand awareness to brand loyalty and purchase intent. Brands are also evaluated on perceived quality, with survey participants answering questions about customer service, in-store experience, design, and sustainability, among others. Respondents have also appraised a brand’s storytelling, role in society, perceived timelessness, digital content, trust, and sense of style.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that at first glance, these homemade cinnamon rolls have all the classics: buttery, golden-brown dough, a gooey cinnamon-and-brown-sugar filling, and a generous swoop of cream cheese frosting. But a couple of smart moves make them especially fluffy, with a tender crumb that stays soft well into the next day (assuming there are any left).

One is tangzhong, a Chinese technique that cooks a small portion of flour and milk into a thick paste before it’s added to the dough. The precooked starch helps the dough hold on to more moisture, resulting in pillowy, supple cinnamon rolls.

It has been revealed that the other is brown butter, which gives the filling a nutty, toasty edge. The tangy cream cheese frosting balances all that richness; add the optional lemon zest for extra brightness.

Can I make these cinnamon rolls the night before?

According to recent reports, yes. You can refrigerate the dough after its first rise or assemble the rolls in their baking pans and refrigerate them before the second rise. Cover tightly with plastic wrap to prevent the dough from drying out. The next day, let the chilled dough sit at room temperature for about an hour before proceeding with the recipe, making sure the shaped rolls have doubled in volume before baking.

Why is my cinnamon roll dough so sticky?

This is a soft, moisture-rich dough, but it should become smooth and elastic as you knead it. For the most consistent results, weigh your flour rather than measuring by volume. Also, make sure the tangzhong has thickened into a paste before adding it to the dough: You should be able to see the tracks of your whisk across the bottom of the saucepan. Avoid adding excessive extra flour, which can make the finished rolls dense.

Can I make these cinnamon rolls without a stand mixer?

Yes, though kneading this soft, enriched dough by hand takes considerable time and effort. Several readers have reported success doing so. If using a stand mixer, keep an eye on the motor during the extended kneading time. If it begins to strain or overheat, stop the machine and finish kneading by hand.

Can I use active dry yeast instead of instant yeast?

Industry observers note that this recipe calls for instant yeast, which can be mixed directly into the dough. Active dry yeast generally requires activation in warm liquid and may affect rising times, so we recommend sticking with instant yeast for the recipe as written. For more information, see our guide to the different types of yeast.

Whisk ¾ cup whole milk and ¼ cup (31 g) all-purpose flour in a medium saucepan until smooth. Place saucepan over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until mixture is thickened and whisk lines are visible on bottom of pan, about 2 minutes. Scrape tangzhong into the bowl of a stand mixer and let cool.

Sources indicate that add 1 large egg, one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.), ⅓ cup (67 g) granulated sugar, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt,  and remaining 1½ cups whole milk to tangzhong and whisk to combine. Add remaining 5½ cups (688 g) all-purpose flour. Fit bowl onto stand mixer; fit mixer with dough hook attachment. Mix on low speed until combined, about 1 minute. Increase speed to medium-low and mix, scraping down sides of bowl occasionally, until dough is smooth and elastic, 18–24 minutes. Pinch off a golf-ball-size piece of dough and stretch between your fingers as thin as possible without breaking. If you can see light through the dough, it’s ready. If not, continue mixing a few more minutes, then try again.

Add ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces, to dough and mix on medium speed until incorporated, about 2 minutes. Continue mixing until dough pulls away cleanly from sides of bowl and is no longer tacky to the touch, 5–7 minutes longer. Remove bowl from mixer and cover with a damp kitchen towel. Let sit in a warm spot until doubled in volume, 60–90 minutes.

In a recent development, while the dough is rising, cook ½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter in a small saucepan over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until butter foams and milk solids turn dark amber, about 4 minutes. Transfer to a heatproof bowl and let cool slightly. Add 1 cup (packed; 200 g) dark brown sugar, 2 Tbsp. ground cinnamon, 2 Tbsp. heavy cream, and ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt to butter and mix to combine.

Butter two 9"-diameter cake pans. Punch down dough and transfer to a lightly floured surface. Stretch dough into a rough rectangle; if dough feels stiff, let sit 5–10 minutes to allow gluten to relax. Arrange dough with short side facing you and roll out to a 24x13" rectangle. Spread filling over dough in an even layer.

Sources indicate that place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 350°. Bake rolls until golden on top and puffed (don’t be alarmed if they rise dramatically in the center), 25–30 minutes.

Meanwhile, using an electric mixer on medium speed or a whisk, beat 4 Tbsp. unsalted butter, room temperature, and 8 oz. cream cheese, room temperature, in a large bowl, scraping down sides of bowl as needed, until combined. Add 1¼ cups (138 g) powdered sugar, 1 Tbsp. heavy cream, 1 tsp. lemon zest (if using), and ¼ tsp. Diamond Crystal or Morton kosher salt and beat until mixture is smooth and sugar is incorporated. Taste and beat in more powdered sugar (up to ¾ cup) if desired. Thin with more cream as needed, a teaspoonful at a time, until frosting is thick but spreadable.

Let cinnamon rolls cool in pan 5 minutes; spread frosting over.

How the ‘blue tsunami’ crested in North Carolina

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1633 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, north Carolina Rep.-elect LaKesha Womack talks to reporters Sunday at the AC Hotel in Washington as she arrives for new member orientation.
  • LaKesha Womack faced towering odds as an underfunded Democrat making her first run for public office in a North Carolina district that Donald Trump carried by 15 points two years ago.
  • According to recent reports, but as early voting surged in mid-October, she sensed she might pull off an upset over Republican Rep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, north Carolina Rep.-elect LaKesha Womack talks to reporters Sunday at the AC Hotel in Washington as she arrives for new member orientation. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

LaKesha Womack faced towering odds as an underfunded Democrat making her first run for public office in a North Carolina district that Donald Trump carried by 15 points two years ago.

According to recent reports, but as early voting surged in mid-October, she sensed she might pull off an upset over Republican Rep. Tim Moore, the influential former speaker of the North Carolina House and a chief architect of the gerrymander that aimed to keep the 14th District safely red.

It has been revealed that “There were a lot of pins and needles,” said Womack, a 49-year-old ordained minister who works at a Charlotte-based nonprofit. After seeing long lines at polling places extend into Election Day, she grew more confident: “People were ready to exercise their voice.”.

Womack – who raised less than $60,000 to Moore’s $2.1 million – eked out a 2-point win in the district, which reaches from the Charlotte suburbs to mountain counties in the west.

Saddled with an unpopular president and broad dissatisfaction with the status quo, Republican incumbents across the nation experienced a midterm drubbing last week. As of Monday evening, House Democrats had netted 42 seats, with more races left to be called. The GOP in North Carolina, a state that Trump carried three times, was among the hardest hit.

Recent findings suggest that democrats have so far flipped five House seats in the Tar Heel State. Besides Womack, the “blue tsunami” also swept in Paul Barringer, a lawyer who founded an outdoor clothing line, and High Point Mayor Cyril Jefferson. And Army veteran Richard Ojeda, who once served in the West Virginia Senate, defeated Rep. Richard Hudson, the chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee.

Sources indicate that democrats also won two races that had been seen as competitive for much of the cycle. Farmer Jamie Ager flipped an open seat in the state’s mountain west, while Rep. Don Davis held on to his Eastern North Carolina district, which Republicans had redrawn in their favor.

Meanwhile, in the state’s hilly northwest corner, 11-term Republican Virginia Foxx, the chairwoman of the powerful Rules Committee, is fighting for her political future: As of Monday afternoon, former journalist Chuck Hubbard led her by 99 votes in the 5th District, though The Associated Press had yet to call the race.

In a recent development, that was also true in the neighboring 10th District, where GOP incumbent Pat Harrigan had a 1-point edge over Democratic physician associate Ashley Bell. Also uncalled were a pair of contests in Eastern North Carolina, where Republican Rep. Greg Murphy clung to a 233-vote edge over Democratic former state Rep. Raymond Smith and GOP Rep. David Rouzer led Democratic social worker Kimberly Hardy by less than a point.

“Nobody could have predicted this,’’ stated David Wilson Brown, who leads the Democratic Party in Gaston County near Charlotte and has lost two bids for the House, including to Foxx in 2020. “It’s a watershed moment.”.

The Democratic rout in the midterm elections was powered by victories in states with latest GOP-favored maps, including Texas, Ohio and Florida.

Industry observers note that but Democrats’ success in North Carolina was especially striking given the steep structural disadvantages the party faced. Since Republicans flipped the state legislature in 2010, and with it control of the redistricting process, no House GOP incumbent had lost a general election in the Tar Heel State until last week.

This year’s  congressional map – the state's sixth in seven election cycles – was engineered by the Republican-led legislature to help the party capture 11 of the state's 14 House seats.

According to recent reports, but the Democratic surge was so big that it easily overpowered the GOP’s built-in edge. Democratic candidates were also lifted by former Gov. Roy Cooper, whose 20-point Senate win provided the underticket with powerful coattails.

“In order for them to gerrymander our state in the way that they did, they were spread very thin,” Brown said, referring to state Republicans. “So they were kind of ripe to be defeated that way.”.

According to recent reports, the repeated rounds of redistricting may have also erased some of the advantages of incumbency, according to Peter L. Francia, a political science professor at East Carolina University. “If you carve up a district every two years, you've taken away some of that [advantage]. And I think that that came back and hurt Republicans in this cycle.”.

Doug Heye, a GOP strategist and a former spokesman for the Republican National Committee, stated redistricting “ticked off a whole lot of voters, and really activated the Democratic base.”.

On the Republican side, voters were “less motivated because they were unexcited about Trump,’’ Heye added.

Republican incumbents accustomed to winning by comfortable margins weren’t prepared for a political environment driven by anger over the war in Iran and angst about the rising cost of living.

Recent findings suggest that “Clearly, a lot of those Republicans didn’t take their elections seriously,” Heye mentioned. “They won last time with 18 points. They weren't on anyone's radar screen, so they didn't think they had to do anything.”.

Womack credits her win to a grassroots campaign centered on economic issues. While her race wasn’t on the national radar – Moore, after all, won by 16 points in 2024 – and her campaign didn’t have money for ads, she was out in the district doing events every day.

Industry observers note that “There are a lot of working families right now who are in the missing middle,” she mentioned in an interview. “They make too much money to get help, but they don't make enough money to get ahead. … Someone who can be working a full-time job, but still doesn’t have enough money to buy groceries or to afford their medications or to have access to health insurance.”.

Sources indicate that womack said her own struggles have shaped her approach to politics. This week, she’s slated to appear in court on a felony charge for allegedly failing to return a rental car in 2019. The incident wound up in one of Moore’s attack ads.

Sources indicate that “There are so many people who [understand] what happens when you're down on your luck and you don't have enough money to make good financial decisions,’’ she said. “Most people don't want those bad decisions to be a definition of their character for the rest of their life.”.

Early in the midterm cycle, Democratic opposition research group American Bridge prepared detailed dossiers on Republican House incumbents in North Carolina.

“Someone like Virginia Foxx, she’s been on the Hill forever,” mentioned Pat Dennis, the group’s president. “She was somebody … who under the radar could be vulnerable. So we started really early.”.

It has been revealed that american Bridge’s political arm spent $340,000 on ads targeting Foxx. One spot featured a man who identified himself as a Trump voter expressing anger at the government’s response to Hurricane Helene, which devastated the mountain communities of Western North Carolina two years ago.

Other Democrats scoffed at the group’s decision to spend money targeting entrenched Republicans far from the main House battleground.

“There was a lot of reluctance from people to really believe that that data was correct, but it was,’’ Dennis noted. “Then over the summer, we saw her numbers collapsing, so we put paid media behind it and it really paid off.”.

Hubbard ran against Foxx two years ago and lost by almost 20 points.

Industry observers note that “I kind of had a notion I was going to do this again,’’ he stated in an interview Saturday while en route to Washington for freshman orientation. “I don’t like to lose at checkers, much less a congressional race.”.

After a court-drawn map resulted in a split North Carolina delegation after the 2022 elections, state Republicans won back control of the map-making process and went on to win 10 of the state’s 14 House seats under a new map two years later.

At Trump’s urging, Republicans made further tweaks to the North Carolina map last year, but the original gerrymander finally came back to bite the GOP in 2026, according to Hubbard.

“North Carolina is one of the most severely gerrymandered states,’’ he said. “And what happened was they had to steal from Peter to pay Paul. It's been referred to by political scientists as a dummymander.”.

As the vote count in the 5th District continues, Foxx, whose campaign declined to comment for this story, has requested the presence of nonpartisan election observers.

They “will serve as vital, watchful eyes to ensure that this sacred process is not impeded and that all legal votes are counted in a consistent, thorough manner,’’ she posted on social media.

But even before the final races are called, Republicans are already looking to the next election.

Heye, who expects North Carolina to remain a purple state in 2028 and beyond, cautioned the Democrats who won last week not to get too comfortable in Washington. He invoked Fred Heineman, the former Raleigh police chief who rode the 1994 “Republican Revolution” to Congress – and lasted a single term.

“Some of them will lose, and some of the people who lost may run two years from now and get their seat back,’’ he mentioned.

One GOP operative, who requested anonymity to speak candidly, offered up a similar assessment.

Trump “didn't keep his promises” and that “just got voters very angry and suppressed the GOP base from coming out because, in a midterm election it's a base turnout contest,’’ the strategist said.

“But these Democrats are renting these districts for two years.”.

#100355. Why Luxury Watch Brands Are Still Struggling Online

Why Luxury Watch Brands Are Still Struggling Online

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2589 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the ever-shifting digital landscape rewards brands that are creative, agile, consistent across geographic areas, and can turn digital awareness into commercial opportunities through an effective omnichannel strategy.
  • Sources indicate that however, traditional discovery channels are proving resilient in the watch industry.
  • It has been revealed that in our digital analysis for the 2026 Vogue Business Watch Index, while the crown once again goes to Cartier, the ranking reveals several changes and surprises, notably IWC’s rise and Rolex’s slide.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the ever-shifting digital landscape rewards brands that are creative, agile, consistent across geographic areas, and can turn digital awareness into commercial opportunities through an effective omnichannel strategy. In this competitive environment, small brands with a focused, strategic approach can appear larger than life, while market leaders resting on their laurels could see their relevance shrink.

Sources indicate that however, traditional discovery channels are proving resilient in the watch industry. Brand-owned websites remain the top destination for information and latest brand or product discovery, despite the rise of social media. The challenge is to turn digital visibility into engagement through strong direct-to-consumer (DTC) websites and a seamless omnichannel experience.

It has been revealed that in our digital analysis for the 2026 Vogue Business Watch Index, while the crown once again goes to Cartier, the ranking reveals several changes and surprises, notably IWC’s rise and Rolex’s slide. Due to the unavailability of data this year, Vogue Business has removed its review of performance on Chinese social media platforms WeChat, Xiaohongshu and Weibo as part of its methodology patch. And while brands continuously refine their tactics on well-established — yet always evolving — digital platforms, it’s also important to track emerging ones that are rapidly capturing the public’s attention.

In a recent development, in this year’s index, Hublot delivers a standout performance, jumping seven positions in the digital ranking vs. 2025 and landing just outside the top five. The key contributors to Hublot’s ascent are its robust digital services, which include a comprehensive omnichannel experience, and its Instagram performance. The brand has seen follower and engagement growth through content created in collaboration with its roster of ambassadors spanning sports and art.

In a recent development, IWC has considerably strengthened its position in the top five, advancing three places and landing second behind Cartier, thanks to exceptional social media performance, particularly on Facebook, where its engineering- and Formula 1-focused content continues to resonate. Omega slipped one place to third, yet remained a strong digital performer. The brand is strong on Instagram, TikTok and WeChat, and its Google Search visibility has increased year-on-year.

Meanwhile, despite its strong awareness and about 185 million Google visits from September 2025 to August 2026, Rolex slipped from third place in 2025 to fifth this year, due to insufficient activity, particularly on TikTok, where the brand has over 230,000 followers.

Longines’s fall from fourth to ninth place stands out. Historically, it’s a brand that performed well on Chinese platforms like Xiaohongshu and WeChat. However, its modest visibility on Western social media channels drags down its overall performance this year and highlights the need to deliver a consistent message across all geographies.

Recent findings suggest that A granular analysis of the overall digital ranking unveils that each brand has its own specific strengths and weaknesses. Yet a dichotomy emerges between brands with strong digital visibility and those that can integrate that digital visibility into omnichannel customer service activities that may ultimately lead to commercial transactions.

The brands that perform best for digital, for example with high levels of engagement and interaction, are not always the brands that consumers rate highly for digital experience. For the most part, our consumer research demonstrates that opinions of content generally lag behind a more positive perception of the overall digital experience, with Tudor showing the biggest gap between the two.

Although Hublot ranks sixth in the overall digital ranking, it still has room to improve its omnichannel digital services. The brand boasts an innovative club-like loyalty program known as Hublotista, open to all Hublot watch owners; it offers live chats and click-and-collect options. However, other elements, such as product personalization and live inventory availability, trail competitors. Hublot is also the top performer on Instagram, but it ranks 15th in its Google Search traffic score. This means the brand excels at creating visibility and capitalizing on it through services, but it still has room to improve its equity in overall desirability.

While Omega sits at 89% and third in the digital ranking, its omnichannel services have significant scope for growth. Although it has several customer service options, some more dynamic offerings, like loyalty programs, live inventories, and product customization, could be strengthened. In contrast, Panerai performs well on omnichannel for a brand of its size, coming in third for this assessment with its Panerai Passport service, WhatsApp customer service option and strong online-offline integration, but its digital performance on socials is significantly behind others, putting it at 18th overall for digital. Meanwhile, Richemont-owned Piaget ranks 16th overall for digital, driven by poorer exposure on Google Search and TikTok, but places fifth for omnichannel with a strong range of customer service options, click-and-collect and pre-order options.

But it’s Rolex that demonstrates the most drastic dichotomy. The undisputed market leader, it generated a total turnover of CHF 11 billion ($13.1 billion) in 2025, up 4% from 2024, and commands a market share of 32.9%, followed by Cartier (8.7%), Patek Philippe (7%) and Omega (6.4%). The brand also tops the YouTube ranking and is the second most-searched brand on Google, behind Cartier. Yet while Rolex ranks fifth overall for digital performance, it is 17th for omnichannel services. Its absence from TikTok and limited digital services, which the brand typically hands over to its distributors rather than managing directly, weigh on its performance.

In a recent development, services generally rank high among respondents’ preferences. Real-time product availability both in-store and online is the most sought-after service for 79%, followed by multiple channels of customer service (email, phone, messenger) at 76%, buying from the brand’s website at 74%, and the ability to speak directly to a brand advisor (phone, video, live chat) when shopping online at 73%. The possibility to pay in local currency far outweighs cryptocurrency (70% vs 26%), although crypto matters more for 41% of older Gen Z and younger millennials aged 25-34. All the services highlighted imply the importance of human contact and physical presence, which are also common denominators for brand experiences — the other most notable development that excites consumers (alongside limited-edition timepieces).

In a recent development, since the early 2000s, when Google Search began to rise in the digital world, search engine optimization (SEO) has been front and center in brands’ digital preoccupations, ensuring their products are easily found on Google and placed at the top of consumers’ search results. Websites, e-commerce platforms and digital campaigns are now built to match SEO criteria. But Google’s dominance is eroding and, with it, the foundations of brands’ digital strategies are starting to wobble, as consumers flock to AI-driven chatbots where GEO (generative engine optimization) becomes the new metric to please.

The watch industry is still, by and large, a sector that relies on traditional modes of discovery. Brand websites are the top channel for both sourcing information and discovering new brands or products, highlighting how important it is for brands to have robust DTC websites. This is reinforced by the fact that, on average across all brands, nearly half (47.8%) of consumers who purchased watches in the last year bought directly from the brand. When researching watches, word-of-mouth recommendations and review sites or discussion forums rank among the top five channels, alongside search engines and magazines.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to discovering new products or brands, however, magazines and social media play an influential role, as do monobrand stores and flagships. Yet in the fast-changing digital landscape, new modes of discovery are becoming increasingly ingrained in shopping habits, and preferred purchasing channels are shifting, with the average number of people using resale rising from 29.7% who shopped in the last year to 40.8% of those intending to buy in the coming year.

Sources indicate that according to a Bain & Company study published in March, 56% of US-based consumers still resort to Google, but 16% already mostly or always use AI chatbots and 28% mix the two. But adoption of AI chatbots is stronger among Gen Z (25% mostly or always use chatbots and 33% mix the two), millennials (24% mostly or always use chatbots and 34% mix the two), and Gen X (14% mostly or always use chatbots and 31% mix the two). Thirty-three per cent of consumers already use AI chatbots for recommendations in general and 19% for shopping assistance specifically.

It has been revealed that in this context, some brands have started to adapt. Nomos Glashütte, an independent watch brand based in the German watchmaking cluster that is also home to Richemont-owned A. Lange & Söhne, has begun updating its website to ensure AI chatbots can read it correctly and surface the brand’s products in their recommendations.

According to recent reports, analysts consider a website overhaul the easiest component of GEO brands can act on; the others remain much harder to control. AI chatbots draw information not only from brands’ websites but also from articles published in legacy media, typically sorted by readership and prestige. This is an element brands can influence through old-school public relations activity, but it is not fully under their sway. The third component is even more elusive: consumers’ comments on social media.

It has been revealed that while brands practice “social listening” to improve on public feedback, they still can’t control people’s opinions and messages. But such comments are increasingly finding their way into AI chatbots, and they predominantly come from social media that are still new territory for brands: Reddit and Substack.

A 2025 survey of Gen Zs, conducted by Vogue Business and youth culture agency Archrival, found that 65% of respondents use Reddit to find and discover products, valuing the platform’s privacy and the ability to ask questions anonymously. Vogue Business also highlighted that users typically spend longer on Reddit’s detailed threads than they do on other social platforms.

Recent findings suggest that AI visibility is rapidly gaining relevance. Launchmetrics launched a latest AI Visibility metric alongside its usual proprietary Media Impact Value. According to the firm’s analysis of brand mentions by AI during the Watches and Wonders fair, “being liked and being mentioned are two different things in AI. Tudor and Panerai come up far less often in AI answers, but when they do appear, they’re described so positively that it impacts their overall rank to third and fourth overall.”.

IWC achieves an impressive 95% score and lands in second place in the digital marketing ranking behind Cartier, as its laser-focused video strategy, highlighting a few key messages, delivers significant results. The Schaffhausen-headquartered brand is best-performing on Facebook with a score of 93%; second best on TikTok with 90%, behind Cartier (95%); and on YouTube with 89%, behind Rolex (92%).

Recent findings suggest that the brand’s message, anchored in engineering excellence and innovation, is articulated through its association with Formula 1 and a few well-selected ambassadors who don’t simply pose wearing a timepiece but get involved in brand-related projects. IWC also regularly features videos of its watchmakers assembling timepieces. One filming Florian Salzer working on the Ingenieur Tourbillon 41 IWC345901 amassed over 10 million views and over half a million likes on TikTok alone.

IWC also runs the successful series “IWC Replies”, in which watchmakers answer technical questions asked by the community, like “Would the perpetual calendar still work after 2299?”.

This year, IWC released a series of timepieces co-designed with George Russell, a driver for the Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula 1 team. The watch was made in the racing team’s blue hue, engraved on the back with Russell’s number 63, and Russell himself featured in the social media campaign. The brand has previously collaborated with supermodel Gisele Bündchen, who was not only an ambassador but an environmental and community projects advisor. The brand playfully mixes engineering-focused content with ambassador-led storytelling. One TikTok video featuring Russell’s teammate, Kimi Antonelli, assembling a timepiece achieved half a million views, proving the appeal of involving the brand’s “myth-makers” in the watchmaking process.

Videos of IWC’s watchmakers at work have helped the brand rise three places to second in this year’s Index.

It has been revealed that IWC also explores content related to travel where precision matters, like space travel and aviation. This year, the brand is collaborating with Vast to test timepieces during space flights. In a more poetic vein, the brand also debuted a new Pilot’s Watch celebrating the 20th anniversary of its association with the foundation linked to author and aviator Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, who wrote the children’s tale of the space traveler The Little Prince.

Managing director, Ulysse Nardin.

In a recent development, while many watchmakers still value traditional media, Ulysse Nardin has embraced social media and made it a pillar of its communications strategy. Why?

Continuous improvement is obviously a must, but in brand-building, it is not enough. There are many elements of brand-building we could choose to focus on, but not all would deliver the same impact. With all the money in the world, I don’t think we could revolutionize the in-store customer experience and move the needle for our brand.

Recent findings suggest that but social media is still a blue ocean, in the sense that small investments can deliver impactful, meaningful results. But you need to know the rules of the game. The type of content that is consumed and thrives on social media is made by content creators, not the polished content by luxury brands. People relate to people, and partnering with content creators is paramount.

We asked ourselves: how can we go viral and put our iconic Freak watch in the minds of millions of people with minimal investment?

We noticed that food-related content was getting a lot of traction, so we decided to collaborate with chocolate specialist Amaury Guichon, who is half Swiss and half French. The video of him making a giant chocolate sculpture of the Freak watch was watched by half a billion people. Amaury Guichon is now a friend of the brand, and we featured him in our UNstoppable campaign on social media, which celebrates the achievements of extraordinary people.

Industry observers note that and you managed to have a big impact at Watches and Wonders with dancing robots. Tell us more about that.

One of the brand’s pillars, which is transversal across all our activities, is our mission to inspire innovation.

We knew that at Watches and Wonders, we did not want to be confined to a box and mark our presence on the whole fair. Renting two robots, which cost us less than a page of advertising in a glossy magazine, proved a very effective way to achieve our objective. We dressed them in sweaters celebrating the 25th anniversary of the Freak watch. As they greeted guests and danced, many visitors stopped to take pictures of them and share them on social media. The visitors became our spontaneous content creators.

Ulysse Nardin’s dancing robots at Watches and Wonders cost less than a magazine ad page and turned visitors into the brand’s content creators.

We spent no money on advertising at Watches and Wonders, but we had a substantial impact. Thanks to these unconventional actions, the Freak watch has become a pillar of the brand, accounting for about 50% of total turnover.

The Vogue Business Watch Index examines watchmakers’ digital activity across 48 social media platforms: the Western trinity of Facebook, Instagram and YouTube as well as the global China-native TikTok. A separate score is assigned for search volumes on Google, as well as for the digital services offered by the brands. All these scores are weighted to produce a final digital ranking.

  • Bakeries are no longer just a stop along the way—they’re the final destination.
  • Bakery tourism is on the rise, and honestly, I'm not surprised.
  • It’s not just individual pastries getting all the attention, either.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bakeries are no longer just a stop along the way—they’re the final destination. According to Yelp’s 2027 Food and Drink Trend report, bakeries are becoming such a hot commodity that people are planning entire trips around viral treats. Yelp searches for “bakeries near me” are up 561% from last year, while searches for a “sweet treat” are up 303%. Treat yo’ self culture is officially here.

Bakery tourism is on the rise, and honestly, I'm not surprised. I, myself, am prone to walking unfamiliar city streets just to get my hands on the town's most beloved pastry. And people are getting pretty specific about what they want. Searches for cardamom buns are up 24%, kouign-amann 67%, and salt bread a whopping 616%.

It’s not just individual pastries getting all the attention, either. Yelp found that searches for “hot and newly introduced bakeries” jumped 359%, while “best gluten-free bakery” rose 113%. Bakeries are also the most-saved type of specialty food shop on Yelp’s My Lists feature. Even New York City's Radio Bakery, which you’ll find below, saw searches increase by 176%. It seems we’re all doing some serious research before our next pastry run.

Recent findings suggest that so which hot spots should you add to your must-visit list? I asked Yelp to do a deep dive into the most-saved bakeries across America to see which ones people are bookmarking. Here's what came out on top.

This famed Taiwanese bakery opened its first U.S. outpost earlier this year in Pasadena, California, and has already gone viral for its unique cream cheese-filled bagels and flaky pastries.

What started out as a pandemic-era creation has now morphed into a line-worthy brick-and-mortar. Bad Butter regularly draws block-long lines, with its breads, croissants, and pastries often selling out.

In Santa Ana, California, 61hundred Bread is known for its signature heirloom blue-corn masa sourdough bread, along with Filipino baked goods like pandesal and ube-filled cruffins.

At this Fresh York City French bakery, the jambon-beurre sandwich is the star item. Fresh baguettes and flaky croissants are also among the other reasons locals and tourists flock to the shop.

Located at the Halepuna Waikiki hotel in Honolulu, Hawaii, Halekulani Bakery is known for its signature coconut cake and assortment of pastries.

Located in Los Angeles, California, Out Of Ordi specializes in Korean-style salt bread.

Newly introduced York City’s Sunday Morning frequently sells out of its viral cinnamon rolls.

San Diego’s Relic Bakery & Kitchen offers a mix of sweet and savory baked goods, from pies and croissants to breads and danishes.

In Upcoming York City, you’ll find Justin’s Salt Bread, voted the city’s best new bakery of the year and known for—you guessed it—its salt bread.

San Francisco’s Butter & Crumble is known for its crumble cakes and laminated pastries, with offerings that rotate seasonally.

Another Honolulu bakery makes the list, although this one comes with a twist. Part bakery, part butcher shop, The Local General Store sells everything from quiche and danishes to sausage and ham.

It looks like my travel schedule just got a little busier (and tastier).

#100351. K-Pop Stars, Art and Unexpected Collabs: Inside the 2026 Watch Innovation Playbook

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3102 w)
