K-Pop Stars, Art and Unexpected Collabs: Inside the 2026 Watch Innovation Playbook

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3102 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After a tough 2025 for the watch industry, 2026 has painted a sunnier picture.
  • Nevertheless, after the shock of the annus horribilis that was 2025, most brands have reviewed their investments, typically ditching high-cost, high-visibility sponsorships in favor of projects that deliver more immediate, tangible results.
  • Following in the footsteps of Rolex, which left Formula 1 sponsorship to LVMH-owned brands, Hublot reduced its involvement in soccer to strengthen collaborations with artists and existing ambassadors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a tough 2025 for the watch industry, 2026 has painted a sunnier picture. Overall export value has grown by 2.7% thanks to unexpected pockets of growth in emerging markets (India +28.5%, Thailand +8.6%, and Mexico +6.2%), which offset drops in traditionally strong markets like China (-5.9%) and Saudi Arabia (-10.3%).

Nevertheless, after the shock of the annus horribilis that was 2025, most brands have reviewed their investments, typically ditching high-cost, high-visibility sponsorships in favor of projects that deliver more immediate, tangible results.

Following in the footsteps of Rolex, which left Formula 1 sponsorship to LVMH-owned brands, Hublot reduced its involvement in soccer to strengthen collaborations with artists and existing ambassadors. Ambassadorship became an evolving concept this year, with brands moving beyond campaign appearances to involve their ambassadors in creating the timepieces they promote: Audemars Piguet released a watch co-designed with tennis player Serena Williams, Movado teamed up with American rapper Ludacris, and Hublot unveiled a watch by British designer Samuel Ross. Another defining ambassador trend has been the emergence of partnerships with non-Western talents predominantly from South Korea, Thailand and India, countries that are delivering positive results for the watch business.

It has been revealed that brands have also been experimenting with collaboration projects outside the typical realms of sports and cars. Visual art has emerged as the watchmakers’ new playground, with Vacheron Constantin unveiling its first mentorship project with The Met in New York and Piaget releasing another watch made in collaboration with The Andy Warhol Foundation. But there were also some unexpected twists, notably with Roger Dubuis teaming up with tattoo artist Dr Woo and Hublot partnering with artist Jeff Koons for timepieces.

Hublot’s partnership with artist Jeff Koons.

Recent findings suggest that brands also ventured into new partnerships. Richard Mille teamed up with the Italian high-end bicycle manufacturer Colnago, Zenith partnered with furniture maker USM, while Ulysse Nardin established an innovative tie-up with pastry chef Amaury Guichon for its Unstoppable Spirits campaign. This suggests that engagement with the luxury watch category is also operating as a gateway to more niche cultural and lifestyle pursuits.

It has been revealed that but collaborations between watch brands were the most prominent modus operandi of 2026. Audemars Piguet and Swatch took center stage with their Royal Pop collection, while Louis Vuitton partnered with independent watchmaker De Bethune and Ulysse Nardin joined forces with Urwerk to unveil the UR-Freak, one of the most contemporary iterations of luxury watchmaking in recent times.

Consumers reflected these sentiments in our 2026 survey. When asked, “Which developments excite you the most in the luxury watch market?”, the top three answers were: limited-edition watches, resale service and experiences. Excitement around resale services was consistent across age groups, with a median value of 60% — the lowest recorded value was among Gen Z (18-24) at 56.4% and the highest among boomers (55-64) at 65.5%.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, 70% of luxury watch consumers globally are excited about limited-edition watches, with this rising to 76% among Chinese shoppers. When it comes to experiences, 58% globally are most excited about these novel ways to experience brands, especially 25- to 34-year-olds, at 66%.

Industry observers note that longines has risen to the top 10 in the Vogue Business Watch Index this year (seeing a 58% increase), thanks to a combination of niche sports and celebrity tie-ins. The brand’s performance was helped by its long-time partnerships with equestrian competitions, which this year enjoyed extra visibility through the digital game Longines League of Nations™ Memory Game, developed in partnership with Fédération Équestre Internationale (FEI). The Commonwealth Games, which take place every four years and of which Longines was a sponsor, offered another boost. Longines’s astute partnerships are also noteworthy. Alongside its long-standing relationships with Jennifer Lawrence and Kate Winslet, the brand has partnered with rising Thai talent, gaining visibility in a country where Swiss watches have grown by 8.6% in value between January and September 2026 vs the same period in 2025.

Meanwhile, “Wes Anderson: The Archives”, the exhibition held at the Design Museum in London between November 2025 and July 2026 and dedicated to the filmmaker and long-time ambassador, was one of the factors that helped Hamburg-headquartered Montblanc improve its innovation score. Another factor was the #LetsWrite campaign, which transformed some of Montblanc’s flagship stores worldwide into oases to rediscover the art of writing. The visibility of these novel initiatives propelled the brand to sixth place, up 36 percentage points.

Montblanc’s partnership with long-time ambassador Wes Anderson, celebrated in the Design Museum’s “Wes Anderson: The Archives” exhibition, helped the brand climb to sixth place for innovation.

It has been revealed that panerai and Piaget both grew by 16%, earning their positions in the top 10. Panerai’s brand exhibition in its hometown of Florence boosted the brand’s score, along with customer services such as virtual try-ons. The collaboration with The Andy Warhol Foundation, an innovative use of a Snapchat lens for virtual try-on, and the offer of a digital product passport (DPP) are some of the factors behind Piaget’s progress.

It has been revealed that at the top of the table, despite a few shuffles, last year’s best performers broadly maintained their positions this year. Breitling takes the crown with 11 percentage points of growth, jumping two positions ahead of IWC and Cartier, which in 2026 occupied second and third place, respectively. Chopard sits in fourth alongside Panerai, which records a substantial 16% increase in fifth position, up three positions vs. 2025. Hublot slips to sixth, down from fourth last year.

It has been revealed that more shifts have happened at the bottom of the table. Although Patek Philippe and Tudor remain among the bottom five, Zenith marks a standout recovery with an increase of 26 percentage points, alongside Rolex, which has moved up by 10 percentage points.

According to recent reports, both Movado and A. Lange & Söhne have lost about 10 percentage points, moving down among the bottom 10 brands, alongside Omega, which has fallen 20 percentage points and landed in the bottom five. Despite its collaboration with Swatch for the Audemars Piguet x Swatch Royal Pop Collection, the Le Brassus-headquartered brand dropped 26 percentage points, losing five positions and landing in the middle of the table at 11th place.

Seismic shifts in the watch industry have prompted brands to sign a upcoming cohort of celebrity ambassadors who can seduce audiences in promising new markets. While China’s economic landscape still keeps imports in negative territory, and the war in Iran has disrupted the Middle East market, with Saudi Arabia’s market contracting by 10.3%, India, South Korea and Thailand are growing.

Sources indicate that in June 2026, Rolex grabbed headlines not with one of its many leading tennis players at Roland-Garros but with the appointment of Priyanka Chopra Jones as its first Indian entertainment celebrity to join its roster of “testimonees” — the brand’s lingo for ambassadors. The brand had previously signed only Indian athletes, including tennis player Vijay Amritraj and golfers Jeev Milkha Singh and Anirban Lahiri. This move acknowledges the growing importance of the Indian market in the watchmaking business. According to the Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry, the value of Indian imports of timepieces grew by 28.5% in 2026 vs 2025 (January–September) and by 40.9% vs 2024 (January–September).

Other watch brands have also signed up Indian celebrities: Omega appointed javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra, and Rado teamed up with female cricketer Smriti Mandhana.

Industry observers note that in the wake of Thailand’s rise in the watch business, brands have been signing up Thai talents in rapid succession. This summer, Cartier added actor PP Krit Amnuaydechkorn to its portfolio of Thai ambassadors, which already includes singer and actor Jeff Satur, actress Kimberley Anne Woltemas, and actor Tor Thanapob Leeratanakachorn. Meanwhile, Piaget has teamed up with Thai actor Apo Nattawin Wattanagitiphat since 2024, and Casio featured Thai kickboxing world champion Superbon Singha Mawynn in its “Tough Like You” campaign.

But a top priority for watch brands right now is having a South Korean talent, preferably from one of the bands riding high on K-pop mania. At the start of 2026, Hublot signed Jung Kook, a member of the beloved band BTS, who has over 27 million Instagram followers and 35 million on TikTok. Meanwhile, in 2025, Piaget appointed actress Gianna Jun, following in the footsteps of Longines, which the year before brought on board actress Bae Suzy, a former member of the K-pop girl group Miss A. Omega has three South Korean ambassadors: actress Shin Min-a and actors Park Bo-gum and Hyun Bin, while Chopard signed all four members of K-pop band Aespa — Karina, Winter, Giselle and Ningning — back in 2023.

Hublot signed Jung Kook, a member of the beloved band BTS, who has over 27 million Instagram followers and 35 million on TikTok.

Watchmakers have also experimented with a different cohort of ambassadors: Ulysse Nardin’s tie-up with chef chocolatier Amaury Guichon led to approximately half a billion views across social media, according to the brand, while Gallet, a brand owned by Breitling, has partnered with a group of six explorers active on social media for its relaunch campaign.

Sources indicate that the watch and automotive partnership is nothing latest, thanks to the overlapping interests in mechanics, design and a predominantly male clientele, and recent collaborations suggest this is unlikely to change. Tag Heuer’s long-standing partnership with Formula 1 was boosted last year when LVMH took over the tournament sponsorship from Rolex, offering the brand the opportunity to further expand associated products and storytelling. Early this year, Breitling signed a global, multi-year partnership with Aston Martin, leading to the release of the Navitimer B01 Chronograph 43 Aston Martin Aramco, marking Breitling’s return to Formula 1. Bianchet announced a partnership with Maserati, unveiling the first UltraFino Maserati at Watches and Wonders in Geneva. Meanwhile, Casio teamed up with Toyota Racing, and Roger Dubuis confirmed its enduring association with Lamborghini.

But there have been some twists in the category. At the end of the summer, Seiko announced a collaboration with Honda — not with any of its cars or muscular motorcycles, but with Motocompo, a compact, foldable scooter — the very opposite of a bling, power-signaling motor vehicle. It was one of many recent unusual collaborations that watchmakers hope will reach newly introduced audiences, unveil novel features of their brand’s DNA, and make them seem less intimidating and more approachable.

According to recent reports, at the end of 2025, Zenith collaborated with the furniture organization USM, whose designs are ubiquitous at Zenith’s headquarters in Le Locle, on a series of four Defy watches featuring USM’s saturated colors and delivered in USM boxes made with its signature Haller modular system. Rado entered into a similar partnership with the industrial design company Tej Chauhan.

According to recent reports, more unusual still, in September this year, Casio unveiled a newly introduced AQ-230ECK with a distinctive matcha-tea-green dial featuring a black fox at 12 o’clock and, at 6 o’clock, the logo of Café Kitsuné, the coffee shop chain of French-Japanese brand Maison Kitsuné. This demonstrates the trend toward unlikely collaborators extends beyond the luxury end of the market and is taking root across the sector as a whole.

Another unlikely partnership was between German watchmaker Nomos and Doctors Without Borders, which aims to raise funds and awareness for the work of doctors in areas plagued by wars, natural disasters and epidemics, and to provide access to necessary health care. This partnership resulted in a limited-edition Ludwig model featuring a red number 12 on a white dial.

Even tried-and-tested art partnerships have lately taken on unexpected forms. At the end of last year, Roger Dubuis released a series of watches in collaboration with Los Angeles-based tattoo artist Dr Woo, while this year, Vacheron Constantin invited artists such as glass-makers and wood furniture designers to miniaturize their work to fit the proportions of a watch dial.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Hublot grabbed headlines with two newly introduced watches co-designed by artist Jeff Koons. The first is the Hublot Classic Fusion Balloon Dog, a series of three timepieces in red, blue and silver, each limited to 200 pieces, mimicking Koons’s iconic inflated dog sculpture in its rounded bezel, case and crown. The second is the more elaborate, gem-set Hublot MP-14 Origin inspired by Koons’s Gazing Ball works. In some ways, these standout partnerships make the high-profile, long-established relationship between Omega and the James Bond franchise — most recently leading to six new Seamaster Diver models inspired by James Bond and Spectre — seem quite tame in comparison.

Industry observers note that omega’s fresh Seamaster Diver 300M Spectre edition. Released on Global James Bond Day, it’s the first time in the brand’s three-decade partnership with the franchise that Omega has made a watch for Bond’s nemesis.

During the watch fair Watches and Wonders in April, Swatch ran a newspaper ad that read, “The real wonders are happening in May.” What subsequently happened was the collaboration that dominated the news in 2026: the one between Audemars Piguet and Swatch for the release of the Royal Pop, the $439 pocket watch shaped like Audemars Piguet’s Royal Oak, made in the eye-popping colors and affordable materials of a Swatch timepiece.

It marks the first time Swatch collaborated with a brand outside its portfolio, as previous tie-ups were with Omega for the MoonSwatch and Blancpain for Fifty Fathoms. It’s also the very first time Audemars Piguet released a watch bearing its logo and costing considerably less than $20,000, its usual entry price.

The enthusiasm around the watch release was so exceptionally high that it led to people camping outside the authorized Swatch stores for days, marred by episodes of violence. “Everybody was so enthusiastic about this innovative product and the combination of two iconic Swiss brands in extremely opposite segments that they forgot the Royal Pop is not a product to be sold only on the launch day but over many months,” Swatch CEO Nick Hayek said, answering the criticism around the launch in an interview with Vogue Business.

In a recent development, but the collaboration was still significant because it considerably boosted awareness of both brands and increased traffic to both their websites and social media accounts. Mr Hayek also hopes that the collaboration can reignite interest in more affordable watches in a climate where the industry keeps moving upmarket. “My father always said: be careful when an industry keeps moving further upmarket and becoming more expensive — you lose creativity, you lose innovation,” Hayek notes. “It’s the same in many industries. If a luxury industry starts producing only for the elite, only for a small bubble of people, eventually billions of real people disconnect.”.

Double-signed watches have been a feature of the watch industry since its infancy, when a watch would bear the logo of the movement maker as well as that of the retailer. In the vintage market, double-signed timepieces such as Audemars Piguet-Tiffany or Patek Philippe-Cartier are sought-after rarities. But as watchmakers progressively chose to produce their own movements, double-signed watches disappeared. This fresh wave of watch brand collaborations aims not only to blend design and storytelling to appeal to a much wider audience, but also to combine elements of the brands’ own movements to intrigue watch nerds.

What have you done to bring your brand closer to women?

According to recent reports, we believe our roots in technique and our passion for precision are genderless and can appeal to both men and women. Women have always been part of the brand’s history, as the jewelry watches in our archive prove. We have never wanted to create a separate universe and products specifically for women. Instead, we have worked on our products, the design of our boutiques, and our communications.

We have expanded our product range to include more ergonomic case sizes, giving clients the freedom to choose proportions that best suit their wrists and personal style. We have also focused on making our boutique design aesthetically appealing and welcoming for both men and women. And finally, communication has been crucial. Female ambassadors, such as supermodel Gisele Bündchen and Eileen Gu, have also hugely helped raise our brand awareness among women.

IWC ambassador Gisele Bündchen.

How has your loyalty to Formula 1 played out in your strategy?

It has been revealed that formula 1, and motorsport in general, has always been part of our identity, and we continue to show that loyalty through our ambassadors, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. Our affinity for Formula 1 led to last year’s collaboration with F1 The Movie.

According to recent reports, our loyalty to Formula 1 is also helping the brand raise its profile among women. In the past, the Formula 1 audience was 80% men and only 20% women. The balance is now 50-50, meaning more women have grown closer to our brand thanks to Formula 1. A case in point is our new friend of the brand, George Russell’s fiancée, Carmen Montero Mundt, who spontaneously began wearing our brand. It often happens that our clients’ wives also like the brand, and entire generations often become loyal clients.

How have you employed social media to draw women closer?

Sources indicate that our social media channels help us connect with women. On our channels, we regularly show famous women and models wearing our watches, as well as the women working in our manufacture. Last year, we introduced the series “IWC.Inspired”, which celebrates the achievements of women from all walks of life who use time wisely and with purpose. So far, we have featured skincare expert Melanie Grant, Michelle Kennedy, founder of the social networking app Peanut, and British model and entrepreneur Jodie Kidd.

The Vogue Business Watch Index assigns an innovation score to the experiences and services brands offer to existing clients, prospective ones and stakeholders at large across the digital and physical worlds.

The services examined in the digital world include NFTs, augmented reality and virtual reality on brands’ websites and social media channels that allow virtual try-ons or immersive, game-like experiences; collaborations across films, TV and gaming; and the digital translation of physical experiences such as exhibitions.

Among the services assessed in the physical world are traceability tools, resale services offered either directly by the brand or a third party, the acceptance of cryptocurrency payments, and virtual consultations straddling the digital and physical realms.

Consumer research was conducted over October 2026, while digital data and innovation audit data captured the period between September 2025 and August 2026. Data was captured across 20 brands and metrics are weighted according to the importance assigned by survey respondents.

Breaking: Bon Appétit Pick: HelloFresh Garlicky Shrimp Couscous Bowl

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most nights I try to hit up an exercise class after work, which means when I finally get home in the evening I’m tired, hungry, and craving something full of nutrients.
  • Sources indicate that this flavorful bowl reminds me of Dig Inn’s glory days—only I can enjoy it without elbowing my way through midtown lunchtime mobs.
  • According to recent reports, you’ll need to grab olive oil, butter, salt, and pepper from your own pantry; everything else is included in your delivery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most nights I try to hit up an exercise class after work, which means when I finally get home in the evening I’m tired, hungry, and craving something full of nutrients. With 26 grams of protein and just 25 minutes of prep-and-cook time, HelloFresh’s Garlicky Shrimp Couscous Bowl is a great solution for dinner.

Sources indicate that this flavorful bowl reminds me of Dig Inn’s glory days—only I can enjoy it without elbowing my way through midtown lunchtime mobs. Roasted broccoli and shrimp sautéed with lemon and plenty of garlic are spooned on top of large couscous pearls. Chili flakes add an extra kick.

According to recent reports, you’ll need to grab olive oil, butter, salt, and pepper from your own pantry; everything else is included in your delivery. The shrimp arrives fully cleaned and deveined, thank god. I love that a small pouch of veggie stock is included for cooking your couscous, a detail that many meal kits overlook.

True to the recipe card’s promise, the meal cooks in less than half an hour. Prep your mise (chop the broccoli, garlic, and parsley; slice your lemon; rinse the shrimp), then get your broccoli in the oven and couscous on the stove. While they do their thing, you cook the shrimp so that everything finishes around the same time.

Recent findings suggest that I found the instructions incredibly clear to follow, including when to add water and butter to your shrimp, and when to reduce the pan’s heat. I don’t often cook shrimp at home, and I was pleasantly surprised how easy it was and how rapidly they pinked up.

Sources indicate that in a word: delish! Garlic can cover a multitude of sins, and there’s a generous amount used when cooking both the couscous and shrimp, the latter also includes garlic powder, for good measure. Lemon and parsley give the dish a nice freshness; the flavors remind me of my favorite clam pie from a local Brooklyn pizzeria.

Sources indicate that this is a great dish for pescatarians, those looking to cut back on red meat, and health-conscious eaters. The small ingredient list is full of nutritional value: carbs, fats, and lean protein to help me refuel after a long day, plus five grams of fiber and vitamin K, calcium, and potassium from the broccoli (cruciferous veggies are super good for you).

Would make again. Sometimes you want to use your time in the kitchen to discover latest flavors and learn new techniques, and sometimes your main goal is getting dinner on the table quickly. This recipe hits on the weeknight trifecta: It’s tasty, easy to make, and nutritious.

Costco's Thanksgiving Dinner Kit Is Officially Back—Here's What It Comes With

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Laura Lamb of @costcohotfinds shared on social media that the warehouse’s Thanksgiving dinner kit has officially returned for 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, depending on who you are, cooking a full Thanksgiving dinner can bring either excitement or complete dread. If you fall into the latter camp, Costco is here to help with its newest offering in the deli department.

Laura Lamb of @costcohotfinds shared on social media that the warehouse’s Thanksgiving dinner kit has officially returned for 2026. The prepared meal includes all the holiday essentials, with much of the prep work already taken care of.

In a recent development, each kit comes with a seasoned half turkey breast over a bed of herbed stuffing, along with Yukon Gold mashed potatoes, green beans, cranberry sauce, and gravy. Costco is pricing the meal at just $3.99 per pound, which works out to around $40 to feed seven to eight people.

The label includes simple instructions for preparing all the components. The uncooked turkey, naturally, takes the most time. Since it’s placed over the stuffing, the turkey drippings add even more flavor and moisture as it roasts in the oven.

According to recent reports, the warehouse keeps this dinner kit pretty consistent from year to year, although one Costco shopper wasn’t as impressed with a particular component this time around. Costco fan and content creator @photogami reports that the gravy is a bit underseasoned and not as good as it was last year. (Thankfully, this issue has a pretty easy solution.).

Lamb also noted that you’ll still need to buy a few extras to round out the meal, like dinner rolls and pumpkin pie. And if you’re a stuffing lover, the amount that comes in Costco’s kit might not be enough for you.

Recent findings suggest that still, it’s hard to argue with the price and convenience—and members are already eager to pick up a kit for their own holiday celebrations. “Got this last year and it was all absolutely delicious,” one user on Instagram wrote. “Highly recommend.” Another commented, “This is such a great idea for a smaller Thanksgiving!”.

If you want to grab a kit for yourself, strategy accordingly. All Costco locations are closed on Thanksgiving Day, so you only have a few days to snag one.

Who Topped the 2026 Vogue Business Watch Index?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1084 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Following a challenging 2025, 2026 has offered some green shoots for the luxury watch industry.
  • Industry observers note that overall Swiss export value has grown by 2.7%, driven by unexpected pockets of growth in emerging markets (India +28.5%, Thailand +8.6% and Mexico +6.2%), which offset drops in traditionally strong markets like China (-5.9%) and Saudi Arabia (-10.3%).
  • Sources indicate that the digital audit highlights how brands are appointing high-profile cultural influencers in newer markets, from K-pop stars to Thai actors, as brand ambassadors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a challenging 2025, 2026 has offered some green shoots for the luxury watch industry.

Industry observers note that overall Swiss export value has grown by 2.7%, driven by unexpected pockets of growth in emerging markets (India +28.5%, Thailand +8.6% and Mexico +6.2%), which offset drops in traditionally strong markets like China (-5.9%) and Saudi Arabia (-10.3%). The latest consumer research from Vogue Business highlights nuanced market trends, underscoring the need for watch brands to pay particular attention to local cultural needs. In China, for example, despite a broader market slowdown, 55% of luxury watch consumers surveyed have bought themselves a timepiece to celebrate their birthday. Recognizing these behaviors can help brands make their messaging more impactful — a strategy that will become increasingly notable as shoppers rely more on emerging channels to discover products and brands.

Sources indicate that the digital audit highlights how brands are appointing high-profile cultural influencers in newer markets, from K-pop stars to Thai actors, as brand ambassadors. As the geography of growth shifts, so too must campaign strategies.

And while mainstream sports like motoring and equestrianism have historically provided key partnerships for luxury watches, more niche sports are helping brands reach fresh audiences. Yet our digital analysis also exposes some tensions the industry is grappling with; the channels relied on for sourcing trusted information are not always the channels consumers use to discover new brands and products and, as use of generative AI becomes more widespread, brands will need to adapt their digital strategies to boost visibility in this emerging space. Opportunities also remain to strengthen the omnichannel experience, with our survey highlighting shopper frustration over limited online service options.

In a recent development, in a market steeped in tradition, established leaders have defended their positions in the ranking, while collaborations with the worlds of film and art are helping legacy brands stay fresh. Consumers also continue to favor buying directly from brands, with 47.8% on average having bought their most recent watches this way or from multibrand specialists (22.5% on average). Yet while brand awareness has risen year on year, purchase intent remains relatively flat, even as enthusiasm for resale grows. As much as the availability of digital product passports (DPPs) and authentication services may encourage shoppers to engage with resale platforms, economic pressures expose a bigger driver: price sensitivity. Older consumers are particularly likely to wait for sales and discounts before making a purchase. This suggests that the demand for innovation in the pre-loved watch environment is as much a reflection of price sensitivity as it is the result of improved services in this space. It also means that, over the coming year, luxury watch brands will need to work harder to defend those “brand upcoming” watch sales in the primary market.

Cartier retains its leadership position for the third year. This summer, Cartier added actor PP Krit Amnuaydechkorn to its portfolio of Thai ambassadors, which already includes singer and actor Jeff Satur, actress Kimberley Anne Woltemas and actor Tor Thanapob Leeratanakachorn. This has helped it to maintain momentum on platforms like Instagram and gain ground on TikTok. Yet while awareness has risen, consumer opinion is more mixed, with small declines in perception of innovation, value for money and experience, showing even leaders cannot rest on their laurels.

Improved consumer perception, the highest recognition and highest purchase intent have helped Rolex to secure the second spot in this year’s ranking. The availability of certified pre-owned Rolexes at official stockists means the brand is well-positioned to take advantage of the rising demand for pre-loved luxury timepieces. Small but steady gains on all Western social media platforms have also helped the brand to stay front of mind for consumers in a cluttered digital landscape.

Omega narrowly misses out on second place this year. The brand benefits from high awareness and improved perception across several metrics. Its strong digital performance is helped by high-profile collaborations, for example, its James Bond/Spectre partnerships, but the provision of omnichannel features and innovation performance leave room for growth.

In a recent development, after breaking into the top five last year, Tag Heuer has managed to hold on to fourth position. The brand benefits from significant gains in consumer awareness, perception of quality, and positive association with more emotional drivers, as well as increased purchase intent in a market where this is relatively flat. Against a backdrop of rising price sensitivity, its positioning may help it to weather a volatile economic period.

In a recent development, after two years spent in sixth position, IWC moves into the top five for the first time this year. The brand ranks second for both Digital and Innovation, with a focused strategy on social media helping it reach fresh audiences. Its ongoing partnership with F1 is also helping to recruit more female followers, while its IWC.Inspired series celebrates women from all walks of life. Meanwhile, its partnership with Watchfinder enables consumers to part-exchange pre-loved IWC timepieces when making their next purchase, providing a seamless way to engage with the increasingly relevant resale market.

Twenty brands are assessed for the Vogue Business Watch Index, with brand performance evaluated against over 100 data points spanning consumer sentiment, digital marketing and innovation.

Sources indicate that the weightings of each assessment category and their metrics are determined by industry relevance and importance to the consumer, allowing for an objective assessment of a brand’s performance. The final weighting for each category is agreed upon following a review process with our data analysts and expert editors. This year, we removed Chinese platforms from our digital audit due to lack of data availability, with weightings being reassigned proportionally to retained digital platforms (Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok and Google Search).

Recent findings suggest that consumer research remains fundamental to the Vogue Business Watch Index, with readers across several Condé Nast titles — including Vogue, GQ, Vanity Fair and Condé Nast Traveler — participating in an annual consumer sentiment survey that ensures granularity is achieved when it comes to understanding awareness, customer challenges and brand perception. This year, we surveyed 1,020 qualified luxury watch consumers in seven markets (the US, UK, France, Germany, Italy, the Middle East and China). Among them, 60% of luxury watch consumers spent between €1,500 and €4,999 on luxury watches in the last five years, while 40% spent over €5,000.

Future iterations of the Vogue Business Watch Index will continue to maximize the brands, metrics, and digital platforms assessed, with additions prioritized in line with industry needs and developments.

In a recent development, in my opinion, the best stuffing is made with cornbread. You bring the best of both worlds together, and it’s the perfect Thanksgiving side. Crisp cornbread croutons are tossed with buttery sage, onion, and celery and baked until toasty golden brown on top and warm and custardy inside for a cornbread stuffing that will upstage even the turkey. We double down on the corn flavor by cutting most of the dairy and swapping in canned creamed corn for the liquid. The resulting cornbread is delicious enough to eat straight out of the pan.

#100339. Industry News: In Alison Roman's World, Curation is King

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (673 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Bonappetit ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: In Alison Roman's World, Curation is King

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (673 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bonappetit

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that with only weeks before opening, Alison Roman’s Brooklyn brick-and-mortar is still unfinished.
  • According to recent reports, the chaos doesn’t seem to be getting to the cookbook author, chef, and aspiring empire-builder.
  • What Roman has built has grown beyond recipes and bean propaganda.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with only weeks before opening, Alison Roman’s Brooklyn brick-and-mortar is still unfinished. “Today they’re doing up the walls and putting in the floors,” Roman states. In short, it does not yet look like a dreamy European-inspired grocer. There are still a mountain of calls to be made, meetings to be had, speed bumps to overcome.

According to recent reports, the chaos doesn’t seem to be getting to the cookbook author, chef, and aspiring empire-builder. “It’s been so fun,” Roman, a Bon Appétit alum, indicates of the process. Perhaps that shouldn’t be a surprise; this breezy effortlessness is at the bedrock of the Alison Roman universe. You know the kind of nonchalant magic I’m talking about: chilling wine bottles in a bathtub of ice, buckets of take-out fried chicken at dinner parties—I mean, this woman was one of the foremost proponents of brothy beans.

What Roman has built has grown beyond recipes and bean propaganda. The ever-creeping edges of her lifestyle brand now encompass a jarred tomato sauce brand, once cheekily titled A Very Good Sauce, now renamed Roman’s. There’s also the new podcast, Having People Over, where she hosts guests for a meal and a yap, plus the speaking tour she’s calling “Food, Life and Other Strong Opinions.” There are the shoes (sleek mules and chunky clogs) she made in collaboration with New York–based footwear brand Margaux. And now First Bloom, the grocery store–slash–wine bar–slash–café that—as of mid-November—is on track to open in December.

The Brooklyn shop is an extension of the original Catskill’s location of the same name. Roman claims this upcoming outpost is “a totally different proposition of what we are offering people.” There’s more budget to work with, there’s more staff, there’s more space, and there’s more food.

According to recent reports, whereas the upstate location’s function is closer to utility—meat and produce from local farms are a major feature—in Brooklyn (where specialty grocers abound) Roman is focusing on something more akin to world-building. But do not call First Bloom a shoppy shop, those whimsically designed boutiques that seem to pop up everywhere selling the same $45 squiggly candlesticks and squeeze-bottle olive oils everyone seems to have. “I think ‘shoppy shop’ is derogatory,” Roman states. “In a world where you can buy anything from anywhere, sometimes it’s nice to be told what to do.”.

At Brooklyn’s First Bloom, the shelves will be stocked with products that Roman herself deems “hyper-defensible.” There’s a reason they’re stocked, and a reason for how they’re priced. They’re best in class or a personal favorite of Roman’s. “Perspective and curation is a really special thing to be able to convey,” she says.

Sources indicate that the vision for First Bloom is set, but with the opening just a month out, Roman doesn’t have all the details nailed down. “We are going to have a rotisserie chicken,” she says. “I don’t know how much it’s going to cost yet,” she follows up rapidly, before I can ask. There will also be a couple salads and a couple sandwiches on offer—plus another secret off-menu sandwich for the neighborhood regulars and the real Roman-heads who know to ask for it. “I’m very if-you-know-you know,’” she says. But Brooklyn’s First Bloom isn’t just for popping into—you’ll be able to lounge with a glass of wine or relax with a snack and a coffee.

Alison Roman’s world is organic, craft-centered, and easy but considered. To step into it is an enticing foil to the AI-fueled tasteslop tilt-a-whirl on which we find ourselves. It’s a vision of a slow, steady, wabi-sabi life that many of us only aspire to. A life where one can even somehow enjoy, say, a monthslong commercial renovation project in one of America’s most competitive real estate markets. That’s the draw of First Bloom. The hard-to-find tinned fish, yes, but also the ease of living in Alison’s world if only for an hour.

And if not, well, it seems like there’ll be a pretty good rotisserie chicken, at least.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you weren’t familiar with John F. Kennedy Jr. in the ’90s, chances are that you are now, thanks to the overwhelming popularity of Love Story, this year’s hit FX series about the marriage of President John F. Kennedy’s son to fashion publicist and style icon Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy, and the couple’s tragic death in 1999.

Recent findings suggest that love Story may have piqued Gen Z’s interest in “John-John,” as John F. Kennedy Jr. was known in the press, but the real man would have turned 66 today. In his honor, we’re taking a look back at some of the images that helped define the presidential scion’s public persona.

Industry observers note that president John F. Kennedy and his wife, Jackie, during the christening of their son, John Jr., in the chapel at Georgetown University Hospital. John Jr.—dressed in the same gown his father had worn in 1917—was just 13 days old at the time.

It has been revealed that as the Newly introduced York Times reported: “The child, christened John Fitzgerald Kennedy Jr., gave one subdued cry during the eleven-minute ritual and opened his eyes when a news photographer took his picture. Otherwise the baby appeared relaxed and drowsy.”.

A young JFK Jr. playing with his mother’s ropes of pearls at the White House.

President John F. Kennedy walking with his toddler son along the White House’s West Wing colonnade.

It has been revealed that john F. Kennedy Jr. was just three days shy of his third birthday when his father was killed in Dallas in November 1963. Here, he’s pictured with his mother and his older sister, Caroline, during President Kennedy’s funeral ceremony.

Awaiting his results at St. Bernard’s 17th Annual Horse Show in New Jersey, where his sister also competed.

Feathery-haired and 10-ish, hitting a forehand return in Central Park.

Posing with Willie Mays at Latest York’s Shea Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that with a head full of curls—and his first cousin Anthony Radziwill—at the kickoff party for that year’s Robert F. Kennedy Memorial Tennis Tournament in Upcoming York.

Boating in Penobscot Bay, Maine, at 16.

Celebrating his graduation from Phillips Academy, Andover.

Cutting a lithe figure—and carrying a boombox!—in Hyannis Port.

Kennedy as Bonario in a production of Ben Jonson’s Volpone during his freshman year at Brown.

Swigging a Coke in Hyannis Port.

Wearing cowboy boots with his graduation robes on Commencement Day at Brown. (His bachelor’s degree was in American Studies.).

In a jaunty little red bow tie at a fundraising event.

Industry observers note that with his cousin Maria Shriver at Caroline Kennedy’s wedding to Edwn Schlossberg on Cape Cod. (Caroline’s dress was by Carolina Herrera.).

Looking matinee-idol handsome during a portrait session in New York.

Speaking to the press about passing the New York bar examination on his third attempt. (He also passed the bar in Connecticut.).

Enjoying a courtside snack at the US Open.

#100333. Latest Update: Which Thanksgiving Foods Belong in the Same Bite?

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (801 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tasteofhome ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Which Thanksgiving Foods Belong in the Same Bite?

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (801 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tasteofhome

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, some Thanksgiving food combinations are obvious.
  • Recent findings suggest that for years, my kids refused to let any two foods touch on their plates.
  • In a recent development, of course, plenty of adults also have strong opinions about which Thanksgiving foods should mingle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Taste of Home's Editorial Process.

In a recent development, some Thanksgiving food combinations are obvious. Others might earn you some questioning looks at the dinner table.

Recent findings suggest that for years, my kids refused to let any two foods touch on their plates. I found this particularly maddening at Thanksgiving. There’s an entire table of food to fit onto a single plate and only so much room to negotiate separate territories for the mashed potatoes and green bean casserole! Thankfully, they’re a little more accommodating these days and, like me, have come to appreciate the occasional overlap between dishes.

In a recent development, of course, plenty of adults also have strong opinions about which Thanksgiving foods should mingle. There are those who insist on keeping every dish separate, those who permit a little gravy to stray onto the stuffing but draw the line at cranberry sauce, and those who deliberately assemble the perfect combination on every forkful. Then there’s always the unhinged relative who stirs the entire contents of their plate into a single, gravy-saturated mass and eats it with the serene confidence of someone who has never once questioned their choices.

Personally, I’m firmly in favor of combining foods, although I do believe a little discretion is in order. Thanksgiving dinner offers a wonderful assortment of rich, savory and tart flavors, and knowing which ones to bring together is part of what makes the meal so satisfying. There’s a culinary reason that cranberry sauce belongs alongside turkey, and that stuffing and mashed potatoes are particularly good together. And once you understand why those combinations work, you can start building some excellent bites of your own.

Absolutely. In fact, some of the most familiar food pairings are built around the idea that one ingredient can supply something another lacks. Think of a rich cut of meat served with a sharp, acidic sauce, or a creamy dish finished with something crisp. Neither component is necessarily lacking on its own, but the contrast makes the combination much more interesting.

Industry observers note that the same principle applies to Thanksgiving foods. Acidity helps balance richness, sweetness can temper salty or intensely savory flavors, and a change in texture can make a forkful more interesting. It’s not particularly complicated, but there’s a difference between understanding why two foods complement each other and simply hoping for the best.

Some combinations are simply better than others, though saying so at Thanksgiving dinner may invite more opinions than you bargained for.

Turkey and cranberry sauce: There’s a reason this pairing has endured for generations. Turkey, particularly the breast meat, is relatively mild, and the tartness of cranberry sauce gives it a welcome lift. It’s also an excellent remedy for turkey that’s spent a little too long in the oven, a situation that has befallen even the most conscientious Thanksgiving cooks.

In a recent development, mashed potatoes, stuffing and gravy: I consider this one of Thanksgiving’s greatest achievements. The smooth, buttery potatoes and herbaceous stuffing are excellent together, and a generous spoonful of gravy makes the whole arrangement even better. There’s nothing particularly subtle about it, but Thanksgiving dinner isn’t generally celebrated for its subtlety.

Recent findings suggest that sweet potatoes and turkey: The natural sweetness of roasted sweet potatoes makes a lovely contrast to savory turkey, particularly the richer dark meat. A traditional sweet potato casserole can work, too, although I draw the line somewhere around the marshmallow topping. I have nothing against marshmallows, but I prefer to encounter them after dinner.

It has been revealed that green bean casserole and mashed potatoes: These are two of my Thanksgiving essentials, and I see no reason they shouldn’t share a fork. The creamy green beans and buttery potatoes are lovely together, but it’s the crispy fried onions that really make the combination work. That salty crunch is a welcome addition to the softer textures.

Turkey, stuffing and cranberry sauce: This is probably my favorite combo of the bunch. The savory turkey and seasoned stuffing are practically made for one another, while a little cranberry sauce cuts through the richness. It’s essentially a Thanksgiving leftover sandwich without the bread, although I wouldn’t object to adding a dinner roll to the equation.

According to recent reports, macaroni and cheese and cranberry sauce: I realize this combination may call my culinary credentials into question, but hear me out. Rich, creamy mac and cheese practically begs for something sharp and acidic to cut through it, and cranberry sauce does exactly that. It’s not so different from serving a sharp cheddar with fruit preserves on a charcuterie board, although I concede that putting cranberry sauce on macaroni and cheese is a considerably harder sell. But that’s half the fun of Thanksgiving dinner: discovering which combinations you’re willing to defend.

Senate Republicans lament midterms, weigh leadership election delay

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (570 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, senate Majority Leader John Thune arrives for a GOP conference meeting at the Capitol on Tuesday.
  • Senate Republicans on Tuesday were weighing whether to postpone their leadership elections after what several senators described as a “frank” conversation about their midterm losses last week.
  • But so far, no official candidate has emerged to challenge John Thune, R-S.D., for the post of minority leader in the upcoming Congress.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, senate Majority Leader John Thune arrives for a GOP conference meeting at the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Republicans on Tuesday were weighing whether to postpone their leadership elections after what several senators described as a “frank” conversation about their midterm losses last week.

But so far, no official candidate has emerged to challenge John Thune, R-S.D., for the post of minority leader in the upcoming Congress.

Recent findings suggest that the conference was supposed to begin its leadership elections Tuesday morning, but pushed those back to hear from members still reeling from the midterm results, which saw the GOP lose their Senate majority. As the conference meeting turned into what some dubbed an “open-mic session,” they took a break to attend previously scheduled committee hearings, with a blueprint to return at 2 p.m. Next they must decide whether to forge ahead and pick leaders Tuesday or to punt those choices to a different day.

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., noted the conversation taking place was “honest” and “frank.”.

In a recent development, “I will vote for the delay,” he noted. “We’ve got a lot of things that we’ve got to think through, and I think to rush into this and to just ratify all the same leadership — I mean, what message does that send?”.

“If you don’t think after losing seven seats minimum that we need to change course, I don’t know what planet you’re on,” he noted, adding he was frustrated that his party didn’t do more to focus on topics like affordability ahead of the midterms. “I know it’s easy to blame other people, but we need to look at what has happened here.”.

Sources indicate that sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., who is leading the charge to delay the leadership elections and collected signatures to call the conference meeting beforehand, called it “a very high-quality conversation” in which he was “leading.”.

“People are voicing opinions on all sides of the issues. It’s one of those times in the Republican conference where you kind of go, ‘We’ve got some smart people, and we’re having a very good, respectful conversation.’”.

No challenger to Thune, the current majority leader, stepped forward during the closed-door meeting, several senators stated. Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., said “they’re not even criticizing Thune” inside the room. “It hasn’t been about John Thune.”.

“It’s been about the family,” Cramer noted, describing it as a “family discussion.” Thune and others in leadership had yet to speak, as the candidate forum hadn’t started yet.

Industry observers note that sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., noted voters reacted to high gas prices, the war in Iran and the cost of living.

“The cost of living defeated us,” Paul said. “I don’t think anybody in Texas who voted for the Democrat governor was voting against John Thune. If you diagnose that as a problem, you’re misdiagnosing the problem.”.

According to recent reports, hawley didn’t say how long he’d like to see a delay. “Long enough for people to think through this, and if there’s somebody else … or several somebodies who want to run for positions, let them think through it.”.

Cramer was asked if senators in the room were placing any blame on President Donald Trump over how he handled midterm messaging.

“There was a lot of discussion about the president,” Cramer said.

John M. Donnelly contributed to the report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Boasting a brief ingredient list and a short cooking time, this easy chicken dish is one you’ll be making all season. Basic butter becomes the star here—it turns brown and nutty, then gets infused with sage and garlic for a savory sauce that’s basted over simply seasoned chicken breasts. A substantial squeeze of lemon, plus its zest, helps balance the richness. This skillet dinner is perfect for a speedy weeknight meal, but it’s also special enough for company.

The protein:You don’t have to limit yourself to chicken here. Feel free to replace the breasts with pork chops, shrimp, scallops, or skinless salmon or halibut fillets. Simply adjust the cooking time to properly cook the protein, but be sure to maintain a medium heat. While meat and fish are often cooked on medium-high heat for a nice char, it needs to be a bit lower to avoid bitter residue in the pan, since the butter will be browned immediately afterward.

Recent findings suggest that the crunch:The sage leaves crisp while the butter browns, but there are also ways to add more texture. Stirring in a handful of slivered almonds toward the end of cooking adds to the nuttiness of the dish; pine nuts, pistachios, or roughly chopped walnuts would also work. If you have a container of them, feel free to sprinkle some fried onions on top tableside.

According to recent reports, storage and serving ideas:This is not a make-ahead situation; it should be eaten immediately after it’s cooked. Serve with a simple salad dressed in a light vinaigrette to balance the richness. To soak up the sauce, mashed potatoes—traditional or sweet—are ideal. Or, to add another nutty element, roast some Brussels sprouts, cauliflower, or butternut squash to eat alongside and round out the meal.

Stainless steel and ceramic nonstick make a pretty dynamic duo in baking. Stainless steel delivers durability and provides a sturdy baking surface, while nonstick helps prevent baked goods from sticking to the pan.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that in a blender, combine 9 pickled Fresnos, stems removed and roughly chopped, plus 2 Tbsp.
  • In a recent development, preheat the oven to 425°F and set racks in the center and top of the oven.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you think cabbage is boring, this dish will absolutely change your mind. Charred aggressively, it takes on a smoky, almost meaty quality—it’s the main event. A drizzle of hot sauce, crispy breadcrumbs, and a cooling yogurt sauce round it out. Treat cabbage like a protein, and it will reward you.

More showstopping cabbage recipes here.

It has been revealed that in a blender, combine 9 pickled Fresnos, stems removed and roughly chopped, plus 2 Tbsp. brine, 1 small shallot, roughly chopped, 3 garlic cloves, 3 Tbsp. red wine vinegar, juice of 1 navel orange, and 1 tsp. kosher salt. Blend on high, taking a pause to scrape the sides, until smooth. With the blender running on low, slowly pour in 1 cup extra-virgin olive oil until the sauce is silky and runny. Transfer the sauce to a bottle or jar and refrigerate for up to 2 weeks.

In a recent development, preheat the oven to 425°F and set racks in the center and top of the oven. Line a sheet tray with parchment paper.

Make the Cabbage: Cut 1 large head green cabbage in half, then slice each half into four wedges. Arrange on the prepared sheet tray, drizzle generously with extra-virgin olive oil and kosher salt, and massage it into all those craggy layers. Roast on the center rack for 20–25 minutes, until a knife slides through easily. Set the broiler to high and slide the cabbage to the top rack. Broil for 2–4 minutes, until the edges are deeply charred and irresistibly crispy.

Industry observers note that while the Cabbage Roasts, Make the Breadcrumbs: In a small skillet over medium heat, melt 1 Tbsp. unsalted butter with 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil. Stir in ½ cup panko breadcrumbs, 1 garlic clove, finely grated, and ½ tsp. kosher salt, then toast, stirring constantly, until golden and fragrant. Remove from the heat and mix in ¼ preserved lemon, store-bought or homemade, peel only, finely diced, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh dill, and 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh parsley. Set aside to cool.

It has been revealed that make the Yogurt: In a small bowl, whisk together 1 cup full-fat Greek yogurt or labne, zest and juice ½ lemon, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh dill, 1 Tbsp. chopped fresh parsley, and 1 tsp. kosher salt until smooth and creamy.

When the cabbage is ready, swoop the yogurt across a serving plate. Arrange the cabbage wedges at dramatic angles. Drizzle generously with hot sauce, letting it seep into the leaves. Finish with the golden breadcrumbs, fresh dill fronds, and a few extra grates of lemon zest. Serve immediately.

The leaders of an effort to overhaul how the House deals with sexual misconduct hope their proposal will see action before the end of the 119th Congress, though they’re split on the odds.

In a recent development, rep. Kat Cammack, R-Fla., chair of the Republican Women’s Caucus, said legislative text is done and is being looked at by the relevant committees.

Recent findings suggest that “Yes, absolutely,” she remarked when asked if the package would get a vote this year. “We’re shopping it now with the different committees, House Admin and Ethics, and waiting on their final feedback, which we should have actually this week.”.

It has been revealed that rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, noted she was still optimistic about getting it done, but stopped short of putting full faith in Republican leadership to get it over the finish line. The effort has been underway since May, when Cammack and Leger Fernández’s caucuses declared a partnership to propose changes after two members of the House resigned amid allegations of sexual misconduct.

Asked if she thought Speaker Mike Johnson would put the proposal on the floor during the busy lame-duck session, Leger Fernández laughed.

“Hopefully, that’s something that will happen, because you know the Republican Women’s Caucus had stated they were optimistic before we left. I’m still optimistic,” she said.

The two groups have spent months holding dozens of meetings with staff, their own caucuses and male members of Congress, among others. Suggestions have included banning members of Congress from engaging in sexual relationships with any House staffer, not just those who work for them directly, and outlining penalties for violaters. Initially, the groups were expected to unveil their work by August recess, but that got pushed back as the House canceled weeks in session and as they cited a desire to get it right.

Cammack remarked she thinks Johnson “has been very sincere in his efforts on this.”.

“That would be a tremendous disappointment” if he didn’t put it on the floor, she noted when asked about the possibility. “I genuinely believe he cares about this issue.”.

According to recent reports, leger Fernández said if it doesn’t get done by the end of the 119th Congress, she hopes some changes would be adopted under the rules package for the next Congress that Democrats bring forward in January. Such packages are typically adopted with party-line votes and give incoming majorities the chance to tweak how the House operates to their liking. While certain narrower proposals aimed at curbing sexual harassment could be written into House rules, others would need to pass both chambers and be enacted into law to take effect.

Recent findings suggest that “We are going to move to make sure it is in the rules package, because we will be in charge next year,” Leger Fernández remarked. “But I would love for it to pass now, because that was a commitment that it be bipartisan.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recipe by Susan Bronson, Rhinelander, Wisconsin.

Tested by Taste of Home Test Kitchen.

Taste of Home's Editorial Process.

Dirty rice has met its noodle match with our Louisiana-style dirty spaghetti.

Industry observers note that let the good times roll with this Louisiana-inspired dirty spaghetti dish! It’s a riff on Cajun-Creole dirty rice that transforms the original into an easy one-pot pasta.

The key it its flavor is Cajun seasoning, a blend cayenne pepper, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika and thyme. And herein lies an important cooking tip: When using store-bought seasoning blends like this one, give them a little taste first before adding anything to the pot. Different brands rely on different ratios of ingredients, and a tablespoon of one product could be much milder (or pack way more heat!) than a tablespoon of another. Your personal preferences matter, too. So whether you are sensitive to spice or like to pack on the heat, make sure you’re adding the proper amount of spice for your taste.

Recent findings suggest that dirty spaghetti is a riff on dirty rice, a classic Cajun-Creole side dish. Traditional dirty rice is made with chopped organ meats such as chicken livers or gizzards, which, along with the herbs and seasonings, color the white rice and earn it its “dirty” moniker. This dish, however, has a meaty base that’s made with ground beef and diced andouille sausage. Like the original, it also features the “holy trinity” of Cajun and Creole cooking: chopped onion, bell pepper and celery. A healthy dose of Cajun seasoning ensures each bite is packed with bold flavor.

Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or large high-sided skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook it until it’s browned, four to six minutes, using a wooden spoon or spatula to break it into small crumbles.

Editor’s Tip: If you use a skillet, make sure it has a lid.

Add the chopped andouille sausage, onion, celery, red pepper and green pepper. Cook them until the vegetables are soft, about three to four minutes. Add the garlic and cook it until it’s fragrant, 30 to 60 seconds. Stir in the tomato paste and Cajun seasoning, and cook for one to two more minutes. Add 3 cups of broth and bring the mixture to a simmer.

Add the broken spaghetti to the pot, ensuring that the noodles are submerged in the liquid and separated as much as possible. Add more liquid if needed. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Cover the pot and simmer the pasta for six minutes.

It has been revealed that remove the lid and continue simmering until the spaghetti is al dente, stirring every two to three minutes. Add more broth as needed. Remove the pot from the heat, and season the pasta to taste with salt and pepper.

Leftover dirty spaghetti can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to four days.

In a recent development, the best way to reheat a pasta dish like this one is either in the oven or on the stovetop. To reheat leftover dirty spaghetti in the oven, transfer it to an oven-safe baking dish, cover it tightly with foil, and cook it in an oven preheated to 350 degrees for about 20 minutes or until it’s heated through. To reheat it on the stovetop, heat a saucepan over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Add the leftover pasta and sauce and saute them for about two to three minutes or until they’re hot.

According to recent reports, yes, you can freeze dirty spaghetti. After allowing it to cool completely, transfer leftovers to a freezer-safe container and store them in the freezer for up to three months. Allow the dirty spaghetti to thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating it.

The best pan for making this one-pot pasta dish is a Dutch oven or a large, high-walled skillet or pot with a tight-fitting lid.

In a recent development, first, be sure to give your Cajun seasoning a little taste first because seasoning blends like this one can vary widely in spiciness. Depending on how spicy your Cajun seasoning is, add more or less to taste. You could also make a homemade Cajun seasoning blend and customize the amount of cayenne pepper and chili powder to your personal taste. The andouille sausage also adds quite a bit of spice; for less heat, skip it entirely, or swap in sweet Italian sausage, breakfast sausage, chicken sausage or a milder smoked sausage like kielbasa.

Industry observers note that you’ll definitely want to pair this dirty spaghetti with crusty French bread, garlic bread or cornbread to sop up any extra sauce. Southern-inspired side dishes to consider include southern green beans, collard greens or black-eyed pea tomato salad. Or, complement the pasta dish’s spicy flavor with a fresh and crisp green salad.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sides are the true stars of Thanksgiving dinner. With so many delicious options to choose from, it's nearly impossible to pick just a few favorites. Between the creamy casseroles and savory stuffing, I have no idea where to start, or how I’m going to make room for everything. To ensure your feast is as great as it can be, check out our top 31 best Thanksgiving sides—you might just find a upcoming family favorite among them.

First things first: If you’re going for the most quintessential Thanksgiving, you’ve got to have the classics. We’re talking stuffing, sweet potato casserole, gravy, green bean casserole, mashed potatoes, cranberry sauce… If you wanted to, you could make all those, stop right there, and have pretty much the perfect meal. If you’ve made those a million times already and want to branch out, but are worried your friends and family might mutiny, we suggest starting small. Try out a latest variation on the tried and true recipes, like our loaded green bean casserole with added bacon, or our melting potatoes, and more.

In a recent development, want even more Thanksgiving ideas? Check out our favorite Thanksgiving salads, soups, cocktails, and desserts.

If you grew up loving the classic tater tot casserole, this tater tot stuffing is begging for a place on your holiday table. Tater tot “croutons” are tossed with sausage crumbles and herby onions and celery for a fresh twist on standard Thanksgiving stuffing that’s simultaneously nostalgic and brand new.

When it comes to versatile sides, it’s difficult to beat classic roasted potatoes. They complete practically any main they’re served alongside! In this recipe, the humble potato is transformed into perfectly crispy, herby bites that put any frozen bag to shame.

If you’re not into creamy, melty macaroni and cheese with an insanely satisfying cheese-pull, then you might want to find another mac recipe. Sorry, but this slow-cooker macaroni and cheese is just too darn dreamy.

Would Grandma really be all that upset if you tried a newly introduced stuffing this holiday? Her cornbread stuffing is undoubtedly delicious and nostalgic, but what if we switched it up a bit this year and tried something new? Enter: flaky, savory-sweet croissant stuffing.

That green bean casserole on your holiday menu is begging for an upgrade, so we're adding just one ingredient (!) to turn your favorite side into gnocchi green bean casserole. Blanched fresh green beans and buttery sliced mushrooms, onions, and garlic get tossed with a creamy béchamel sauce and pillowy gnocchi, then baked until bubbly. Seriously. That’s it.

This recipe is for everyone who hates marshmallows atop their sweet potato casserole—in their place is a buttery, brown sugar pecan topping that is still perfectly sweet and Thanksgiving-worthy.

If you thought kale Caesar was over, you’ve clearly never topped it with crispy frico squash croutons. Featuring butternut squash and crispy baked Parmesan frico, this autumn spin on the classic Caesar salad will have you wishing it was fall all year round.

When it comes to the significant Thanksgiving feast, we consider the roast turkey and the sweet potato casserole as sides to the STUFFING. A good stuffing makes or breaks Thanksgiving dinner, so follow our tips to make it the best you can.

It has been revealed that this sweet-tart sauce is almost as easy as opening up the canned stuff, and you know your Thanksgiving spread deserves better. This is one of the Thanksgiving dishes you can make up to a week in advance. (Bonus: The flavors will meld and deepen while it hangs out in the fridge.).

According to recent reports, packed with sweet corn, balanced by a pinch of paprika and herby chives, this fall casserole has an insanely tender and custardy texture that will have you on your third helping before you even know what hit you. Let this classic side be the star of your Thanksgiving dinner if you’re ever in the mood for endless praise and compliments.

Industry observers note that whether you’re drizzling it over your roast turkey, mashed potatoes, or flaky biscuits, homemade gravy is an absolute must-have during the holidays. Since it’s such a staple, it's gotta be perfect—THIS is the recipe you need.

There is nothing better than a soft, homemade dinner roll. These rolls use sweet potatoes to make them even softer and fluffier, similar to our classic potato rolls. You can use sweet potato puree from a can, or if you have leftover baked sweet potato, you can use that as well.

Unlike potatoes au gratin, which typically contain cheese, traditional scalloped potatoes are very simple: just thinly sliced potatoes cooked in a mixture of milk and heavy cream that’s infused with aromatics, such as shallots, garlic, and herbs. Our only add-on? A bit of finely shredded Parmesan.

What do you get when you take mac & cheese on a shopping spree to the fanciest cheese shop you know and shower it with gold leaf? Million-dollar mac. Showcasing a trifecta of bougie (and delicious) cheeses and a crispy crunchy panko topping, this irresistible comfort food in a casserole will take center stage on any table it hits.

Onion Soup Mix Roasted Potatoes.

We can all agree that roasting potatoes is the best way to cook 'em up, right? And if roasting potatoes in the oven wasn’t simple enough, we’ve made seasoning even simpler by using a flavor-packed packet of onion soup mix. Potatoes don’t get any better or easier than this.

Sources indicate that fondue mashed potatoes, or more classically known as pommes aligot, are super-creamy, silky mashed potatoes that have a starchy, cheesy pull like you’ve never seen before. The buttery potato mixed with fresh garlic, white wine, and mild Gruyère is really an experience you're going to love.

Recent findings suggest that wave goodbye to that can of cream of mushroom soup and meet your upcoming favorite green bean casserole! It's got bacon, chives, and SO much cheese. If you've got vegetarian company, feel free to leave the bacon out—it's got plenty of cheese to make up for it.

If you love stovetop mac 'n' cheese on your Thanksgiving table, you’ve got to try this creamy butternut squash orzo. Butternut squash and Parmesan join forces with orzo to create a cheesy pasta skillet that hits every nostalgic note.

Also known as cornbread dressing, this dish is a classic in the South, where you’ll often find it mixed with sausage, bacon, jalapeños, nuts, and even chopped oysters. We kept ours simple with flavors you’d find in classic stuffing, but don't let us stop you from jazzing up yours.

In a recent development, to make this side dish, we treat orzo like risotto, then top it with crunchy herbed breadcrumbs for added texture. The orzo soaks up the cheese sauce, and you get an incredible sauce-to-pasta ratio with multitudes of creaminess in every bite.
